sentences.zh: 齋清阿童添雲彭三元蕭捷三周清元蔡應龍

translations.idiomatic: Zhai Qing'a, Tong Tianyun, Peng Sanyuan, Xiao Jiesan, Zhou Qingyuan, and Cai Yinglong

translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhongde, Liu Yulin and others, Huang Jinyou, Lin Rui, Cai Dongxiang, and Zou Shangyuan

translations.literal: Hao Shangxiang, Zhang Yuxiang, his elder brother Zhang Yuqing, Cao Renmei, Mao Kekuan, Xing Lianke
translations.idiomatic: Hao Shangxiang, Zhang Yuxiang, his elder brother Zhang Yuqing, Cao Renmei, Mao Kekuan, and Xing Lianke

translations.literal: Tian Xingqi, Tian Xingsheng, Ma Dingguo
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xingqi, Tian Xingsheng, and Ma Dingguo

sentences.zh: 齋清阿，字竹塍，納喇氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Zhai Qing'a, styled Zhucheng, of the Nara clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Qing'a, whose style was Zhucheng, belonged to the Nara clan and was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 早喪父，母氏撫之。

translations.literal: His father died early; his mother raised him.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at an early age and was brought up by his mother.

sentences.zh: 家貧，月夕至撤去鐙火。

translations.literal: The family was poor; on moonlit nights they would even remove the lamp fire.
translations.idiomatic: The household was so poor that on bright moonlit nights they would even put out their lamps.

sentences.zh: 膂力過人，取巨磚置平地，拳擊之，立碎。

translations.literal: His physical strength surpassed others'; he would take a huge brick, place it on level ground, strike it with his fist, and it would shatter at once.
translations.idiomatic: His strength was extraordinary: he could set a large brick on the ground, strike it with his fist, and shatter it instantly.

sentences.zh: 以善​​射得名，嘗隨扈盛京，命射，中靶，賜克食。

translations.literal: He became famous for skill in archery; once while accompanying the imperial procession to Shengjing, he was ordered to shoot, hit the target, and was rewarded with kesi food.
translations.idiomatic: He won renown as a fine archer. Once, while escorting the court to Shengjing, he was told to shoot, hit the mark, and was rewarded with a portion of the imperial meal.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，發閩、浙，以都司用，補浙江杭州營都司，為總督孫爾準所賞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang he was dispatched to Fujian and Zhejiang and appointed to use as colonel; he was appointed colonel of the Hangzhou garrison in Zhejiang and was appreciated by Governor Sun Erzhun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Daoguang reign he was sent to Fujian and Zhejiang and appointed colonel of the Hangzhou garrison in Zhejiang, where Governor Sun Erzhun took notice of him.

sentences.zh: 英吉利船入犯，獻燒船退敵策，不用。

translations.literal: When English ships invaded, he submitted a plan to burn ships and drive off the enemy, but it was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When British vessels attacked, he proposed burning enemy ships to repel them, but the plan was rejected.

sentences.zh: 遞擢至廣東肇慶協副將。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to deputy brigade-general of the Zhaoqing command in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in steady promotion until he became deputy brigade-general of the Zhaoqing command in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 三十年，廣西金田亂起，檄令率兵至兩粵交界開建縣堵禦。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when the Jintian rebellion broke out in Guangxi, he was ordered by dispatch to lead troops to Kaijian County on the border of the two Guang provinces to block the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of the reign, after the uprising at Jintian in Guangxi, he was ordered to lead troops to Kaijian County on the Guangdong–Guangxi border to hold the rebels in check.

sentences.zh: 匪二千餘，船四十餘，從縣北金莊偷越，督兵進擊，斬其酋二人，餘敗竄，自是不敢犯境。

translations.literal: More than two thousand bandits in over forty boats stole across from Jinzhuang north of the county; he directed the troops in an advance attack, beheaded two of their chieftains, and the rest were defeated and fled; thereafter they no longer dared violate the border.
translations.idiomatic: When more than two thousand rebels in some forty boats slipped across from Jinzhuang north of the county, he led his men in a counterattack, beheaded two of their leaders, and routed the rest. After that they did not dare cross the border again.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，廣寧屬江谷屯積匪滋擾，廣東兵會剿，竄廣西懷集一帶，至賀縣屯聚。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, bandits accumulated and harassed Jianggu Tun in Guangning; Guangdong troops joined in suppression, and the rebels fled to the Huaiji region in Guangxi and gathered at Hexian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng, rebel bands that had gathered at Jianggu Tun in Guangning grew increasingly troublesome. Guangdong forces joined in the campaign, but the rebels slipped into the Huaiji area of Guangxi and massed at Hexian.

sentences.zh: 廣西大吏以廣東各官惟知驅賊了事，移文廣東詰之。

translations.literal: The high officials of Guangxi, holding that Guangdong officials only knew how to drive bandits away to settle matters, sent documents to Guangdong reproaching them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi's senior officials complained that their Guangdong counterparts merely drove rebels across the border to be rid of them, and sent formal dispatches to Guangdong demanding an explanation.

sentences.zh: 總督徐廣縉檄肇慶府知府蔡振武、參將左炘赴廣西勦賊，道出開建。

translations.literal: Governor Xu Guangjin dispatched Zhaoqing prefect Cai Zhenwu and Colonel Zuo Xin to Guangxi to suppress bandits; their route passed through Kaijian.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Xu Guangjin ordered Zhaoqing prefect Cai Zhenwu and Colonel Zuo Xin to Guangxi to suppress the rebels, and their march took them through Kaijian.

sentences.zh: 齋清阿以越境追賊，須重兵制其死命，原統駐劄開建之師同赴廣西。

translations.literal: Zhai Qing'a held that to pursue bandits across the border required a large force to curb them fatally, and requested that the troops originally stationed at Kaijian under his command go together to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Qing'a argued that pursuing rebels across the border would require a substantial force to crush them decisively, and asked that the troops he had commanded at Kaijian march with him into Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 守備薩國亮以無越境勦賊之責諫，齋清阿奮然曰：「賊勢蔓延，若畫分畛域，何以紓民困而報國恩？

translations.literal: Garrison commander Sa Guoliang remonstrated that there was no duty to suppress bandits beyond the border; Zhai Qing'a said resolutely: "The bandit force is spreading; if we draw boundaries, how can we relieve the people's hardship and repay the state's grace?"
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Sa Guoliang urged that they had no mandate to fight rebels outside the province, but Zhai Qing'a declared with fervor: "The rebels are spreading everywhere. If we draw lines on a map, how can we ease the people's suffering or repay the emperor's favor?"

sentences.zh: 吾雖逾七旬，精力未衰，正臣子戮力時也！

translations.literal: "Although I am past seventy, my energy has not declined — this is precisely the time for subjects to exert themselves to the utmost!"
translations.idiomatic: "I am past seventy, yet my strength has not failed me. This is exactly when a loyal subject should give his all!"

sentences.zh: 」遂與振武等督兵入廣西境。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced into Guangxi territory together with Zhenwu and the others directing troops.
translations.idiomatic: With that he led his troops into Guangxi alongside Zhenwu and the others.

sentences.zh: 至賀縣鋪門圩，復進至蜑家坪，距賊巢里許，賊突出數百人撲營，官軍迎擊之，斃賊數十人。

translations.literal: When they reached Pumen market in Hexian and advanced further to Danjiaping, about a li from the bandit nest, several hundred bandits suddenly burst out and charged the camp; the government troops met them in battle and killed several tens of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Pumen market in Hexian and pushed on to Danjiaping, scarcely a li from the rebel stronghold. Several hundred rebels suddenly rushed the camp; government forces met them head-on and killed several dozen.

sentences.zh: 賊退回松圩，在圩內施放大砲，官軍避入田中，火藥槍繩盡濕，賊復分隊挑戰，抄官兵後，爇火燒山，齋清阿督兵以槍擊斃賊七十餘人。

translations.literal: The bandits retreated to Song market and fired great guns from within the market; the government troops avoided into the fields, gunpowder and gun cords all soaked through; the bandits again divided forces to challenge, cutting behind the government troops and setting fires to burn the hills; Zhai Qing'a directed the troops and with gunfire killed more than seventy bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to Song market and shelled them from within the town. Government troops took cover in the fields, but their powder and match cords were soaked through. The rebels split into detachments to press the attack, worked around behind the government lines, and set the hills ablaze. Zhai Qing'a directed rifle fire that killed more than seventy rebels.

sentences.zh: 值日暮，孤軍無援，深入被困。

translations.literal: As evening fell, the isolated army had no reinforcements and was trapped deep within.
translations.idiomatic: Night fell on an isolated force with no relief, cut off deep in enemy country.

sentences.zh: 事急，掣佩刀連刃數賊，肩中火箭，猶拔箭作戰，手刃執旗賊目一人，刀折，歿於陣，手握斷刀牢不可開，怒目上視，懍然如生，時咸豐元年四月也。

translations.literal: When matters grew critical, he drew his waist knife and in succession cut down several bandits; struck in the shoulder by a fire-arrow, he still pulled out the arrow and fought on, personally killing one bandit chieftain bearing a flag; when his blade broke he fell in battle; he gripped the broken blade so tightly it could not be opened, glaring upward in anger, imposing as if alive — this was in the fourth month of the first year of Xianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the crisis he drew his side sword and cut down several rebels in succession. Struck in the shoulder by a fire-arrow, he pulled it out and kept fighting, personally killing a rebel standard-bearer. When his blade snapped he fell on the field. His grip on the broken sword was so tight it could not be pried loose; he glared upward in fury, stern as though still alive. It was the fourth month of the first year of Xianfeng.

sentences.zh: 卹贈總兵，賞世職，予諡威烈。

translations.literal: In condolence he was posthumously granted the rank of brigade-general, rewarded with hereditary office, and given the posthumous title Weilie.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him posthumous promotion to brigade-general, an hereditary office, and the posthumous title Weilie.

sentences.zh: 童添雲，字鎮銘，湖南平江人。

translations.literal: Tong Tianyun, styled Zhenming, was a native of Pingjiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Tianyun, whose style was Zhenming, came from Pingjiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以貧，偕弟必發走長沙為戰兵。

translations.literal: Because of poverty, he went with his younger brother Bifa to Changsha to serve as a campaigning soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Poor as they were, he and his younger brother Bifa went to Changsha to enlist as campaigning soldiers.

sentences.zh: 饒膂力，能開五石弓，射必命中。

translations.literal: He had powerful arms and could draw a five-stone bow; whenever he shot he invariably hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: He was powerfully built, could draw a five-stone bow, and never missed his mark.

sentences.zh: 道光二十二年，從提督楊芳出師廣東，一日，夷撲城，有營在城外，芳欲調入，火攻甚熾。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Daoguang he followed Regional Commander Yang Fang's expedition to Guangdong; one day when the foreigners assaulted the city, there was a camp outside the walls; Yang Fang wished to bring them in, but the fire attack was extremely fierce.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Daoguang he marched to Guangdong under Regional Commander Yang Fang. One day the foreigners stormed the city. A camp lay outside the walls, and Yang Fang wanted to pull the men in, but the enemy's fire assault was overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 募敢死者持令縋城出，添雲應募，少選，兵皆入城，芳奇之。

translations.literal: He recruited daring men to hold orders and be lowered by rope out of the city; Tianyun volunteered; after a short while the troops had all entered the city, and Yang Fang found him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fang recruited volunteers to carry orders and be lowered by rope from the wall. Tianyun stepped forward. Before long every man was back inside the city, and Yang Fang marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，粵賊圍長沙，與必發從守城，圍解，添雲語人曰：「吾觀諸將中能稱將才者，惟塔都司與彭千總耳。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, Cantonese bandits besieged Changsha; he and Bifa followed in defending the city; when the siege was lifted, Tianyun said to people: "Among the various generals, the only ones who can be called commanding talent are Battalion Commander Ta and Battalion Commander Peng."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng, Cantonese rebels besieged Changsha. He and Bifa helped defend the city. When the siege was raised, Tianyun told others: "Of all the officers I have seen, only Battalion Commander Ta and Battalion Commander Peng truly deserve to be called generals."

sentences.zh: 」塔即塔齊布，彭即三元也。

translations.literal: "Ta was Ta Qibu, and Peng was Sanyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Ta was Ta Qibu, and Peng was Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 會塔齊布練標兵，添雲隸麾下，三元時別將一營，深相結納。

translations.literal: When Ta Qibu drilled the banner troops, Tianyun served under him; at that time Sanyuan separately commanded a battalion, and they formed a deep bond.
translations.idiomatic: When Ta Qibu began drilling the Green Standard troops, Tianyun served under him. Sanyuan then commanded a separate battalion, and the two men became close allies.

sentences.zh: 茶陵土寇起，塔齊布命解火藥，期三日，添雲逾宿至，吒曰：「何速也？

translations.literal: When native bandits rose at Chaling, Ta Qibu ordered gunpowder delivered within three days; Tianyun arrived in more than overnight; Ta exclaimed: "Why so fast?"
translations.idiomatic: When local bandits rose at Chaling, Ta Qibu ordered gunpowder delivered within three days. Tianyun arrived in little more than a day. Ta cried out in astonishment: "How did you get here so quickly?"

sentences.zh: 」添雲曰：「遲恐有阻，則貽誤大矣。

translations.literal: Tianyun said: "Delay might cause obstruction, and that would be a great failure."
translations.idiomatic: Tianyun replied: "Any delay might cause an obstruction, and that would be a grave mistake."

sentences.zh: 四年三月，賊陷湘潭，塔齊布帥標兵等拒戰，添雲與必發從。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year, when bandits took Xiangtan, Ta Qibu led the banner troops and others to resist; Tianyun and Bifa followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year the rebels seized Xiangtan. Ta Qibu led the banner troops and others to resist, and Tianyun and Bifa went with him.

sentences.zh: 時賊踞城外民廛，塔齊布好輕騎觀賊，策馬入黃龍巷，必發先驅，巷狹而長，甫入，賊突出刺塔齊布，必發急以背承之，中肩，塔齊布跳而免，必發死之。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits occupied civilian houses outside the city; Ta Qibu was fond of riding lightly to observe the bandits and urged his horse into Huanglong Lane; Bifa went ahead as vanguard; the lane was narrow and long; just after entering, bandits suddenly burst out and stabbed at Ta Qibu; Bifa hurriedly received the blow with his back, struck in the shoulder; Ta Qibu leaped and escaped; Bifa died for him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the civilian quarters outside the walls. Ta Qibu liked to ride out lightly to scout the enemy and spurred his horse into Huanglong Lane with Bifa in the lead. The lane was narrow and long. They had barely entered when rebels rushed out to stab Ta Qibu. Bifa threw his back between them and took a wound in the shoulder. Ta Qibu leaped clear and escaped; Bifa died in his place.

sentences.zh: 越二日，師大捷。

translations.literal: Two days later the army won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later the army won a resounding victory.

sentences.zh: 湘潭平，擢守備，或賀之，添雲憤然曰：「賊戕吾弟，雖官至一品，弗原也！

translations.literal: When Xiangtan was pacified he was promoted to garrison commander; when some congratulated him, Tianyun said angrily: "The bandits killed my younger brother — even if I reached the rank of first grade, I would not forgive them!"
translations.idiomatic: After Xiangtan was recovered he was promoted to garrison commander. When someone congratulated him, Tianyun said in anger: "The rebels killed my brother. Even if I rose to the highest rank, I could never forgive them!"

sentences.zh: 原生啖賊肉耳，何賀為？

translations.literal: "In life I would gnaw the bandits' flesh — what is there to congratulate?"
translations.idiomatic: "In this life I would gnaw their flesh. What is there to celebrate?"

sentences.zh: 」遂由湘潭轉戰至岳州，從克岳州，擢都司。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Xiangtan he fought on to Yuezhou, followed in taking Yuezhou, and was promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiangtan he fought on to Yuezhou, took part in the recovery of the city, and was promoted to colonel.

sentences.zh: 克武昌，擢游擊。

translations.literal: When Wuchang was taken, he was promoted to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchang fell he was promoted to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 克興國、大冶、黃梅、廣濟，破田家鎮，擢參將。

translations.literal: He took Xingguo, Daye, Huangmei, and Guangji, broke through Tianjia Town, and was promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He helped capture Xingguo, Daye, Huangmei, and Guangji, broke through Tianjia Town, and was promoted to colonel.

sentences.zh: 添雲身長面赤，額以下痘瘢如錢。

translations.literal: Tianyun was tall with a red face; below his forehead smallpox scars like coins.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyun was tall, with a ruddy face and coin-sized pockmarks from his forehead downward.

sentences.zh: 橫矛陷陣，槍丸如雨，不少卻。

translations.literal: Charging the battle line with spear leveled, with bullets like rain he did not retreat in the least.
translations.idiomatic: He charged the enemy ranks with leveled spear and did not flinch though bullets fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 賊見其旗，輒相語曰：「童麻子至矣！

translations.literal: When bandits saw his banner they would say to one another: "Tong the pockmarked one has arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever rebels saw his banner they would say to one another: "Tong the pockmarked one is here!"

sentences.zh: 」則皆走。

translations.literal: Then they would all flee.
translations.idiomatic: Then they would all flee.

sentences.zh: 五年十二月，攻九江，城砲傷胸，舁歸營，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifth year, attacking Jiujiang, a city cannon wounded his chest; carried back to camp, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fifth year, while attacking Jiujiang, he was struck in the chest by a city gun. Carried back to camp, he died.

sentences.zh: 發其笥，衣數領而已，同營皆痛哭之。

translations.literal: When his chest was opened there were only a few garments; everyone in the camp wept bitterly for him.
translations.idiomatic: When his trunk was opened it held only a few garments. The whole camp wept for him.

sentences.zh: 詔贈副將，諡壯節，附祀塔齊布祠。

translations.literal: By imperial decree he was posthumously granted the rank of deputy brigade-general, given the posthumous title Zhuangjie, and granted ancillary worship in Ta Qibu's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously granted him the rank of deputy brigade-general, the title Zhuangjie, and a place in ancillary worship at Ta Qibu's shrine.

sentences.zh: 彭三元，字春浦，湖南善化人。

translations.literal: Peng Sanyuan, styled Chunpu, was a native of Shanhua in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Sanyuan, whose style was Chunpu, came from Shanhua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十五年武進士，用衛守備，借補千總。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang he passed the military jinshi examination and was appointed to use as garrison commander of the guard, and was lent appointment as battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang he took the military jinshi degree, was appointed to serve as garrison commander of the guard, and was lent to fill a battalion command.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，粵匪竄湖南道州，勾結會匪犯東安，三元偕署守備週祿兩次迎剿，殲賊多名。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, Cantonese bandits fled into Daozhou in Hunan, colluded with secret-society bandits to invade Dong'an, and Sanyuan together with acting garrison commander Zhou Lu twice met them in suppression and destroyed many bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng, Cantonese rebels slipped into Daozhou in Hunan and joined local secret-society bands in an attack on Dong'an. Sanyuan and acting garrison commander Zhou Lu met them twice in battle and killed many rebels.

sentences.zh: 三年，敘省城防堵功，用守備。

translations.literal: In the third year, in recognition of merit in defending and blocking at the provincial capital, he was appointed to use as garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year his service in the capital's defense was recorded, and he was appointed garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 侍郎曾國籓檄寶慶知府魁聯募寶勇千名，分屬三元五百人。

translations.literal: Vice President Zeng Guofan dispatched Baoxing prefect Kui Lian to recruit a thousand Bao Braves, of whom five hundred were placed under Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Vice President Zeng Guofan ordered Baoxing prefect Kui Lian to raise a thousand Bao Braves, and five hundred were assigned to Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 旋平江西泰和土匪於茶陵、安仁。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he pacified native bandits of Taihe in Jiangxi at Chaling and Anren.
translations.idiomatic: He soon suppressed the Taihe bandits of Jiangxi in operations at Chaling and Anren.

sentences.zh: 四年，隨副將塔齊布勦賊湘潭，復其城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed Deputy Brigadier Ta Qibu in suppressing bandits at Xiangtan and recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed Deputy Brigadier Ta Qibu in the campaign at Xiangtan and helped recover the city.

sentences.zh: 六月，進攻岳州，是時湘潭潰賊由靖港竄岳州，增壘設卡，為久抗計。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he advanced to attack Yuezhou; at that time defeated bandits from Xiangtan fled through Jinggang to Yuezhou, added fortifications and set up checkpoints, planning prolonged resistance.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the army advanced on Yuezhou. Defeated rebels from Xiangtan had fled through Jinggang into Yuezhou, thrown up new works, and set up checkpoints, intending to hold out indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 巡撫駱秉章暨國籓會督戰船，塔齊布亦統陸路官軍，約期並進。

translations.literal: Governor Luo Bingzhang together with Guofan jointly directed the war vessels; Ta Qibu also commanded the land-route government troops; they set a date to advance together.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Luo Bingzhang and Guofan coordinated the fleet, while Ta Qibu commanded the land forces. They fixed a date for a joint advance.

sentences.zh: 先以疑兵誘賊，賊擁至，觸伏盡殪，擊沉賊船百餘只，遂復岳州。

translations.literal: First they used decoy troops to lure the bandits; the bandits surged forward, triggered ambushes and were entirely destroyed, and over a hundred bandit boats were sunk; thereupon Yuezhou was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Decoy troops first lured the rebels forward. When they rushed in they walked into ambushes and were wiped out. More than a hundred rebel boats were sunk, and Yuezhou was recovered.

sentences.zh: 七月，賊水陸大至，官軍迎擊，悉焚其船，其由陸路來犯者，三元沿岸截擊，殲賊目一、餘匪百餘，生擒四十餘名。

translations.literal: In the seventh month bandits arrived in force by land and water; the government troops met them in battle, burned all their boats, and those who came by land route — Sanyuan intercepted along the shore, destroyed one bandit chieftain and more than a hundred remaining bandits, and captured alive more than forty.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the rebels came in force by land and water. Government troops met them, burned their fleet, and Sanyuan cut off the land columns along the riverbank, killing one rebel leader and more than a hundred others and taking more than forty prisoners.

sentences.zh: 嗣賊由高橋撲鳳凰山大營，塔齊布督率將弁進剿，三元出奇抄截，分路迎擊，斃賊六百餘名。

translations.literal: Thereafter bandits from Gaoqiao rushed the great camp at Fenghuang Mountain; Ta Qibu directed officers in suppression; Sanyuan made a surprise outflanking interception, met them on divided routes, and killed more than six hundred bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels from Gaoqiao struck the main camp at Fenghuang Mountain, Ta Qibu led his officers against them while Sanyuan made a flanking move by surprise. Fighting on several fronts they killed more than six hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 八月，匪於崇陽交界設卡抗拒，九月，三元偕候選知府羅澤南分路進攻，抵其壘，痛殲之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month bandits set up checkpoints at the border of Chongyang to resist; in the ninth month Sanyuan together with candidate prefect Luo Zinan advanced on divided routes, reached their fortifications, and destroyed them severely.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month rebels set up blocking posts on the Chongyang border. In the ninth month Sanyuan and candidate prefect Luo Zinan attacked on separate routes, reached their stockades, and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 尋隨塔齊布由嘉魚轉戰而前，所向披靡，直抵武漢。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he followed Ta Qibu from Jiayu fighting forward; wherever they went they swept all before them, reaching straight to Wuhan.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Ta Qibu from Jiayu, fighting his way forward until nothing could stand before them and they reached Wuhan.

sentences.zh: 塔齊布分軍三路：一攻武昌，一攻漢陽，一由水路進剿。

translations.literal: Ta Qibu divided the army into three routes: one to attack Wuchang, one to attack Hanyang, and one to advance by water route in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Ta Qibu divided his forces three ways: one column for Wuchang, one for Hanyang, and one to advance by river.

sentences.zh: 時風勢順利，官軍縱火，焚賊船數十隻，乘勢奮擊，斃賊無數。

translations.literal: At that time the wind was favorable; the government troops set fires, burned several tens of bandit boats, and taking advantage of the momentum pressed the attack fiercely, killing countless bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The wind favored them. Government forces set fires that burned dozens of rebel boats, then pressed the attack and killed rebels beyond count.

sentences.zh: 漢陽賊大懼，棄城遁，武昌賊亦遁，遂復之。

translations.literal: The bandits in Hanyang were greatly afraid, abandoned the city and fled; the bandits in Wuchang also fled, and the cities were thereby recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in Hanyang panicked, abandoned the city, and fled. Those in Wuchang fled as well, and both cities were recovered.

sentences.zh: 三元並截於洪山要隘，斬馘甚多。

translations.literal: Sanyuan also intercepted at the strategic pass of Hong Mountain and beheaded many.
translations.idiomatic: Sanyuan also blocked the vital pass at Hong Mountain and took many heads.

sentences.zh: 十月，偕澤南進屯馬嶺坳，直偪半壁山。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he advanced together with Zinan to encamp at Maling'ao, pressing straight on Banbishan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he joined Zinan in advancing to camp at Maling'ao, pressing directly on Banbishan.

sentences.zh: 賊悉眾至，官軍徑搗賊壘，賊狂竄，三元等分途截殺，斬偽丞相林紹璋及偽將軍指揮等。

translations.literal: The bandits brought all their forces; the government troops drove straight at the bandit fortifications; the bandits fled wildly; Sanyuan and others intercepted and killed on divided routes, beheading the false chancellor Lin Shaozhang and false generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels massed their full strength. Government troops struck straight at their works, and the rebels broke and ran. Sanyuan and the others cut them down on several roads, killing the false chancellor Lin Shaozhang and several false generals and commanders.

sentences.zh: 越數日，賊復由田家鎮渡江來犯，塔齊布擊卻之，列隊江乾。

translations.literal: Several days later the bandits again crossed the river from Tianjia Town to attack; Ta Qibu repelled them and drew up ranks along the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Days later rebels crossed the river again from Tianjia Town. Ta Qibu drove them back and formed his ranks along the bank.

sentences.zh: 賊偵官軍盡赴下游，徑從上游登岸，將掩襲澤南老營，三元馳至，率眾奮擊，追至牛礶磯，毀其船，斃賊百餘，餘眾潰遁。

translations.literal: The bandits reconnoitered that the government troops had all gone downstream, went straight upstream to land, and were about to make a surprise attack on Zinan's old camp; Sanyuan galloped there, led the masses in fierce attack, pursued to Niuguanji, destroyed their boats, killed more than a hundred bandits, and the remaining masses scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels learned that government forces had all moved downstream, landed upstream, and were about to surprise Zinan's main camp. Sanyuan rode hard to the spot, led a fierce counterattack, pursued them to Niuguanji, destroyed their boats, killed more than a hundred rebels, and put the rest to flight.

sentences.zh: 時三元累功擢至游擊，捷入，進參將。

translations.literal: At that time Sanyuan, through accumulated merit, had been promoted to brigade commander; when the victory report arrived, he was advanced to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: By then Sanyuan's accumulated victories had earned him promotion to brigade commander, and when word of the latest success arrived he was raised to colonel.

sentences.zh: 旋隨塔齊布進攻黃梅，時湖北踞匪招安慶援賊併入廣濟，塔齊布擊走之。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he followed Ta Qibu in attacking Huangmei; at that time bandits holding Hubei summoned Anqing relief bandits who merged into Guangji; Ta Qibu drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Ta Qibu against Huangmei. Rebels holding ground in Hubei called in reinforcements from Anqing, who joined forces at Guangji, but Ta Qibu drove them off.

sentences.zh: 賊敗竄黃梅，官軍追剿至大河埔。

translations.literal: The bandits were defeated and fled to Huangmei; the government troops pursued in suppression to Dahepu.
translations.idiomatic: The defeated rebels fled toward Huangmei, and government troops pursued them as far as Dahepu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，軍至黃梅，塔齊布偕澤南攻北門，三元列陣橋西以遏賊衝，塔齊布、澤南自城北溝港中取道入，三元等亦由城西越二橋，從柵門躍入。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the army reached Huangmei; Ta Qibu together with Zinan attacked the north gate; Sanyuan drew up battle lines west of the bridge to block bandit charges; Ta Qibu and Zinan entered by a route from the ditch and harbor north of the city; Sanyuan and others also crossed two bridges from the west of the city and leaped in through the stockade gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the army reached Huangmei. Ta Qibu and Zinan assaulted the north gate while Sanyuan formed his line west of the bridge to block a rebel breakout. Ta Qibu and Zinan entered through the ditch and harbor north of the city wall, while Sanyuan crossed two bridges from the west and vaulted in through the stockade gate.

sentences.zh: 賊驚竄，官軍四面兜圍，其由營壘突出者，殲滅殆盡。

translations.literal: The bandits fled in alarm; the government troops surrounded on all four sides; those who burst out from the camp fortifications were nearly all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke in panic. Government forces closed in on every side, and those who tried to break out of the camps were almost all killed.

sentences.zh: 克黃梅，移剿九壟驛，擒偽丞相餘福勝。

translations.literal: When Huangmei was taken, they moved to suppress Jiulong Post, capturing the false chancellor Yu Fusheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Huangmei fell they moved against Jiulong Post and captured the false chancellor Yu Fusheng.

sentences.zh: 大軍复渡南岸，攻九江城，三元戰績最多。

translations.literal: The great army again crossed to the south bank and attacked Jiujiang city; Sanyuan's battle achievements were the most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The main force crossed to the south bank again to attack Jiujiang, and Sanyuan's record in battle was the most distinguished.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，武昌复陷。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year, Wuchang again fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year Wuchang fell again.

sentences.zh: 八月，塔齊佈病歿，三元副澤南迴援武昌。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Ta Qibu died of illness; Sanyuan assisted Zinan in returning to relieve Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Ta Qibu died of illness, and Sanyuan served under Zinan in the relief march on Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 九月，复通城，進師崇陽，賊夜遁，遂克之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month they recovered Tongcheng, advanced the army to Chongyang, the bandits fled by night, and the city was thereby taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they recovered Tongcheng and advanced on Chongyang. The rebels fled by night, and the city was taken.

sentences.zh: 國籓疏保堪勝總兵人員，三元得記名以總兵用。

translations.literal: Guofan memorialized recommending persons fit to serve as brigade-general; Sanyuan was recorded by name to use as brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan memorialized recommending officers fit for brigade-general's rank, and Sanyuan was placed on the list for appointment as brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 會湖南防兵戰蒲圻羊樓峒失利，澤南飭諸營移駐羊樓峒，遏賊上犯，獨率三元及湘副中營官李杏春駐崇陽，於是乘勝攻蒲圻，斃賊數百。

translations.literal: When Hunan defense troops were defeated fighting at Yangloudong in Puqi, Zinan ordered the various camps to move and encamp at Yangloudong to block bandits advancing upward; he alone led Sanyuan and Hunan deputy central battalion officer Li Xingchun to garrison Chongyang; thereupon taking advantage of victory they attacked Puqi and killed several hundred bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Hunan's defensive forces were beaten at Yangloudong near Puqi, Zinan ordered the other camps to move up to Yangloudong to block a rebel advance while he alone kept Sanyuan and Li Xingchun of the Hunan central battalion with him at Chongyang. They then pressed their advantage against Puqi and killed several hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊首石達開率賊大至，三元等分路抵禦，鏖戰多時，斃賊百餘。

translations.literal: Bandit chieftain Shi Dakai led bandits in great force; Sanyuan and others resisted on divided routes, fought bitterly for a long time, and killed more than a hundred bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leader Shi Dakai arrived in force. Sanyuan and the others met him on several fronts, fought for hours, and killed more than a hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 翌日，賊悉眾來攻，繞營三匝，眾寡不敵，遂歿於陣。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits brought all their forces to attack, encircled the camp three times around, were unequal in numbers, and he thereby fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels attacked with their full strength, ringed the camp three deep, and overwhelmed by numbers he fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 贈副將銜，附祀塔齊布專祠，諡勤勇。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the rank of deputy brigade-general, granted ancillary worship in Ta Qibu's dedicated shrine, and given the posthumous title Qinyong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of deputy brigade-general, given a place in ancillary worship at Ta Qibu's dedicated shrine, and honored with the posthumous title Qinyong.

sentences.zh: 三元忠勇識大體，嘗戰濠頭堡，忽訛言子瑾光陣亡，左右以告，三元急止之曰：「速擊賊！

translations.literal: Sanyuan was loyal, brave, and understood the larger situation; once fighting at Haotou Fort, suddenly a false report spread that his son Jinguang had fallen in battle; those beside him told him; Sanyuan urgently stopped them and said: "Quickly attack the bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: Sanyuan was loyal, brave, and understood what mattered in war. Once at Haotou Fort a false rumor suddenly spread that his son Jinguang had been killed. His attendants were about to tell him, but he cut them off at once: "Attack the rebels now!"

sentences.zh: 無以吾子阻士氣。

translations.literal: "Do not let my son obstruct the troops' morale."
translations.idiomatic: "Do not let news of my son break the men's spirit."

sentences.zh: 」督戰益急。

translations.literal: He directed battle with still greater urgency.
translations.idiomatic: He drove the battle forward all the harder.

sentences.zh: 陣歿之日，將出隊，馬忽踶齧，三上三墜，眾以為不祥。

translations.literal: On the day he fell in battle, as he was about to lead his detachment out, his horse suddenly reared and bit; three times up and three times fallen; the masses regarded it as inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died in battle, as he was about to lead his men out, his horse suddenly reared and snapped at him. Three times it threw him, and his soldiers took it as an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 杏春亦同時歿於陣。

translations.literal: Xingchun also fell in battle at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xingchun fell on the field at the same time.

sentences.zh: 蕭捷三，字敏南，湖南武陵人。

translations.literal: Xiao Jiesan, styled Minnan, was a native of Wuling in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jiesan, whose style was Minnan, came from Wuling in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 由武舉投營效力，擢千總。

translations.literal: From military licentiate he entered camp to render service and was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the military provincial examination, he entered active service in the army and was promoted to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，以守省城功遷守備，署湘陰千總。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, for merit in defending the provincial capital he was transferred to garrison commander and served as acting battalion commander of Xiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Xianfeng reign, for his service in defending the provincial capital he was promoted to garrison commander and appointed acting battalion commander of Xiangyin.

sentences.zh: 四年，賊陷湘陰，坐免。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when bandits took Xiangyin, he was dismissed for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after rebels captured Xiangyin, he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓奇其才，檄領水師。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan regarded his talent as extraordinary and ordered him to command the naval force.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan was impressed by his ability and put him in command of the river fleet.

sentences.zh: 既克岳州，沿江進剿。

translations.literal: After Yuezhou was taken, they advanced along the river to suppress the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuezhou had fallen, they pushed downriver in pursuit of the rebels.

sentences.zh: 閏七月，敗賊高橋、城陵磯，進攻擂鼓台，捷三偕李孟群、楊載福等搜捕兩岸伏賊，俘馘甚眾。

translations.literal: In the intercalary seventh month they defeated bandits at Gaoqiao and Chenglingji, advanced to attack Leigutai, and Jiesan together with Li Mengqun, Yang Zaifu, and others searched out and captured hidden bandits on both banks, taking very many prisoners and heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary seventh month they routed the rebels at Gaoqiao and Chenglingji and pressed the attack on Leigutai. Jiesan, Li Mengqun, Yang Zaifu, and others swept both banks for hidden rebels and took a great number of prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 乘勝追至六溪口，平賊壘，毀賊艘殆盡，水陸各軍遂進抵嘉魚。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory they pursued to Liuxikou, leveled the bandit fortifications, and destroyed nearly all the bandit vessels; the land and river forces then advanced to Jiayu.
translations.idiomatic: Following up their victory they chased the enemy to Liuxikou, destroyed the rebel stockades, and wrecked almost every rebel ship. The combined land and river columns then reached Jiayu.

sentences.zh: 以功復職，授永綏協守備。

translations.literal: For merit he was restored to office and appointed garrison commander of the Yongshuo garrison.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was reinstated and made garrison commander of the Yongshuo garrison.

sentences.zh: 八月，進規武漢，水師分兩隊，捷三率戰艦為前隊，冒砲駛至鸚鵡洲，擲火球焚沿江賊柵，賊不支，揚帆下遁，急駛出賊前，毀其輜重。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they advanced against Wuhan; the naval force divided into two columns, with Jiesan leading the warships as the vanguard. Braving cannon fire he sailed to Yingwuzhou, cast fire balls to burn the bandit barriers along the river, and when the bandits could not hold they set sail and fled downstream. He raced ahead of them and destroyed their baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the army moved on Wuhan. The fleet split into two squadrons, with Jiesan leading the vanguard in the warships. Under heavy fire he reached Yingwuzhou, hurled fire balls that set the rebel barriers along the shore ablaze, and when the rebels broke and fled downstream he sprinted ahead of them and destroyed their supplies.

sentences.zh: 渡江攻漢陽朝宗門外土城，偕載福等殊死戰，焚漢口以內賊船皆盡。

translations.literal: Crossing the river he attacked the earthen wall outside Chaozong Gate at Hanyang; together with Zaifu and others he fought a desperate battle and burned all the bandit boats within Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river and assaulted the earthen fort outside Chaozong Gate at Hanyang. Fighting alongside Zaifu and the others to the death, he burned every rebel vessel as far inland as Hankou.

sentences.zh: 會陸軍破花園賊壘，武昌、漢陽同日復，進都司。

translations.literal: When the land army broke the bandit fortifications at Huayuan, Wuchang and Hanyang were recovered on the same day, and he was promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: When the land forces overran the rebel stockades at Huayuan, Wuchang and Hanyang were retaken the same day, and he was promoted to colonel.

sentences.zh: 時餘賊尚據襄河，乃扼新灘口，溯流進剿，賊艘千餘，連檣下駛，迎擊敗之。

translations.literal: At that time remaining bandits still held the Xiang River; he therefore seized Xintankou and advanced upstream to suppress them. More than a thousand bandit vessels sailed downstream in linked formation, and he met and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel remnants still held the Xiang River, so he blocked Xintankou and fought upstream against them. When more than a thousand rebel boats came down in linked columns, he met them head-on and routed them.

sentences.zh: 追至上游，突有悍賊數舟，用火彈撲營，灼捷三頭面手足幾死，仍裹創力戰，追剿二十餘裡。

translations.literal: Pursuing to the upper reaches, suddenly several fierce bandit boats hurled fire bombs at the camp, scorching Jiesan's head, face, hands, and feet so that he nearly died; still he bound his wounds and fought on, pursuing and suppressing for more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: In the pursuit upstream, several fierce rebel boats suddenly hurled fire bombs at his camp, burning Jiesan's head, face, hands, and feet so badly that he nearly died. He bandaged his wounds and kept fighting, driving the pursuit more than twenty li.

sentences.zh: 襄河肅清。

translations.literal: The Xiang River was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiang River was cleared of rebels.

sentences.zh: 尋偕彭玉麟敗賊蘄州釣魚台、骨牌磯，遂大破田家鎮，逾九江，直趨湖口。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, together with Peng Yulin, he defeated bandits at Diaoyutai and Gupaiji in Qizhou, then broke Tianjiazhen in a great victory, passed Jiujiang, and pressed straight for Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Peng Yulin in defeating the rebels at Diaoyutai and Gupaiji near Qizhou, smashed Tianjiazhen in a major victory, passed Jiujiang, and drove straight for Hukou.

sentences.zh: 先是江西吳城戰艦數百淪於賊，賊實沙石沉湖口，截江路，於對岸梅家洲築城，環列巨砲，拒官軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, several hundred warships from Wucheng in Jiangxi had fallen to the bandits. The bandits filled Hukou with sand and stone to block the river route, built a fort on the opposite bank at Meijiazhou, and lined up heavy cannon in a ring to resist the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, several hundred warships from Wucheng in Jiangxi had been lost to the rebels. The rebels choked Hukou with sand and stone to cut the river, built a fort on the opposite bank at Meijiazhou, and ringed it with heavy guns to hold off the government forces.

sentences.zh: 十二月，捷三駕火舟徑衝賊柵，燔賊舟百數，乘勝駛入內湖，泊大孤塘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Jiesan drove fire ships straight through the bandit barriers, burned several hundred bandit boats, and, pressing the victory, sailed into the inner lake and anchored at Dagutang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Jiesan sent fire ships straight at the rebel barriers, burned several hundred rebel boats, and rode the victory into the inner lake, where he anchored at Dagutang.

sentences.zh: 游擊孫昌國、黃翼升等出賊不意，焚內湖賊舟二百餘。

translations.literal: Brigade commanders Sun Changguo, Huang Yisheng, and others caught the bandits unawares and burned more than two hundred bandit boats on the inner lake.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade commanders Sun Changguo and Huang Yisheng took the rebels by surprise and burned more than two hundred rebel boats on the inner lake.

sentences.zh: 賊益囊土塞湖口，水涸，師弗克歸。

translations.literal: The bandits further filled bags of earth to block Hukou; the water fell, and the army could not return.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels piled earth into Hukou until the water fell away, and the fleet could not get back out.

sentences.zh: 賊以小艇雜外江巨艦中，潛縱火，水師驚潰，國籓大營泊九江北岸，亦被焚襲。

translations.literal: The bandits mixed small boats among the great ships on the outer river and secretly set fire; the naval force panicked and broke. Guofan's main camp, anchored on the north bank of Jiujiang, was also burned and attacked.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hid small boats among the great ships on the outer river and set them afire by stealth. The fleet panicked and scattered, and Guofan's main camp on the north bank at Jiujiang was burned and raided as well.

sentences.zh: 捷三陷入內湖，內外隔絕，以忠義激勵將士，軍心彌固。

translations.literal: Jiesan was trapped in the inner lake, cut off inside and out, yet he roused officers and soldiers with appeals to loyalty and righteousness, and army morale grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped in the inner lake and cut off from the main force, Jiesan rallied his officers and men on loyalty and duty, and their morale held firm.

sentences.zh: 五年，國籓入江西，益大治水師，疏薦捷三忠勇，晉游擊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Guofan entered Jiangxi and expanded the naval force on a greater scale; he memorialized recommending Jiesan's loyalty and bravery, and Jiesan was promoted to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Guofan entered Jiangxi and greatly expanded the river fleet. He memorialized praising Jiesan's loyalty and courage, and Jiesan was promoted to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 四月，敗賊雞公湖，复都昌。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he defeated bandits at Jigong Lake and recovered Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he defeated the rebels at Jigong Lake and retook Duchang.

sentences.zh: 五月，賊由大孤塘上犯，捷三逆擊，屢敗之青山，奪回舊所失帥船及賊魁艨艟巨艦。

translations.literal: In the fifth month bandits advanced upstream from Dagutang; Jiesan met them in counterattack and repeatedly defeated them at Qingshan, recovering the commander's ship he had formerly lost and the rebel chieftain's great mengchong warship.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month rebels came up from Dagutang. Jiesan met them head-on, repeatedly routed them at Qingshan, and recovered both his old command ship and the rebel leader's great mengchong warship.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，國籓檄平江營陸軍渡湖，約水師夾攻湖口，克之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Guofan ordered the Pingjiang battalion land force to cross the lake and arranged with the naval force for a pincer attack on Hukou; it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Guofan ordered the Pingjiang battalion to cross the lake and coordinated a joint assault with the fleet on Hukou, which was then taken.

sentences.zh: 賊退保石鐘山堅壘，捷三率十七舟銳進，遙見陸軍圍石鐘，氣益奮，方衝越賊艘，上下夾擊而下，石鐘山、梅家洲賊壘砲齊發，捷三中砲死。

translations.literal: The bandits fell back to hold the strong fortifications at Shizhong Mountain. Jiesan led seventeen boats in a sharp advance; from afar he saw the land army besieging Shizhong, and his spirit rose still higher. Just as he was charging through the bandit vessels in a combined attack from above and below, the bandit fortifications at Shizhong Mountain and Meijiazhou opened fire together, and Jiesan was struck by a cannonball and died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back to the stronghold on Shizhong Mountain. Jiesan led seventeen boats in a fierce charge. Seeing the land force already closing on Shizhong, he fought with redoubled ardor. As he drove through the rebel boats in a combined assault from river and shore, the rebel batteries on Shizhong Mountain and Meijiazhou opened fire together, and Jiesan was killed by a cannon shot.

sentences.zh: 詔贈副將，諡節愍，賞世職。

translations.literal: By imperial decree he was posthumously granted the rank of deputy brigade-general, given the posthumous title Jiemin, and rewarded with hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously granted him the rank of deputy brigade-general, the posthumous title Jiemin, and an hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 九年，建石鐘山水師昭忠祠，祀死事將士三千餘人，捷三為之冠。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Shizhong Mountain naval shrine to the loyal and fallen was built to worship more than three thousand officers and soldiers who died in service; Jiesan stood first among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year a shrine to the loyal dead of the river fleet was built at Shizhong Mountain for more than three thousand officers and soldiers who fell in service, with Jiesan placed at the head of the roll.

sentences.zh: 周清元，字玉泉，湘陰人。

translations.literal: Zhou Qingyuan, styled Yuquan, was a native of Xiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qingyuan, whose style was Yuquan, came from Xiangyin.

sentences.zh: 世業農。

translations.literal: His family occupation for generations was farming.
translations.idiomatic: His family had farmed for generations.

sentences.zh: 時與群兒角戲於牧場，立表數十步外，飛石命中。

translations.literal: As a boy he wrestled and played with other children on the pasture ground; setting up a target several tens of paces away, he could hit it with a thrown stone.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he wrestled and played with the other children on the pasture. He could set up a mark dozens of paces away and hit it with a thrown stone.

sentences.zh: 掘溝數丈，跳越之，能往復十次，群兒皆出其下。

translations.literal: He dug a ditch several zhang deep and leaped over it, able to go back and forth ten times; all the other children were below him.
translations.idiomatic: He dug a ditch several zhang deep and cleared it in repeated leaps, going back and forth ten times. None of the other boys could match him.

sentences.zh: 同里左明志以拳勇鳴於鄉，招致門下，傳以技，言：「天下幸無事，有事，則清元暨子光培皆驍將也。

translations.literal: A fellow townsman, Zuo Mingzhi, was famed in the district for boxing and bravery; he took Qingyuan into his household, taught him the art, and said: "If all under Heaven fortunately has no trouble, well and good; but if trouble comes, then both Qingyuan and my son Guangpei will be fierce generals."
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor, Zuo Mingzhi, was renowned locally for boxing and courage. He took Qingyuan under his wing and trained him, saying: "If the realm stays at peace, so much the better; but if war comes, Qingyuan and my son Guangpei will both prove fierce commanders."

sentences.zh: 」咸豐二年冬，賊自益陽竄臨資口，清元混跡市中，默識其軍卒舟艦糧械之數，聞提督向榮尾追至八字哨，相距三十里，遮道見榮曰：「廣西能戰賊，不過三千餘人，餘皆裹脅也。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Xianfeng, bandits fled from Yiyang toward Linzikou. Qingyuan mingled in the market and silently noted the numbers of their soldiers, boats, and grain and weapons. Hearing that Grand Coordinator Xiang Rong was pursuing close behind and had reached Bazishao, thirty li away, he blocked the road and saw Rong, saying: "Of the bandits from Guangxi who can really fight, there are no more than three thousand-odd; the rest are all coerced followers."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Xianfeng, rebels fleeing from Yiyang made for Linzikou. Qingyuan moved unnoticed through the market and quietly counted their men, boats, grain, and arms. Learning that Grand Coordinator Xiang Rong was close behind and had reached Bazishao, thirty li away, he intercepted Rong on the road and said: "Of the Guangxi rebels who can actually fight, there are no more than about three thousand; the rest are all dragooned followers."

sentences.zh: 臨資口四面阻水，湘包其東南，資繞其西北，數十里平原，渺無障蔽。

translations.literal: Linzikou is blocked by water on all four sides: the Xiang River wraps its southeast, the Zi River loops its northwest, and for several tens of li there is open plain with scarcely any cover.
translations.idiomatic: Linzikou is hemmed in by water on every side—the Xiang on the southeast, the Zi on the northwest—and for dozens of li around it lies open plain without cover.

sentences.zh: 賊所擄民船笨重不易行，一炬可盡也。

translations.literal: The civilian boats the bandits had seized are heavy and clumsy and hard to move; one torch could burn them all.
translations.idiomatic: The civilian boats they have seized are heavy and slow; a single blaze could destroy them all.

sentences.zh: 請以兵扼要路，使不得偷渡，賊糧盡，旬日當餓死，何怯而不為？

translations.literal: I beg that troops be sent to hold the critical routes so they cannot slip across; when the bandits' grain is exhausted, within ten days they should starve to death—why shrink from doing this?
translations.idiomatic: Send troops to hold the key crossings so they cannot escape. Once their supplies run out, they will starve within ten days. Why hesitate to act?

sentences.zh: 」榮不省，固請，榮叱之退。

translations.literal: Rong did not understand; Qingyuan pressed his plea, and Rong shouted at him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Rong did not grasp his point. When Qingyuan pressed the matter, Rong shouted him away.

sentences.zh: 賊遂從容駛去。

translations.literal: The bandits then sailed away at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then sailed off unhurried.

sentences.zh: 及東南糜爛，清元歎曰：「賊自走絕地，向公縱之去，能辭咎耶？

translations.literal: When the southeast was ravaged, Qingyuan sighed and said: "The bandits had walked themselves into a dead end, yet Lord Xiang let them go—can he escape blame?"
translations.idiomatic: When the southeast lay in ruins, Qingyuan sighed and said: "The rebels had trapped themselves in a dead end, yet Lord Xiang let them go. How can he escape blame?"

sentences.zh: 三年，國籓大治水軍，清元與光培同應募，隸千總楊載福部下。

translations.literal: In the third year Guofan greatly developed the naval force; Qingyuan and Guangpei both answered the call together and served under battalion commander Yang Zaifu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Guofan built up the river fleet on a large scale. Qingyuan and Guangpei both enlisted and served under battalion commander Yang Zaifu.

sentences.zh: 載福嘗為湘陰汛外委，夙才清元；

translations.literal: Zaifu had once been an external assistant at the Xiangyin garrison post and had long recognized Qingyuan's talent;
translations.idiomatic: Zaifu had once served as an external assistant at the Xiangyin garrison and had long known Qingyuan's ability;

sentences.zh: 捷三官湘陰時，亦知清元驍勇，故戰必與俱。

translations.literal: when Jiesan held office in Xiangyin he too knew Qingyuan's fierce bravery, so in battle he always kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: and when Jiesan had served at Xiangyin he too had recognized Qingyuan's courage, so in every battle he kept him close.

sentences.zh: 四年，賊踞湘潭，載福等帥水師進剿，時賊掠民船數千，旗幟蔽兩岸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year bandits held Xiangtan; Zaifu and others led the naval force forward to suppress them. At that time the bandits had seized several thousand civilian boats, and their banners covered both banks.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year rebels held Xiangtan, and Zaifu led the fleet against them. The rebels had seized thousands of civilian boats, and their banners darkened both banks.

sentences.zh: 水軍本新募，又經岳州新挫，望之奪氣​​。

translations.literal: The naval force had only just been newly recruited and had also recently suffered defeat at Yuezhou; at the sight their spirit was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet was newly recruited and had just been beaten at Yuezhou; at the sight the men lost heart.

sentences.zh: 清元言於介眾曰：「民船不能戰，一炬可盡也！

translations.literal: Qingyuan said to the officers and soldiers: "Civilian boats cannot fight; one torch can burn them all!"
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan told the officers and men: "Those civilian boats cannot fight. One blaze can destroy them all!"

sentences.zh: 」遂隨載福猛擊，逼賊巨艦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed Zaifu in a fierce attack and pressed close to the bandits' great ships.
translations.idiomatic: He then charged with Zaifu, closing hard on the rebel great ships.

sentences.zh: 賊倉卒以瓷碗來擲，清元手接而回擲之，中賊渠。

translations.literal: The bandits in haste hurled porcelain bowls; Qingyuan caught them in his hand and threw them back, striking a bandit chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hurled porcelain bowls in desperation. Qingyuan caught them and threw them back, striking a rebel leader.

sentences.zh: 載福躍登賊舟，清元隨聳身入，用火球分擲左右舟，風烈火大熾，賊爭赴水死。

translations.literal: Zaifu leaped aboard a bandit boat; Qingyuan vaulted in after him, cast fire balls to left and right boats, and with wind fierce the fire blazed greatly; bandits scrambled into the water to die.
translations.idiomatic: Zaifu leaped onto a rebel boat and Qingyuan vaulted in after him. They hurled fire balls to the boats on either side; the wind fanned the flames until they roared, and rebels plunged into the water to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 從軍見火起，急槳爭進，分途縱火，燔賊船皆盡。

translations.literal: The following troops saw the fire rise, rowed urgently in competition to advance, set fires on separate routes, and burned all the bandit boats.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the blaze, the rest of the force rowed forward at full speed, spread out to set fires on every side, and burned the rebel fleet to the last boat.

sentences.zh: 以功拔充哨官，隨攻克岳州、嘉魚。

translations.literal: For merit he was specially promoted to squad leader and followed in the capture of Yuezhou and Jiayu.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to squad leader and took part in the capture of Yuezhou and Jiayu.

sentences.zh: 八月，攻克武漢，受重創，力疾進剿蘄、黃、田家鎮皆有功。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Wuhan was taken; he received grave wounds yet forced himself onward despite illness to suppress bandits, and at Qizhou, Huangzhou, and Tianjiazhen he had merit in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wuhan fell. Though badly wounded, he pressed on in spite of his injuries and distinguished himself at Qizhou, Huangzhou, and Tianjiazhen.

sentences.zh: 五年，武昌再陷，隨彭玉麟回援，駐金口，扼上游。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Wuchang fell again; he followed Peng Yulin back to relieve it, encamped at Jinkou, and blocked the upper reaches.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Wuchang fell again. He returned with Peng Yulin to relieve the city, encamped at Jinkou, and held the upper river.

sentences.zh: 每戰必身先，不受創不止。

translations.literal: In every battle he always led from the front; unless wounded he would not stop.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he led from the front and would not stop until he had been wounded.

sentences.zh: 六年，胡林翼攻武昌，經歲不下，議先斷糧路困賊，乃檄水師清江面賊船。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Hu Linyi attacked Wuchang; for a full year he could not take it. It was proposed first to cut the grain route and wear the bandits down, and he therefore ordered the naval force to clear bandit boats from the river surface.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Hu Linyi besieged Wuchang for a full year without success. The plan was to cut the rebels' supply line and starve them out, so he ordered the fleet to sweep rebel boats from the river.

sentences.zh: 清元時典水師副後營，率先下駛，越武、漢二城，直駐沙口，屢敗賊。

translations.literal: Qingyuan then commanded the naval force's rear auxiliary second battalion; he took the lead sailing downstream, passed the two cities of Wuchang and Hanyang, and went straight to encamp at Shakou, repeatedly defeating bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan then commanded the fleet's rear auxiliary second battalion. He led the way downstream, passed Wuchang and Hanyang, and pushed straight to Shakou, repeatedly defeating the rebels.

sentences.zh: 駐沙口八閱月，賊糧斷，城賊乃困。

translations.literal: Encamped at Shakou for eight months, he cut off the bandits' grain; the bandits in the city were thereby trapped.
translations.idiomatic: After eight months at Shakou he had cut the rebels' supplies, and the garrison in the city was brought to bay.

sentences.zh: 十一月二十二日，清元由沙口帥師上擊，先破賊浮橋，斷其鐵鍊，大戰黃鶴樓下，被砲傷，力戰不退，各營繼之，遂克武昌。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of the eleventh month Qingyuan led his force upstream from Shakou in attack, first broke the bandits' pontoon bridge and severed their iron chains, and fought a great battle below Yellow Crane Tower. Wounded by cannon, he fought on without retreat; the various battalions followed, and Wuchang was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second of the eleventh month Qingyuan led his men upstream from Shakou. He first broke the rebel pontoon bridge and cut their iron chains, then fought a major battle below Yellow Crane Tower. Hit by cannon fire, he held his ground; the other battalions came up behind him, and Wuchang fell.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以創重卒於軍，年二十有六。

translations.literal: Before long, from the severity of his wounds he died in camp at the age of twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he died in camp from his wounds, aged twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 清元時已洊保參將，詔視副將例議卹，諡貞愍，賞世職。

translations.literal: Qingyuan had already been repeatedly recommended for brigade-general; by imperial decree he was treated under the regulations for deputy brigade-general in deliberating condolence rewards, given the posthumous title Zhenmin, and granted hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan had already been recommended for promotion to brigade-general. The throne ordered condolence honors according to the regulations for a deputy brigade-general, granted him the posthumous title Zhenmin, and awarded an hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 石鐘山昭忠祠，捷三冠而清元次之。

translations.literal: At the Shizhong Mountain shrine to the loyal and fallen, Jiesan stood first and Qingyuan second.
translations.idiomatic: At the shrine to the loyal dead on Shizhong Mountain, Jiesan was honored first and Qingyuan second.

sentences.zh: 蔡應龍，江西樂平人。

translations.literal: Cai Yinglong was a native of Leping in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yinglong came from Leping in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 由行伍洊升千總。

translations.literal: From the ranks he was promoted in succession to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 道光三十年，升廣西永寧營守備。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang he was promoted to garrison commander of the Yongning garrison in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of the Daoguang reign he was promoted to garrison commander of the Yongning garrison in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年七月，提督向榮擊賊於東鄉，馬中砲斃，應龍以所乘馬授榮，步行接戰，立斃賊三人，榮乃得免。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Xianfeng, Grand Coordinator Xiang Rong fought bandits at Dongxiang; his horse was struck by a cannonball and killed. Yinglong gave Rong the horse he was riding, fought on foot to meet the enemy, and on the spot killed three bandits, so that Rong was able to escape.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Xianfeng, Grand Coordinator Xiang Rong fought rebels at Dongxiang. His horse was killed by a cannon shot. Yinglong gave Rong his own mount, fought on foot, and killed three rebels on the spot, allowing Rong to escape.

sentences.zh: 欽差大臣賽尚阿以聞，授梧州都司。

translations.literal: Imperial Commissioner Saishang'a reported the matter, and Yinglong was appointed colonel at Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Commissioner Saishang'a reported the deed, and Yinglong was appointed colonel at Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，晉游擊。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，江寧賊掠商船，泊觀音門外，時榮官欽差大臣，飭應龍偕知府陳景曾馳往，諭以大義，船戶各憬悟聽命，自焚其船，押船賊無一得脫者，計焚毀及逃竄千餘艘，遣散水手萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, bandits at Jiangning seized merchant boats and anchored outside Guanyin Gate. At that time Rong held the post of Imperial Commissioner; he ordered Yinglong together with prefect Chen Jingzeng to ride there in haste, admonished them with the greater principle of righteousness, and the boat owners each awakened and obeyed, burning their own boats. Of the bandits guarding the boats not one escaped; in all more than a thousand boats were burned or destroyed in flight, and more than ten thousand sailors were dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year rebels at Jiangning seized merchant boats and anchored outside Guanyin Gate. Rong, then serving as Imperial Commissioner, sent Yinglong with Prefect Chen Jingzeng to the scene. They appealed to the boat owners' sense of duty; each man came to his senses and obeyed, burning his own vessel. Not one rebel boat guard escaped. More than a thousand boats were burned or wrecked in flight, and more than ten thousand sailors were sent home.

sentences.zh: 時賊踞城外街，與雨花台相犄角，應龍潛師過雨花台，至街尾縱火燒賊壘，賊驚遁，官軍截擊之，斬馘無算。

translations.literal: At that time bandits held the streets outside the city in mutual support with Yuhuatai. Yinglong led troops secretly past Yuhuatai, reached the end of the street, and set fire to the bandit fortifications. The bandits fled in alarm; the government army intercepted and struck them, killing and beheading beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels then held the streets outside the walls in mutual support with Yuhuatai. Yinglong slipped troops past Yuhuatai, reached the far end of the street, and set the rebel stockades ablaze. The rebels broke and fled; government troops cut them off and killed them beyond count.

sentences.zh: 四年，升全州營參將。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to brigade-general of the Quanzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to brigade-general of the Quanzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 五月，大兵圍偪江寧，賊拒守不出，應龍登鍾山，望太平門外賊勢，賊見官軍少，包抄而上，應龍且戰且退，以伏兵擊賊，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the great army pressed and besieged Jiangning; the bandits held firm and would not come out. Yinglong ascended Zhong Mountain to observe the bandit force outside Taiping Gate. The bandits saw that the government army was few and enveloped them from the flanks and advanced. Yinglong fought while retreating and struck the bandits with hidden troops, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the main force closed in on Jiangning, but the rebels held the walls and refused to come out. Yinglong climbed Zhong Mountain to survey the rebel positions outside Taiping Gate. Seeing how few government troops were present, the rebels tried to envelop them. Yinglong fought a fighting retreat, then hit them with ambush troops and routed them.

sentences.zh: 時賊船麕集於江北七里洲，應龍駕小船入，潛薄北岸，射火箭毀其船二十，而大隊賊船適至，應龍舍舟陸戰，燃砲擊沉賊船數只。

translations.literal: At that time bandit boats were densely gathered at Qilizhou on the north bank of the river. Yinglong drove a small boat in, secretly approached the north bank, and shot fire arrows that destroyed twenty of their boats. Just then a large force of bandit boats arrived; Yinglong abandoned his boat to fight on land, fired cannon, and sank several bandit boats.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel boats were massed at Qilizhou on the north bank. Yinglong took a small boat in, stole up to the north shore, and destroyed twenty boats with fire arrows. A large rebel squadron then arrived; Yinglong left his boat to fight on land, fired his guns, and sank several rebel vessels.

sentences.zh: 閏七月，擊賊洪武門，斬首數百級，复連敗賊高橋門等處，三日斃賊數千。

translations.literal: In the intercalary seventh month he attacked bandits at Hongwu Gate and took several hundred heads; he again defeated bandits in succession at Gaoqiao Gate and other places, and in three days killed several thousand bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary seventh month he attacked rebels at Hongwu Gate and took several hundred heads. He then routed them again at Gaoqiao Gate and elsewhere, killing several thousand rebels in three days.

sentences.zh: 賊猝於兩花台、洪武門突出，撲七星橋營壘，應龍擊卻之。

translations.literal: Bandits suddenly burst out at Lianghuatai and Hongwu Gate, rushed the camp fortifications at Qixing Bridge, and Yinglong struck and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels suddenly sallied from Lianghuatai and Hongwu Gate and stormed the camp at Qixing Bridge. Yinglong beat them back.

sentences.zh: 旋升楚雄副將。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to deputy brigade-general at Chuxiong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to deputy brigade-general at Chuxiong.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊造木簰，上施木城，列巨砲，沿南岸下駛，至八卦洲擱淺。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the bandits built wooden rafts, mounted wooden forts upon them, lined up heavy cannon, and sailed downstream along the south bank until they ran aground at Baguazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the rebels built wooden rafts topped with wooden forts and heavy guns, then floated them down the south bank until they ran aground at Baguazhou.

sentences.zh: 應龍乘夜發火燒之，賊爭赴水死。

translations.literal: Yinglong took advantage of the night to set fire and burn them; bandits scrambled into the water to die.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong attacked by night and set them ablaze. Rebels plunged into the water to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 官軍突煙上簰，擒斬餘黨淨盡。

translations.literal: The government army burst through the smoke onto the rafts, captured and beheaded the remaining partisans, and cleared them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops charged through the smoke onto the rafts, captured and killed the survivors, and wiped them out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 時浦口九洑洲久為賊踞，以梗官軍，陸軍攻之，賊船來援。

translations.literal: At that time Jiufuzhou at Pukou had long been held by bandits, obstructing the government army. The land force attacked it, and bandit boats came to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiufuzhou at Pukou had long been held by rebels and blocked government operations. When the land force attacked it, rebel boats came to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 應龍統帶紅單、拖罟各船截擊，賊敗遁，官軍遂奪九洑洲。

translations.literal: Yinglong commanded red-banner boats, drag-net boats, and other vessels to intercept and strike; the bandits were defeated and fled, and the government army then took Jiufuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong led red-banner boats, drag-net boats, and other vessels in an intercepting attack. The rebels were beaten and fled, and the government forces took Jiufuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，赴秣陵關查勘地勢，還言於榮，請乘虛襲板橋賊營，既可援應水師，更可抄出雨花台、上坊橋諸賊營之後。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he went to Moling Pass to survey the terrain, returned and spoke to Rong, and requested to take advantage of a gap to strike the bandit camp at Banqiao. This would both support the naval force and allow a flanking move behind the bandit camps at Yuhuatai, Shangfang Bridge, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he reconnoitered the ground at Moling Pass and, on returning, urged Rong to seize the moment and strike the rebel camp at Banqiao. The move would both support the fleet and allow troops to get behind the rebel camps at Yuhuatai, Shangfang Bridge, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 遂率千人間道襲擊，街外賊敗走，餘賊憑壘死守，复急攻之，焚其壘。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led a thousand men by a hidden route in a surprise attack; the bandits outside the streets were defeated and fled, while the remaining bandits relied on their fortifications and defended to the death. He again pressed the attack urgently and burned their fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: He then led a thousand men by a hidden path in a surprise attack. The rebels in the outer streets broke and ran; the rest held their stockades to the death. He pressed the assault and burned the fortifications.

sentences.zh: 五年九月，官軍為蕪湖援賊牽制，應龍攻奪米家嶺賊壘二、廣福磯賊壘四。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year the government army was tied down by bandits relieving Wuhu; Yinglong attacked and seized two bandit fortifications at Mijialing and four bandit fortifications at Guangfuji.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifth year government forces were pinned down by rebels relieving Wuhu. Yinglong captured two rebel stockades at Mijialing and four at Guangfuji.

sentences.zh: 賊旋於丁橋一帶袤延築壘，其地則外圍塘港，中間小路。

translations.literal: The bandits then built fortifications in extended lines along the Dingqiao stretch; the ground was surrounded outside by ponds and channels, with a small path in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then threw up a long line of stockades around Dingqiao. The ground was ringed by ponds and canals, with a narrow path through the middle.

sentences.zh: 應龍率師攻擊時許，遽麾軍退，誘賊過而擊之，殲溺無算。

translations.literal: Yinglong led his force in attack for some time, then suddenly waved the army to retreat, lured the bandits across, and struck them, killing and drowning beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong attacked for a time, then suddenly ordered a withdrawal, drew the rebels across the path, and struck them, killing and drowning them beyond count.

sentences.zh: 六年，江寧賊分股至楊家壩、陳莊築壘，欲窺倉頭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year bandits at Jiangning split into detachments and came to Yangjiaba and Chenzhuang to build fortifications, intending to spy out Cangtou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year rebel detachments from Jiangning built stockades at Yangjiaba and Chenzhuang, probing toward Cangtou.

sentences.zh: 應龍與總兵張國樑分路衝擊，斷賊為二，賊敗竄歸巢。

translations.literal: Yinglong together with regional commander Zhang Guoliang charged on divided routes, cut the bandits in two, and the bandits were defeated and fled back to their lair.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong and Regional Commander Zhang Guoliang attacked on separate routes, cut the rebel force in two, and drove the survivors back to their base.

sentences.zh: 三月，督兵攻拔炭渚、下蜀街、太平橋一帶賊壘七，毀沿江賊卡十餘處，殲斃四千餘人。

translations.literal: In the third month he directed troops to attack and take seven bandit fortifications along the Tanzhu, Xiashujie, and Taipingqiao stretch, destroyed more than ten bandit checkpoints along the river, and killed more than four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he led troops in capturing seven rebel stockades around Tanzhu, Xiashujie, and Taipingqiao, destroyed more than ten rebel river checkpoints, and killed more than four thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 五月，赴援寧國，戰歿。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he went to relieve Ningguo and fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he marched to relieve Ningguo and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 榮以聞，詔以應龍在窯灣力戰身亡，命優恤，諡勇介，給世職。

translations.literal: Rong reported the matter; by imperial decree, because Yinglong had fought fiercely at Yaowan and died, he was ordered exceptional condolence rewards, given the posthumous title Yongjie, and granted hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: Rong reported his death. The throne learned that Yinglong had fought to the end at Yaowan and ordered exceptional honors, granting him the posthumous title Yongjie and an hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 蕭意文，字章甫，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Xiao Yiwen, styled Zhangfu, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yiwen, whose style was Zhangfu, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 初隸羅澤南麾下，從征江西、湖北，累以功至參將。

translations.literal: At first he served under Luo Zinan, followed campaigns in Jiangxi and Hubei, and through repeated merit rose to brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Luo Zinan, campaigned in Jiangxi and Hubei, and rose through repeated distinction to brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，李續賓徵皖北，從克潛山、太湖、舒城、桐城，進攻三河鎮。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng, when Li Xubin campaigned in northern Anhui, Yiwen followed in the capture of Qianshan, Taihu, Shucheng, and Tongcheng, and advanced to attack Sanhe Town.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xianfeng, when Li Xubin campaigned in northern Anhui, he followed in the capture of Qianshan, Taihu, Shucheng, and Tongcheng and advanced against Sanhe Town.

sentences.zh: 三河鎮者，舒、廬適中地，賊屯糧械以濟廬州、金陵者也。

translations.literal: Sanhe Town lay midway between Shucheng and Luzhou; the bandits stored grain and weapons there to supply Luzhou and Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhe Town stood midway between Shucheng and Luzhou. The rebels kept grain and arms there to supply Luzhou and Jinling.

sentences.zh: 築大城，環以九壘，備嚴甚。

translations.literal: They built a great walled town ringed by nine fortifications; defenses were very strict.
translations.idiomatic: They had built a great walled town ringed by nine outlying stockades, and its defenses were formidable.

sentences.zh: 續賓銳意攻取，十月，分三路進剿，意文攻河南老鼠夾賊壘，冒砲石先進，各營繼之，縱火焚其壘，賊大亂。

translations.literal: Xubin was determined to take it. In the tenth month he divided into three routes to advance and suppress the bandits. Yiwen attacked the bandit fortification at Laoshujia south of the river, braved cannon and stones to advance first, and the various battalions followed. They set fire and burned the fortifications, and the bandits fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Xubin was determined to take the town. In the tenth month he divided his force into three columns. Yiwen assaulted the rebel stockade at Laoshujia south of the river, leading the charge under cannon fire and falling stones. The other battalions followed, set the stockades ablaze, and threw the rebels into chaos.

sentences.zh: 意文受砲創，殊死戰，奪柵入，九壘皆下，賊盡殲，無脫者。

translations.literal: Yiwen received a cannon wound yet fought a desperate battle, seized the barriers and entered; all nine fortifications were taken, the bandits were entirely exterminated, and none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded by cannon fire, Yiwen fought on to the death, broke through the barriers, and took all nine stockades. The rebels were wiped out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 官軍傷亡千餘，意文以創重歸營卒。

translations.literal: The government army had more than a thousand killed and wounded; Yiwen, from the severity of his wounds, returned to camp and died.
translations.idiomatic: The government force lost more than a thousand killed and wounded. Yiwen returned to camp with grave wounds and died there.

sentences.zh: 詔贈副將，諡剛勇。

translations.literal: By imperial decree he was posthumously granted the rank of deputy brigade-general and given the posthumous title Gangyong.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously granted him the rank of deputy brigade-general and the posthumous title Gangyong.

sentences.zh: 續賓部將以敢戰著、同死三河之難者，彭友勝、劉神山，均見續賓傳。

translations.literal: Among Xubin's subordinate generals famed for daring in battle who died together in the calamity at Sanhe were Peng Yousheng and Liu Shenshan; both are treated in Xubin's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Among Xubin's officers noted for courage who died with him in the disaster at Sanhe were Peng Yousheng and Liu Shenshan; both are discussed in Xubin's biography.

sentences.zh: 周福高，字子祥。

translations.literal: Zhou Fugao, styled Zixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fugao, courtesy name Zixiang.

sentences.zh: 亦先從澤南援剿江、鄂。

translations.literal: He too had earlier followed Ze'nan to relieve and suppress bandits in Jiang and E.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier served under Luo Ze'nan in relief operations against rebels in Jiangxi and Hubei.

sentences.zh: 續賓接統湘軍，福高無役不從。

translations.literal: When Xubin took command of the Xiang Army, Fugao followed him in every campaign without exception.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xubin assumed command of the Xiang Army, Fugao followed him into every battle.

sentences.zh: 以小池口、梅家洲諸戰尤用命，累官至參將。

translations.literal: In battles at such places as Xiaochikou and Meijiazhou he was especially dutiful in executing orders, and through repeated promotions rose to the rank of colonel.
