translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself at Xiaochikou, Meijiazhou, and other engagements, eventually rising through the ranks to colonel.

sentences.zh: 軍抵三河，援賊麕至，諸將知戰必敗，無鬥志。

translations.literal: When the army reached Sanhe, relieving bandits swarmed in; the generals knew battle must end in defeat and lost fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Sanhe, rebel reinforcements poured in. The officers knew the battle was lost before it began, and their will to fight collapsed.

sentences.zh: 福高憤然曰：「男兒效力疆場，寧可逆計禍福，敗則死耳，吾輩畏死不來矣！

translations.literal: Fugao said angrily: "A man serves on the battlefield—how can he beforehand calculate fortune and disaster? Defeat means death, nothing more; if we feared death we would never have come!"
translations.idiomatic: Fugao spoke in anger: "A man serves at the frontier—who weighs profit and loss before the fight? If we fall, we fall; if we feared death, we would never have come at all!"

sentences.zh: 既至此，敢惜死隳壯志！

translations.literal: Having come this far, how dare one spare his life and ruin heroic resolve!
translations.idiomatic: Having come this far, how can we cling to life and break our oath?

sentences.zh: 」遂慷慨赴敵，力戰而歿。

translations.literal: " Then he went forth generously toward the enemy, fought with all his strength, and died.
translations.idiomatic: With that he charged into the enemy ranks, fought until he could fight no more, and fell.

sentences.zh: 詔贈副將，諡敏烈。

translations.literal: By imperial decree he was posthumously granted the rank of deputy brigade-general and given the posthumous title Minlie.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously granted him the rank of deputy brigade-general and the posthumous title Minlie.

sentences.zh: 彭志德，字道一。

translations.literal: Peng Zhide, styled Daoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Zhide, courtesy name Daoyi.

sentences.zh: 隸湘軍，每戰必為前驅，恥居人後。

translations.literal: Attached to the Xiang Army, in every battle he invariably served as vanguard, taking shame in falling behind others.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Xiang Army and always took the vanguard, ashamed to let others pass him by.

sentences.zh: 累官至參將。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he rose to the rank of colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated promotions brought him to the rank of colonel.

sentences.zh: 三河之役，諸營皆潰，志德率所部貫賊陣突出，死者過半，身受重創。

translations.literal: In the battle of Sanhe, all camps broke; Zhide led his command to pierce through the bandit array and break out; more than half died, and he himself received grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: At Sanhe the whole line collapsed. Zhide drove his men through the rebel formation and broke out, losing more than half his force and taking grave wounds himself.

sentences.zh: 走入中右營，與副將李存漢等竭力死守，越三日，營陷，死之。

translations.literal: He entered the central-right camp and, with deputy brigade-general Li Cunhan and others, exerted every effort in staunch defense; after three days the camp fell and he died there.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back to the central-right camp, where he and Deputy Brigadier Li Cunhan held out with every ounce of strength. After three days the camp was overrun and he died in its defense.

sentences.zh: 詔贈副將，諡武烈。

translations.literal: By imperial decree he was posthumously granted the rank of deputy brigade-general and given the posthumous title Wulie.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously granted him the rank of deputy brigade-general and the posthumous title Wulie.

sentences.zh: 李存漢，以鄉勇隨剿廣西、江西、湖北等省，累官至副將。

translations.literal: Li Cunhan, as village militia, followed campaigns to suppress bandits in Guangxi, Jiangxi, Hubei, and other provinces, rising through repeated promotions to deputy brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunhan entered service as village militia and fought rebels across Guangxi, Jiangxi, Hubei, and other provinces, eventually rising to deputy brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 未抵三河鎮之先，進攻舒城者凡五營，並西北面賊壘，獨存漢一軍攻東南城門。

translations.literal: Before reaching Sanhe town, five camps in all advanced to attack Shucheng, all joining against the bandit fortifications on the northwest face; Cunhan alone with one army attacked the southeast city gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army reached Sanhe, five battalions besieged Shucheng and assaulted the rebel works on the northwest side; Cunhan alone was assigned to storm the southeast gate.

sentences.zh: 壘既破，城賊以存漢故，弗能救，旋棄城遁，追斬無遺。

translations.literal: Once the fortifications were broken, the city bandits, because of Cunhan, could not be relieved; soon they abandoned the city and fled; pursuit cut them down without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Once the works fell, the rebels inside could not be reinforced because of Cunhan's position; they soon abandoned the city and fled, and the pursuers cut down every last man.

sentences.zh: 續賓被圍三河，調桐城戍兵未至，事迫，誓必死，存漢等皆跪泣，原從死以報國。

translations.literal: Xubin was besieged at Sanhe; troops garrisoned at Tongcheng whom he summoned had not arrived; the situation pressed; he swore he must die; Cunhan and the others all knelt weeping, wishing to follow him in death to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xubin was trapped at Sanhe and the Tongcheng garrison he had called for had not arrived, the crisis was upon them. He vowed to die where he stood. Cunhan and the others knelt in tears and begged to die with him in service to the throne.

sentences.zh: 續賓陷陣卒，存漢與道員孫守信等堅守待援，力持三晝夜。

translations.literal: Xubin fell in the array and died; Cunhan, with circuit intendant Sun Shouxin and others, held firm awaiting relief, strenuously maintaining the position for three day-and-nights.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xubin fell in battle. Cunhan, Circuit Intendant Sun Shouxin, and the others held on for three days and nights, waiting for relief that never came.

sentences.zh: 營陷，存漢率壯士衝賊陣，越壕走保桐城。

translations.literal: The camp fell; Cunhan led brave warriors to charge the bandit array, crossed the moat, and fled to hold Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the camp finally fell, Cunhan led a band of picked men through the rebel lines, crossed the moat, and withdrew toward Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 賊大至，城破，存漢巷戰歿。

translations.literal: Bandits arrived in great numbers; the city was breached; Cunhan died fighting in the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel forces arrived in overwhelming numbers. The city fell, and Cunhan died fighting street by street.

sentences.zh: 詔贈總兵，諡果愍。

translations.literal: By imperial decree he was posthumously granted the rank of brigade-general and given the posthumous title Guomin.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously granted him the rank of brigade-general and the posthumous title Guomin.

sentences.zh: 福高、志德、存漢均湘鄉人，並附祀續賓祠。

translations.literal: Fugao, Zhide, and Cunhan were all natives of Xiangxiang; all were jointly enshrined in Xubin's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Fugao, Zhide, and Cunhan were all from Xiangxiang and were jointly enshrined in Li Xubin's memorial temple.

sentences.zh: 同時游擊杜廷光、王懷興，均湘鄉人，均以苦戰陣亡。

translations.literal: At the same time, guerrilla officers Du Tingguang and Wang Huaixing, both natives of Xiangxiang, both died in fierce battle on the field.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, Guerrilla Officers Du Tingguang and Wang Huaixing, fellow natives of Xiangxiang, also fell after bitter fighting.

sentences.zh: 賴高翔，福建和平人。

translations.literal: Lai Gaoxiang, a native of Heping, Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Gaoxiang was a native of Heping in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 少入行伍，累功至千總。

translations.literal: In youth he entered the ranks; through accumulated merit he reached the rank of battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the army in youth and rose through merit to the rank of battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，潮州小刀會匪糾土匪陷漳州，高翔從總兵饒廷選討平之，擢漳州城守營都司。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, Small Sword Society bandits of Chaozhou joined with mountain bandits and seized Zhangzhou; Gaoxiang followed brigade-general Rao Tingxuan to suppress and pacify them, and was promoted to battalion commander of the Zhangzhou city garrison battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853, Chaozhou Small Sword Society rebels allied with mountain bandits to capture Zhangzhou. Gaoxiang served under Brigade General Rao Tingxuan in retaking the city and was promoted to battalion commander of the Zhangzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 四年，漳浦古竹社匪戕官擾亂，築石堡自固，官軍久攻未拔。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Guzhu Society bandits of Zhangpu murdered officials and stirred disorder, built stone forts to secure themselves, and government troops long besieged without taking them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854, rebels of the Guzhu Society in Zhangpu murdered officials and seized control, building stone forts for defense. Government forces besieged them for a long time without success.

sentences.zh: 高翔偕龍巖游擊馬至元、漳州鎮左營游擊惠壽等冒雨直搗賊巢。

translations.literal: Gaoxiang, together with Longyan guerrilla officer Ma Zhiyuan, Zhangzhou garrison left-battalion guerrilla officer Huishou, and others, braved rain to strike directly at the bandit nest.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoxiang joined Guerrilla Officer Ma Zhiyuan of Longyan, Guerrilla Officer Huishou of the Zhangzhou garrison's left battalion, and others in a rain-soaked assault on the rebel stronghold.

sentences.zh: 賊固守不下，高翔夜偕勇首畢定邦潛師梯登，克石堡，斬獲無算。

translations.literal: The bandits defended firmly and could not be dislodged; at night Gaoxiang, with brave-leader Bi Dingbang, led troops secretly by ladder ascent, captured the stone fort, and killed and captured beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held firm. That night Gaoxiang and the brave captain Bi Dingbang led a stealth force up scaling ladders, stormed the stone fort, and killed and captured beyond count.

sentences.zh: 餘匪乘夜奔竄，窮追至海汊，皆赴水死，漳州平。

translations.literal: Remaining bandits fled by night; pursuit to the sea inlets drove them all to drown themselves; Zhangzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors fled under cover of darkness. Pursuit drove them to the tidal channels, where they drowned themselves to the last man. Zhangzhou was at last pacified.

sentences.zh: 六年，江西邊錢會匪糾粵賊陷新城、貴溪，謀攻廣信。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Qian Society bandits on the Jiangxi border joined Guangdong bandits, seized Xincheng and Guixi, and plotted to attack Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856, Qian Society rebels on the Jiangxi border allied with Guangdong bandits to capture Xincheng and Guixi and advance on Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 知府沈葆楨以血書告急於廷選，高翔時從廷選駐防玉山，倍道赴之。

translations.literal: Prefect Shen Baozhen wrote an urgent report in blood to Tingxuan; Gaoxiang at the time followed Tingxuan garrisoning Yushan and traveled double marches to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Shen Baozhen sent Rao Tingxuan an urgent plea written in his own blood. Gaoxiang was then stationed with Rao at Yushan and marched at double speed to the relief.

sentences.zh: 廷選軍素無部伍，唯高翔與定邦以敢戰名，行不齎糧，止不為屯，故赴急易。

translations.literal: Tingxuan's army by nature had no fixed formations; only Gaoxiang and Dingbang were famed for daring in battle; on march they carried no grain, at halt they made no encampment; hence responding to emergencies was easy.
translations.idiomatic: Rao's force was loosely organized, but Gaoxiang and Dingbang were famed for their fighting spirit. They marched without baggage trains and seldom made formal camps, which made them swift to answer a call for help.

sentences.zh: 軍至廣信，寇旋至，背城擊賊，屢破之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Guangxin, raiders soon arrived; fighting with the city at their backs they struck bandits and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The relief force reached Guangxin just as the rebels arrived. Fighting with their backs to the city wall, they repulsed the enemy again and again.

sentences.zh: 賊來益眾，幕府文員皆懼，慫廷選還軍，高翔、定邦怒曰：「諸君怯，何如勿來？

translations.literal: Bandits came in ever greater numbers; civil officials in the headquarters all feared and urged Tingxuan to withdraw the army; Gaoxiang and Dingbang said angrily: "You gentlemen are timid—why come at all?
translations.idiomatic: As rebel numbers swelled, the civilian advisers in headquarters panicked and urged Rao to withdraw. Gaoxiang and Dingbang said in fury: "If you were such cowards, why come at all?

sentences.zh: 今我在城中，賊不知我虛實，以我能援廣信，後路必有大軍。

translations.literal: Now that we are in the city, the bandits do not know our strength or weakness; believing we can relieve Guangxin, they must think a great army follows behind us.
translations.idiomatic: As long as we hold the city, the rebels cannot gauge our strength. They will assume that anyone who could relieve Guangxin must have a larger force coming up behind.

sentences.zh: 若棄城遁，賊知吾兵寡，氣益壯，追殲立盡，尚何浙境之可歸耶？

translations.literal: If we abandon the city and flee, bandits will know our troops are few, grow bolder, pursue and annihilate us instantly—how then could we ever return to Zhejiang territory?
translations.idiomatic: If we abandon the city and run, they will know how few we are, gather their courage, and cut us down to the last man on the retreat. What hope would there be of returning to Zhejiang alive?

sentences.zh: 當為諸君決死戰，翼日觀吾破賊！

translations.literal: We shall decide a battle to the death for you gentlemen—watch us break the bandits on the morrow!
translations.idiomatic: We will fight this battle to the death for you. Watch us break the rebels tomorrow!

sentences.zh: 」乃偕定邦開城縱擊，自晨至日昃，盡毀城外賊壘，斃賊三千餘，斬渠帥數人，賊駭遁。

translations.literal: " Then together with Dingbang they opened the city gates and launched a general assault; from morning until the sun declined they destroyed all bandit fortifications outside the walls, killed more than three thousand bandits, beheaded several chieftains, and the bandits fled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: With that they threw open the gates and charged. From morning until mid-afternoon they demolished every rebel fort outside the walls, killed more than three thousand men, beheaded several rebel chiefs, and sent the rest fleeing in terror.

sentences.zh: 論功以游擊用。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed to serve as guerrilla officer.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to guerrilla officer.

sentences.zh: 廣信圍既解，廷選還浙，高翔留駐廣信。

translations.literal: Once the siege of Guangxin was lifted, Tingxuan returned to Zhejiang; Gaoxiang remained garrisoned at Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege of Guangxin was lifted, Rao returned to Zhejiang while Gaoxiang remained as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 明年七月，樂平賊踞縣城，將軍福興檄高翔往剿，賊眾五六千，分道抗拒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the following year, bandits occupied Leping county seat; General Fuxing ordered Gaoxiang to proceed against them; bandit forces numbered five or six thousand and resisted on separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the following year, rebels seized Leping. General Fuxing ordered Gaoxiang to suppress them. Five or six thousand rebels split into columns to resist.

sentences.zh: 高翔督都司馮日坤、勇目刁士樞等迎擊，賊殊死鬥，高翔突陣負創，戰益力。

translations.literal: Gaoxiang supervised battalion commander Feng Rikun, brave-captain Diao Shishu, and others in meeting the attack; bandits fought desperately; Gaoxiang broke through the array and was wounded, yet fought all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoxiang directed Battalion Commander Feng Rikun, Brave Captain Diao Shishu, and others in the counterattack. The rebels fought to the death. Gaoxiang was wounded charging the rebel line but fought on with redoubled fury.

sentences.zh: 擊斃黃衣賊目，橫衝賊營，賊大潰，乘勝蹙之，生擒偽指揮遜天侯等，餘賊竄景德鎮，遂克樂平。

translations.literal: They struck and killed a yellow-robed bandit officer, charged across the bandit camp; bandits broke in great rout; pressing the victory they captured alive the false commander Xuntian Hou and others; remaining bandits fled to Jingde Town; Leping was thus taken.
translations.idiomatic: They killed a yellow-robed rebel officer and swept through the enemy camp. The rebels broke and fled. Pressing the advantage, they captured the pseudo-commander the Marquis of Xuntian and others alive. The survivors withdrew toward Jingdezhen, and Leping fell.

sentences.zh: 移防弋陽，八年二月，補游擊。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison Yiyang; in the second month of the eighth year he was formally appointed guerrilla officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to garrison Yiyang and in February 1858 received a formal appointment as guerrilla officer.

sentences.zh: 臨江餘寇合撫州賊趨廣豐，福興退駐廣信，高翔自弋陽聞警赴援，轉戰至鉛山之石塘，賊勢益盛，兵寡援絕，力戰死。

translations.literal: Remaining bandits of Linjiang combined with Fuzhou bandits and advanced on Guangfeng; Fuxing withdrew to garrison Guangxin; Gaoxiang from Yiyang heard the alarm and rushed to aid, fighting through to Shitang in Qianshan; bandit strength grew ever greater; troops were few and relief cut off; he fought with all his strength and died.
translations.idiomatic: Remnant rebels from Linjiang joined forces with rebels from Fuzhou and marched on Guangfeng. Fuxing fell back to Guangxin. Gaoxiang marched from Yiyang at the first alarm and fought his way to Shitang in Qianshan, where rebel strength was overwhelming, reinforcements never came, and he died fighting to the last.

sentences.zh: 贈副將，給世職。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted the rank of deputy brigade-general; given hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of deputy brigade-general and a hereditary office for his descendants.

sentences.zh: 畢定邦，字康侯，山東淄川人。

translations.literal: Bi Dingbang, styled Kanghou, a native of Zichuan, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Dingbang, courtesy name Kanghou, was a native of Zichuan in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 以武童投效漳州軍營。

translations.literal: As a military licentiate he volunteered for the Zhangzhou army camp.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a military licentiate in the Zhangzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 小刀會匪陷漳州，紳民輸款，游擊饒廷選約內應，定邦率建勇助剿，戰最力，從復府城。

translations.literal: When Small Sword Society bandits seized Zhangzhou, gentry and people submitted; guerrilla officer Rao Tingxuan arranged an inside response; Dingbang led Jian braves to aid suppression, fought with greatest exertion, and joined in recovering the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Small Sword Society took Zhangzhou, local gentry and people began paying tribute to the rebels. Guerrilla Officer Rao Tingxuan arranged an uprising from within, and Dingbang led militia from Jian in the counterattack, fighting at the forefront and helping retake the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 以次討平雲霄、漳浦賊匪，斬獲尤眾。

translations.literal: In order he suppressed and pacified bandits in Yunxiao and Zhangpu; kills and captures were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He then helped pacify rebels in Yunxiao and Zhangpu, accounting for an especially large number of kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 复討平仙遊會匪，總督王懿德檄定邦率仙游得勝之師，間道馳剿。

translations.literal: Again he suppressed Xianyou Society bandits; Governor-General Wang Yide ordered Dingbang to lead the victorious troops from Xianyou by hidden route in rapid suppression.
translations.idiomatic: After helping put down society rebels in Xianyou, Governor-General Wang Yide ordered Dingbang to lead the victorious Xianyou force by a concealed route in a rapid strike.

sentences.zh: 冬夜四鼓，蛇行進，將賊堡附近釘桶竹籤拔除，黎旦，奮勇梯登，與高翔同有功，復與高翔同解廣信圍，累擢至參將。

translations.literal: On a winter night at the fourth watch they crawled forward like snakes, pulled out nail-barrels and bamboo spikes near the bandit fort; at dawn they scaled walls with brave assault; with Gaoxiang he shared merit; again with Gaoxiang he jointly relieved the siege of Guangxin; through repeated promotions he rose to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: On a winter night in the fourth watch they crawled forward under cover, pulled up the nail-stakes and bamboo spikes around the rebel fort, and at dawn stormed the walls by ladder. He won credit alongside Gaoxiang at the stone fort and again in the relief of Guangxin, rising through repeated promotions to colonel.

sentences.zh: 七年，粵賊竄圍建寧，分黨陷邵武、浦城，定邦奉檄援閩，率部眾疾趨抵甌寧，直前搏賊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Guangdong bandits fled and besieged Jianning; dividing their forces they seized Shaowu and Pucheng; Dingbang received orders to aid Fujian, led his troops in rapid march to reach Ouning, and went straight forward to grapple with bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857, Guangdong rebels besieged Jianning while detachments seized Shaowu and Pucheng. Ordered to reinforce Fujian, Dingbang rushed his troops to Ouning and threw them straight at the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊由建陽逃竄，复糾鄉團夾擊。

translations.literal: Bandits fled through Jianyang; again he mustered village corps for pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled through Jianyang, where he rallied local militia for a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 賊斷七星橋抗拒，令鄉團伏山腰，張幟以疑之，躬率勁旅迫橋，以輕兵由淺處渡河，前後合攻。

translations.literal: Bandits cut off Qixing Bridge to resist; he ordered village corps to lie ambushed on the mountainside and raise banners to confuse them; personally he led crack troops to press the bridge; with light troops he crossed the river at a shallow place; front and rear joined in attack.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels blocked Qixing Bridge. He hid militia on the hillside with banners to hold their attention, then personally led crack troops to the bridge while light units waded the shallows upstream and downstream. Front and rear closed in together.

sentences.zh: 賊殊鬥，黃衣悍黨數十，屢出盪決，盡殪之，賊大奔。

translations.literal: Bandits fought desperately; several dozen fierce yellow-robed partisans repeatedly sallied forth in decisive charges; all were slaughtered; bandits fled in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fought furiously. Several dozen ferocious fighters in yellow surcoats charged out again and again in sorties; every one was cut down, and the rest broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 毀賊壘十一，焚逆舟六十，直逼建寧臨江門。

translations.literal: They destroyed eleven bandit forts, burned sixty rebel boats, and pressed straight to Jianning's Linjiang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: They destroyed eleven rebel fortifications, burned sixty rebel boats, and pressed all the way to Linjiang Gate outside Jianning.

sentences.zh: 大股賊復來犯，縱擊敗之，斬悍目六，斃賊數千，踏平城外賊壘，遂解建寧之圍。

translations.literal: A large force of bandits again came to attack; he launched a general assault and defeated them, beheaded six fierce chiefs, killed several thousand bandits, leveled all bandit forts outside the walls, and thus lifted the siege of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: When a large rebel force returned, he drove them off, beheaded six fierce chieftains, killed several thousand men, flattened every fort outside the walls, and broke the siege of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 進搗邵武，克之，遷參將。

translations.literal: Advancing to strike Shaowu, he took it and was transferred to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Shaowu, captured it, and was promoted to colonel.

sentences.zh: 复督鄉團剿平浦城之賊，閩邊肅清，以副將升用。

translations.literal: Again supervising village corps he suppressed and pacified bandits of Pucheng; the Fujian border was cleared; he was promoted to serve as deputy brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: He then led local militia in clearing rebels from Pucheng, pacifying the Fujian border, and was promoted to deputy brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 進剿白水墩賊匪，中彈，卒於軍，年二十六。

translations.literal: Advancing to suppress bandits at Baishuidun, he was struck by a bullet and died in the army, aged twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: While pressing an attack on rebels at Baishuidun he was shot and died in camp at the age of twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 給世職，諡愍烈，與高翔同附祀廷選祠。

translations.literal: Given hereditary office; posthumous title Minlie; jointly enshrined with Gaoxiang in Tingxuan's temple.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a hereditary office and the posthumous title Minlie, and was enshrined with Gaoxiang in Rao Tingxuan's memorial temple.

sentences.zh: 劉德亮，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: Liu Deliang, a native of Changsha, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Deliang was a native of Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，投效水師營，隨道員褚汝航等破岳州踞賊，又隨知府彭玉麟克漢口鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he volunteered for the naval battalion; following circuit intendant Chu Ruhang and others he broke bandits occupying Yuezhou; again following prefect Peng Yulin he captured Hankou market-town.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he joined the naval forces and served under Circuit Intendant Chu Ruhang in breaking the rebel hold on Yuezhou, then under Prefect Peng Yulin in the capture of Hankou.

sentences.zh: 五年，勦賊武、漢、蘄、黃間，大小數十戰，德亮皆衝鋒陷陣，又隨軍斫斷橫江鐵鎖，擊沙洲爭渡之賊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he suppressed bandits between Wu, Han, Qi, and Huang; in several dozen battles large and small Deliang always charged the vanguard and plunged into arrays; again following the army he chopped through iron chains spanning the river and struck bandits at Shazhou fighting to cross.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he fought rebels across the Wuchang, Hankou, Qizhou, and Huangzhou region in dozens of engagements, always in the vanguard. He also helped cut the iron chains stretched across the Yangtze and drive off rebels fighting for a crossing at Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 嗣偕都司胡友亮堵賊童司牌，焚內湖賊艇，並燒浮橋。

translations.literal: Subsequently, together with battalion commander Hu Youliang, he blocked bandits at Tongsi Pai, burned bandit boats on the inner lake, and also burned floating bridges.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Battalion Commander Hu Youliang in blocking rebels at Tongsi Pai, burning rebel craft on the inner lake, and setting fire to their pontoon bridges.

sentences.zh: 尋與游擊孫昌凱會剿黃梅踞賊，破其要衝。

translations.literal: Soon, together with guerrilla officer Sun Changkai, he jointly suppressed bandits occupying Huangmei and broke their vital strongpoint.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Guerrilla Officer Sun Changkai in a combined operation against rebels holding Huangmei and broke their main strongpoint.

sentences.zh: 八年，福建陸路提督楊載福等攻九江，發地雷，轟塌城垣，賊由龍口河傾壁出竄，德亮率所部登岸截擊，殲數百人，复府城。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Fujian land-route provincial commander-in-chief Yang Zaifu and others attacked Jiujiang; they fired land mines, blasting down city walls; bandits poured out through Longkou River along collapsed walls in flight; Deliang led his command ashore to intercept and strike, annihilating several hundred, and recovered the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858, Provincial Commander Yang Zaifu and others besieged Jiujiang. Land mines brought down the walls, and rebels poured out through the breach at Longkou River. Deliang led his men ashore to intercept them, killed several hundred, and helped retake the city.

sentences.zh: 又隨載福軍進規安慶，先破大通賊壘。

translations.literal: Again following Zaifu's army he advanced to target Anqing and first broke bandit forts at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched with Yang's force toward Anqing and first stormed the rebel fortifications at Datong.

sentences.zh: 趨銅陵，德亮麾隊攻其北，直偪城下，身受七傷，猶裹創仰攻不退。

translations.literal: Pressing toward Tongling, Deliang waved his command to attack its north, pressing straight to the foot of the walls; he received seven wounds yet, wrapping his wounds, assaulted upward without retreating.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongling he led his company against the north wall and pressed to the foot of the ramparts. He took seven wounds yet bound them and kept assaulting upward without yielding.

sentences.zh: 池州賊黨萬餘來救安慶，擄民船渡至樅陽，載福令隨總兵陳金鼇等馳往截剿。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand bandit allies from Chizhou came to relieve Anqing, seized civilian boats and crossed to Zongyang; Zaifu ordered him to follow brigade-general Chen Jin'ao and others in rapid march to intercept and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand rebels from Chizhou marched to relieve Anqing, seized civilian boats, and crossed to Zongyang. Yang ordered Deliang to follow Brigade General Chen Jin'ao on a forced march to cut them off.

sentences.zh: 師至羅塘洲嘴，樅陽港內木椿鐵鍊層層攔截，泊賊船百餘。

translations.literal: When the army reached Luotang Continent Point, inside Zongyang harbor wooden piles and iron chains blocked in layers, with more than a hundred bandit boats moored.
translations.idiomatic: At Luotangzhou Point they found Zongyang harbor blocked with layer upon layer of wooden piles and iron chains, and more than a hundred rebel vessels at anchor.

sentences.zh: 副將王明山等登洲轟擊，督勇鳧水過港，賊驚潰，官軍盡焚其船。

translations.literal: Deputy brigade-general Wang Mingshan and others landed on the continent and opened bombardment; supervising braves they swam across the harbor; bandits fled in panic; government troops burned all their boats.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Brigadier Wang Mingshan and others landed on the point and opened fire. Deliang's braves swam the harbor under covering fire. The rebels panicked and fled, and government forces burned every rebel vessel.

sentences.zh: 遂率隊攻樅陽街尾，金鼇攻樅陽街頭。

translations.literal: Then he led his company to attack the tail end of Zongyang street; Jin'ao attacked the head of Zongyang street.
translations.idiomatic: Deliang then led his detachment against the lower end of Zongyang while Chen Jin'ao struck the upper end.

sentences.zh: 賊排砲抗拒，德亮鼓眾飛槳進截新河鐵鍊，麾隊登岸直攻中路，副將李朝斌抄賊壘後，官軍三路進偪賊壕，平其五壘，逐北二十餘裡，賊屍枕藉。

translations.literal: Bandits lined cannon to resist; Deliang roused the multitude, flew oars forward to intercept the iron chains at Xinhe, waved his command ashore to attack the center route directly; deputy brigade-general Li Chaobin outflanked behind bandit forts; government troops on three routes pressed close to bandit moats, leveled five forts, pursued north more than twenty li, and bandit corpses lay piled upon one another.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels lined up their cannon to hold them off. Deliang drove his men forward at the oars to seize the iron chains at Xinhe, landed to strike the center, while Deputy Brigadier Li Chaobin flanked the rebel forts from behind. Government forces closed on three sides, flattened five fortifications, and pursued the fleeing rebels for more than twenty li, leaving corpses piled along the road.

sentences.zh: 累功擢至參將。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he was promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merit he was promoted to colonel.

sentences.zh: 十年，再攻樅陽，破鮑家村賊壘，斬晏家塘賊魁。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he again attacked Zongyang, broke bandit forts at Baojia Village, and beheaded the bandit chieftain at Yanjiatang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he attacked Zongyang again, stormed the rebel fort at Baojia Village, and beheaded the rebel chief at Yanjiatang.

sentences.zh: 時池州賊以殷家彙為犄角，載福率步隊往攻，而令德亮等以舢板夾擊，斃匪甚多，獲槍械馬匹稱是。

translations.literal: At the time Chizhou bandits used Yinjiahui as a supporting horn; Zaifu led infantry to attack, while ordering Deliang and others with sampans to strike from both flanks; many bandits were killed; guns, weapons, and horses captured were commensurably numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Chizhou rebels had fortified Yinjiahui as an outwork. Yang led infantry against it while Deliang and others closed in from both flanks with sampans, killing large numbers and capturing a correspondingly great haul of arms and horses.

sentences.zh: 殷家匯賊壘既平，乘勝攻池州，德亮由東門外卡緣牆斬關入，破其石壘，盡毀東門外房屋，復分攻南門，獲逆艇八。

translations.literal: Once the bandit fort at Yinjiahui was pacified, pressing the victory they attacked Chizhou; Deliang from the outpost card east of the gate climbed the wall along its length, cut through the gate and entered, broke their stone fort, destroyed all houses east of the gate, again divided forces to attack the south gate, and captured eight rebel boats.
translations.idiomatic: After Yinjiahui fell they pressed on to Chizhou. Deliang scaled the wall outside the east gate, broke through the barrier, stormed the stone fort, demolished every building east of the gate, then split his force to attack the south gate and captured eight rebel vessels.

sentences.zh: 德亮奮不顧身，執旗先登，中砲，歿於陣。

translations.literal: Deliang exerted himself without regard for his body, grasped the banner and climbed first, was struck by cannon, and died in the array.
translations.idiomatic: Deliang, heedless of his own life, seized the banner and was first over the wall. A cannon shot killed him where he stood.

sentences.zh: 載福上聞，詔令議卹，諡威毅，給世職。

translations.literal: Zaifu reported upward; by decree he was ordered considered for condolence payment; posthumous title Weiyi; given hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: Yang reported his death to the throne, which ordered condolence payments and granted him the posthumous title Weiyi and a hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 陳大富，字餘庵，湖南武陵人。

translations.literal: Chen Dafu, styled Yu'an, a native of Wuling, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Dafu, courtesy name Yu'an, was a native of Wuling in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 起行伍。

translations.literal: He rose from the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks.

sentences.zh: 道光末，以外委從提督向榮勦賊廣西，回援長沙，追賊武昌，屢著戰績，洊擢常德協都司。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daoguang reign, as an external delegate he followed provincial commander-in-chief Xiang Rong to suppress bandits in Guangxi, returned to relieve Changsha, pursued bandits to Wuchang, repeatedly distinguished himself in battle, and through successive promotions rose to battalion commander of the Changde Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Daoguang era he served as an acting officer under Provincial Commander Xiang Rong against rebels in Guangxi, helped relieve Changsha, pursued the enemy to Wuchang, and won repeated distinction, rising through successive promotions to battalion commander of the Changde Brigade.

sentences.zh: 進剿江寧，轉戰蕪湖、鎮江間，以功賞花翎。

translations.literal: Advancing to suppress Jiangning, he fought back and forth between Wuhu and Zhenjiang; for merit he was awarded the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against Jiangning and fought between Wuhu and Zhenjiang, earning the peacock feather for his service.

sentences.zh: 咸豐七年，隨提督鄧紹良复寧國屬之灣沚、黃池，進游擊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xianfeng he followed provincial commander Deng Shaoliang in recovering Wanzhi and Huangchi, districts belonging to Ningguo, and was promoted to guerrilla officer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he served under Provincial Commander Deng Shaoliang in retaking Wanzhi and Huangchi, dependencies of Ningguo, and was promoted to guerrilla officer.

sentences.zh: 尋援浙江，敗賊金華、處州，除參將。

translations.literal: Soon he aided Zhejiang, defeated bandits at Jinhua and Chuzhou, and was appointed colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reinforced Zhejiang, defeated rebels at Jinhua and Chuzhou, and was appointed colonel.

sentences.zh: 賊竄婺源、石埭、太平，先後擊走之。

translations.literal: Bandits fled to Wuyuan, Shidi, and Taiping; he successively struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels raided Wuyuan, Shidi, and Taiping, he drove them off in turn.

sentences.zh: 以從復涇縣，拔南陵，擢副將。

translations.literal: For following in the recovery of Jing County and capturing Nanling, he was promoted to deputy brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in retaking Jing County and capturing Nanling he was promoted to deputy brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 八年十一月，灣沚師潰，紹良死，大富左次南陵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eighth year the army at Wanzhi was routed; Shaoliang died; Dafu shifted his position to Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: In November 1858 the force at Wanzhi was routed and Deng Shaoliang was killed. Dafu withdrew to Nanling.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，賊犯南陵，百計環攻，不得逞，十年三月，圍始解。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year bandits attacked Nanling; by every stratagem they encircled and assaulted but could not succeed; in the third month of the tenth year the siege was at last lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the following year rebels besieged Nanling by every means but could not take it. The siege was not lifted until March 1860.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其功，除皖南鎮總兵。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his merit and appointed him brigade-general of the Southern Anhui garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his service and appointed him brigade-general of the Southern Anhui garrison.

sentences.zh: 五月，偽侍王李世賢圍寧國，分黨攻金壇、南陵，時提督週天受守寧國，總兵蕭知音、參將周天孚等守金壇，大富仍守南陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the false Prince of Shi Li Shixian besieged Ningguo, divided forces to attack Jintan and Nanling; at the time provincial commander Zhou Tianshou defended Ningguo, brigade-general Xiao Zhiyin, colonel Zhou Tianfu, and others defended Jintan, and Dafu still defended Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the pseudo-Prince of Shi, Li Shixian, besieged Ningguo and sent detachments against Jintan and Nanling. Provincial Commander Zhou Tianshou held Ningguo, Brigade General Xiao Zhiyin and Colonel Zhou Tianfu held Jintan, and Dafu continued to hold Nanling.

sentences.zh: 賊眾數十萬，官軍勢不敵，各血戰死守待援。

translations.literal: Bandit forces numbered several hundred thousand; government troops' strength could not match; each bloodied battle in staunch defense awaiting relief.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel numbers ran into the hundreds of thousands. Government forces were heavily outmatched, yet each garrison fought on in blood and held out for relief.

sentences.zh: 七月，金壇陷，賊屠其城，天受知寧城不守，則盡出城中兵民數万令各逃生，自誓以身殉。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Jintan fell; bandits slaughtered its city; Tianshou knew Ning city could not be held; then he sent out all soldiers and people in the city, numbering tens of thousands, ordering each to escape for his life; he himself vowed to die with his body as sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Jintan fell and the rebels massacred its people. Seeing that Ningguo could not be held, Zhou Tianshou sent the city's entire population—soldiers and civilians numbering in the tens of thousands—out to escape and swore to die in its defense.

sentences.zh: 寧民扶老攜幼走南陵，大富開門納之。

translations.literal: Ningguo people, supporting the aged and leading the young, fled toward Nanling; Dafu opened the gates and received them.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Ningguo fled toward Nanling, old and young together. Dafu opened the gates and took them in.

sentences.zh: 八月，寧國陷，賊圍南陵益急，城中食且盡，大富以忠義激勵軍民，皆誓死弗去。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Ningguo fell; bandits besieged Nanling ever more urgently; food in the city was nearly exhausted; Dafu with loyalty and righteousness roused soldiers and people; all swore to die and not leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Ningguo fell. The siege of Nanling tightened, provisions ran low, and Dafu roused soldiers and civilians alike with appeals to loyalty and duty until all swore to hold the city or die in it.

sentences.zh: 夜遣壯士縋城出，乞援於水師，前後數輩為邏賊遮獲，最後乃得達。

translations.literal: At night he sent brave men to let themselves down from the wall and go out, begging aid from the naval force; several parties before and after were intercepted and captured by bandits on the road, but at last one got through.
translations.idiomatic: By night he sent brave men over the wall on ropes to beg relief from the fleet. Party after party was intercepted on the road, until at last one got through.

sentences.zh: 時提督楊岳斌統水師奮袂起，九月，揚帆進泊魯港，聲言攻蕪湖，密飭各營扼要隘。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Coordinator Yang Yuebin, commanding the naval force, roused himself; in the ninth month he set sail and advanced to anchor at Lugang, proclaiming an attack on Wuhu while secretly ordering each camp to hold the strategic passes.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Yang Yuebin, commanding the fleet, roused his forces. In the ninth month he sailed up and anchored at Lugang, announcing an assault on Wuhu while secretly ordering each camp to seize the key passes.

sentences.zh: 十月，水師驟登陸，出賊不意，悉燔港左右賊屯，圍賊爭馳奔魯港，囂且亂。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the naval force suddenly landed, catching the bandits off guard; they burned all bandit encampments left and right of the harbor; besieging bandits all rushed helter-skelter toward Lugang, clamorous and in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the fleet made a sudden landing and caught the rebels by surprise. It burned every rebel camp on both sides of the harbor. The besiegers broke and raced for Lugang in a noisy, chaotic rout.

sentences.zh: 大富乘城遙望見，拊髀曰：「援師至矣！

translations.literal: Dafu, riding atop the wall, saw them from afar and, slapping his thigh, said: "Relief troops have arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: Watching from the wall, Dafu saw them in the distance and slapped his thigh. "Relief has come!" he cried.

sentences.zh: 」遂出城夾擊，賊披靡，追殺十餘裡，與援師會殲賊萬餘，撲水死者無算，圍立解。

translations.literal: Then he sallied from the city in a pincer attack; the bandits broke and scattered; they pursued and killed them for more than ten li, joined the relief troops, and together annihilated over ten thousand bandits; those who plunged into the water and drowned were beyond counting; the siege was forthwith lifted.
translations.idiomatic: He then led a sortie in concert with the relief force. The rebels collapsed. The pursuit ran more than ten li, and together they destroyed over ten thousand of the enemy; countless others drowned in the water, and the siege was lifted at once.

sentences.zh: 城中兵不食月餘，僅存皮骨，民餓殍相屬。

translations.literal: The soldiers in the city had eaten nothing for more than a month; they were skin and bones; the people lay dead of starvation one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison had gone without food for more than a month and was reduced to skin and bone. Starvation deaths among the civilians followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 岳斌船粟往哺，歡聲雷動。

translations.literal: Yuebin sent grain on ships to feed them; cheers shook like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuebin sent grain by ship to feed them, and cheers rolled through the city like thunder.

sentences.zh: 大富方繕城垣固守，岳斌力言形勢不便，乃帥師屯上游，市民從者十餘萬。

translations.literal: Dafu was repairing the walls to hold firm; Yuebin strongly argued that the position was unfavorable, and so led the army to encamp upstream; more than a hundred thousand townspeople followed.
translations.idiomatic: Dafu was repairing the walls to hold the city, but Yuebin insisted the position was untenable and led the army upstream instead. More than a hundred thousand townspeople followed.

sentences.zh: 大富前後守南陵，始被圍經年，繼六閱月，以蕞爾城抗巨寇，忍死待援，卒熸凶焰，由是以善守名於時。

translations.literal: Dafu had defended Nanling before and after: first besieged for a full year, then for six months more; with this tiny city he resisted a massive enemy, enduring death while awaiting relief, and in the end extinguished the bandits' fierce flame—thus he won at that time the reputation of an excellent defender.
translations.idiomatic: Dafu had held Nanling through siege after siege—first for a full year, then for six months more. With this tiny city he had faced a vast enemy force, clinging to life until relief came and at last breaking their momentum. From that time he was famed as a master of defense.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，會水師復建德。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, the naval force joined in recovering Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year the fleet took part in recovering Jiande.

sentences.zh: 二月，李世賢率黨數万竄景德鎮，大富率兵四千自建德往援。

translations.literal: In the second month Li Shixian led tens of thousands of followers into Jingdezhen; Dafu led four thousand troops from Jiande to their relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Li Shixian led tens of thousands of followers into Jingdezhen. Dafu marched four thousand men from Jiande to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 賊銜恨，以計陷之。

translations.literal: The bandits bore a grudge and ensnared him by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, nursing a grudge, trapped him by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 盡伏悍賊牛角嶺、柳家灣、迴龍嶺等處，率隊由鎮南雙鳳橋竄李村，誘官軍，佯敗遁。

translations.literal: They hid fierce bandits at Niujiao Ridge, Liujiawan, Huilong Ridge, and other places; leading their columns they fled south from the town via Shuangfeng Bridge toward Licun, luring the government army and feigning defeat in flight.
translations.idiomatic: They concealed their best fighters at Niujiao Ridge, Liujiawan, Huilong Ridge, and elsewhere, then led their columns south from town by Shuangfeng Bridge toward Licun, feigning defeat to draw the government troops on.

sentences.zh: 大富率眾前進，躍馬爭先，參將田應科等繼之，賊突從鎮東抄出，伏賊盡起，大富挺矛力禦，砲洞左乳，血淋漓，仍裹創鏖戰。

translations.literal: Dafu led the crowd forward, spurring his horse to take the lead; Colonel Tian Yingke and others followed; bandits suddenly emerged from the east of the town in a flanking move; all the hidden bandits rose up; Dafu grasped his spear and fought hard; a cannon ball pierced his left breast; blood poured; still he bound his wound and battled on.
translations.idiomatic: Dafu led the advance at a gallop, with Colonel Tian Yingke and others close behind. Rebels suddenly swept out from the east of town, and every ambush party rose at once. Dafu fought on with his spear until a cannon ball tore through his left breast. Blood streamed down, yet he bound the wound and kept fighting.

sentences.zh: 賊從間道襲焚我營，應科及游擊蕭傳科、胡占鼇，都司胡鳳雝、熊定邦、吳定魁，千總羅廷材皆戰死。

translations.literal: Bandits by a hidden path attacked and burned our camp; Yingke, Brigade Commander Xiao Chuanke, Hu Zhanao, Battalion Commander Hu Fengyong, Xiong Dingbang, Wu Dingkui, and Battalion Commander Luo Tingcai all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels struck by a hidden route and burned the camp. Tian Yingke, Brigade Commander Xiao Chuanke, Hu Zhanao, Battalion Commanders Hu Fengyong, Xiong Dingbang, and Wu Dingkui, and Battalion Commander Luo Tingcai all fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 大富見營中火起，下馬北鄉叩首，曰：「臣力竭矣！

translations.literal: Dafu saw fire rising in the camp; he dismounted, turned north, and kowtowed, saying: "Your servant's strength is exhausted!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the camp in flames, Dafu dismounted, turned north, and kowtowed. "I have done all I can," he said.

sentences.zh: 」投李村河死。

translations.literal: He threw himself into the Licun River and died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he threw himself into the Licun River and died.

sentences.zh: 贈提督，諡威肅，建專祠南陵，應科等並附祀。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the rank of grand coordinator; given the posthumous title Weisu; a special shrine was built at Nanling; Yingke and the others were also granted ancillary worship there.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously granted him the rank of grand coordinator and the posthumous title Weisu, built him a dedicated shrine at Nanling, and enshrined Yingke and the others there as well.

sentences.zh: 陳萬勝，湘潭人。

translations.literal: Chen Wansheng was a native of Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wansheng was a native of Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 官軍規复江寧，圍攻將四年，用地雷法，穴城三十餘處，皆不就。

translations.literal: When the government army planned to recover Jiangning, the siege had lasted nearly four years; they used the underground-mine method and tunneled under the wall in more than thirty places, but none succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The government campaign to recover Jiangning had already lasted nearly four years. More than thirty mining tunnels were dug beneath the walls, but none succeeded.

sentences.zh: 同治三年六月，提督李臣典請從賊砲最密處重闕隧道，統帥曾國荃韙之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Tongzhi, Grand Coordinator Li Chengdian requested to reopen a tunnel at the spot where rebel artillery was densest; Commander Zeng Guoquan approved it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Tongzhi, Grand Coordinator Li Chengdian proposed reopening a tunnel at the point where rebel artillery was thickest. Commander Zeng Guoquan agreed.

sentences.zh: 命各軍於城下築砲台，護地道，別遣軍士刈濕葦蒿M5積城下，覆以沙土，陽為肉薄登城狀。

translations.literal: He ordered each army to build batteries below the wall to protect the tunnel; separately he sent soldiers to cut wet reeds and wormwood and pile them at the foot of the wall, cover them with sand and earth, and openly feign the appearance of a close assault to scale the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered each unit to build batteries below the wall to shield the tunnel, while other troops cut wet reeds and wormwood, piled them at the base of the wall, and covered them with sand and earth to simulate a close assault up the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 賊用全力扞爭，砲彈雨下。

translations.literal: The bandits contested with all their strength; cannonballs fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels met the effort with all their strength, and cannonballs fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 是月十五日，賊出死黨燒砲台，官軍血戰竟夕，十六日，地雷發，遂克偽都。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth of that month the bandits sent their most devoted followers to burn the batteries; the government army fought a bloody battle all night; on the sixteenth the land mine detonated, and they then captured the rebel capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth the rebels sent their most fanatical followers to burn the batteries, and the government troops fought through the night. On the sixteenth the mine exploded, and the rebel capital fell.

sentences.zh: 萬勝與郭鵬程、王紹羲則於先一日死之。

translations.literal: Wansheng, together with Guo Pengcheng and Wang Shaoxi, had died the day before.
translations.idiomatic: Wansheng, Guo Pengcheng, and Wang Shaoxi had already died the day before.

sentences.zh: 萬勝初隸吉字營，從大軍規江寧，皆為軍鋒，累功擢副將。

translations.literal: Wansheng had first served in the Jizi Battalion; following the great army in the campaign against Jiangning, he was always at the army's spearhead; for accumulated merit he was promoted to deputy brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: Wansheng had first served in the Jizi Battalion. In the campaign against Jiangning he was always in the van of the army, and for repeated merit was promoted to deputy brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 地道既成，國荃入隧親勘之，悍賊出太平門，直犯地道。

translations.literal: Once the tunnel was complete, Guoquan entered it to inspect personally; fierce bandits came out from Taiping Gate and struck straight at the tunnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the tunnel was finished, Guoquan entered it to inspect the work in person. Fierce rebels sallied from Taiping Gate and attacked the tunnel directly.

sentences.zh: 別從朝陽門出數百人燒各砲台及所積蘆蒿，萬勝督隊血戰，殲百餘人，力竭死之。

translations.literal: Separately several hundred men came out from Chaoyang Gate to burn each battery and the piled reeds; Wansheng commanded his unit in bloody combat, killing more than a hundred; exhausted, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile several hundred rebels came out from Chaoyang Gate to burn the batteries and the piled reeds. Wansheng led his men in bloody fighting, killed more than a hundred of the enemy, and died when his strength gave out.

sentences.zh: 賊裂屍，竿其首於城。

translations.literal: The bandits dismembered his corpse and displayed his head on a pole on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dismembered his body and raised his head on a pole atop the wall.

sentences.zh: 鵬程，湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Pengcheng was a native of Xiangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pengcheng was a native of Xiangxiang.

sentences.zh: 先後隸羅澤南、李續賓營，累以克九江、援寶慶諸役擢副將；

translations.literal: He had successively served in the camps of Luo Zinan and Li Xubin; for repeated merit in taking Jiujiang and relieving Baoqing he was promoted to deputy brigade-general;
translations.idiomatic: He had served in turn under Luo Zinan and Li Xubin, and for repeated merit in the capture of Jiujiang and the relief of Baoqing was promoted to deputy brigade-general;

sentences.zh: 又以皖北肅清，以總兵記名簡放。

translations.literal: And for further clearing northern Anhui he was placed on the roster for appointment as brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: and for further service in clearing northern Anhui was placed on the roster for appointment as brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 紹羲，同邑人。

translations.literal: Shaoxi was from the same district.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shaoxi was from the same district.

sentences.zh: 少入湘軍，累功亦以總兵記名簡放。

translations.literal: In youth he entered the Hunan Army; for accumulated merit he too was placed on the roster for appointment as brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hunan Army while still young, and for accumulated merit was likewise placed on the roster for appointment as brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 是役也，賊以砲火轟擊，密如飛蝗，皆奮前督攻，同時歿於陣。

translations.literal: In this battle cannon and fire beat down on them thick as flying locusts; all advanced bravely to direct the assault and at the same time fell in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In that battle cannon fire fell on them thick as locusts, yet all three pressed forward to lead the assault and fell together in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 城复，以三人死綏事上聞，有詔惋惜，各賞三等輕車都尉世職，諡萬勝武烈，鵬程勇烈，紹羲剛毅。

translations.literal: When the city was recovered, report was made to the throne of the three men's deaths in faithful service at their posts; an edict expressed regret; each was granted a third-class Qing Che Duwei hereditary office; Wansheng was given the posthumous title Wulie, Pengcheng Yonglie, and Shaoxi Gangyi.
translations.idiomatic: After the city was recovered, their deaths in faithful service were reported to the throne. An edict expressed the court's grief, and each was granted a third-class hereditary Che Duwei enfeoffment. Wansheng received the posthumous title Wulie, Pengcheng Yonglie, and Shaoxi Gangyi.

sentences.zh: 王之敬，浙江奉化人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhijing was a native of Fenghua, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhijing was a native of Fenghua, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光二十九年，由水勇散目隨捕江蘇洋盜出力，拔補水師千總。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang, as a private in the water militia he followed efforts against Jiangsu pirates and distinguished himself; he was selected and appointed battalion commander in the naval force.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang, as a private in the water militia he took part in suppressing Jiangsu pirates and distinguished himself. He was selected and appointed battalion commander in the naval force.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪陷江寧，之敬管帶艇師，接戰甚勇，升守備。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, when the Cantonese rebels took Jiangning, Zhijing commanded boat forces; he engaged fiercely and was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng, when the Cantonese rebels took Jiangning, Zhijing commanded the boat squadrons, fought with great courage, and was promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，由浦口會各營連䑸勦賊，毀賊船獲勝，擢游擊。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, from Pukou he joined various camps in chaining boats to suppress bandits; he destroyed rebel vessels and won; he was promoted to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year he joined other camps at Pukou in a chained-boat operation against the rebels, destroyed enemy vessels, and won promotion to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 尋升太湖協副將。

translations.literal: Soon after he was promoted to vice commander of the Taihu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice commander of the Taihu garrison.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷江南福山鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to brigade-general of Fushan garrison in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to brigade-general of the Fushan garrison in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 適值蘇、常淪陷，太湖三面皆賊，之敬孤軍設守，屢挫賊鋒，東西兩山，賴以安堵。

translations.literal: It happened that Suzhou and Changzhou had fallen; Taihu was surrounded on three sides by bandits; Zhijing held his isolated army on the defensive; he repeatedly blunted the bandit spearhead; the Eastern and Western Hills both relied on him for peace and security.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou and Changzhou had just fallen, and Taihu was surrounded by rebels on three sides. Zhijing held his isolated force on the defensive, repeatedly blunted the rebel advance, and kept the Eastern and Western Hills secure.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，賊忽率眾圍撲東山，之敬迎戰失利，東山遂陷，之敬失所在。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year bandits suddenly led a mass to assault the Eastern Hill; Zhijing went out to meet them but was defeated; the Eastern Hill then fell; Zhijing's whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year rebels suddenly led a large force against the Eastern Hill. Zhijing met them in battle but was defeated. The Eastern Hill fell, and Zhijing disappeared.

sentences.zh: 嗣之敬之子祖培尋父屍至教場之西，見所畜犬臥土堆上，向之哀號，知有異，掘之得之敬屍，卷以席，傷痕遍體，而面目如生。

translations.literal: Later Zhijing's son Zufei searched for his father's corpse west of the drill ground; he saw the dog they kept lying on a mound of earth, howling toward it in grief; knowing something was amiss, he dug and found Zhijing's corpse; he wrapped it in a mat; wounds covered the body, yet the face looked as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhijing's son Zufei searched for his father's body west of the drill ground. The family dog lay on a mound of earth, howling at it in grief. Sensing something wrong, Zufei dug there and found Zhijing's corpse wrapped in a mat. Wounds covered the body, yet the face looked as if he were still alive.

sentences.zh: 詢居民，系於賊船退後撈獲掩埋者，不知其為總兵也。

translations.literal: Questioning residents, they learned that after the bandits' boats withdrew someone had fished it out and buried it, not knowing he was the brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: Questioning local residents, he learned that after the rebel boats withdrew someone had pulled the body from the water and buried it, never knowing he was a brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 之敬性忠勇，號能戰，至此以寡不敵眾被害，人爭惜之。

translations.literal: Zhijing was loyal and brave by nature, renowned as a fighter; here, outnumbered, he was killed; people everywhere lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing was loyal and brave by nature and famed as a fighter. Here, overwhelmed by numbers, he was killed, and men everywhere mourned him.

sentences.zh: 贈提督銜，諡果愍，建祠於太湖東西兩山。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the rank of grand coordinator; given the posthumous title Guomin; a shrine was built on the Eastern and Western Hills of Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of grand coordinator, given the posthumous title Guomin, and enshrined on the Eastern and Western Hills of Taihu.

sentences.zh: 陳忠德，字仁山，湖南清泉人。

translations.literal: Chen Zhongde, styled Renshan, was a native of Qingquan, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhongde, styled Renshan, was a native of Qingquan, Hunan.

sentences.zh: 操舟為業。

translations.literal: He made a living steering boats.
translations.idiomatic: He made his living as a boatman.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，粵賊圍長沙，掠舟北渡，遂陷賊中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, when Cantonese rebels besieged Changsha, they seized boats to cross north and he fell among the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng, when Cantonese rebels besieged Changsha, they seized boats to cross northward, and he was swept up among them.

sentences.zh: 忠德驍勇有智略，偽盡力於賊，久之，大見信任。

translations.literal: Zhongde was fierce and courageous with resource; he feigned full devotion to the rebels; over time he won great trust.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde was fierce, brave, and shrewd. He pretended to serve the rebels wholeheartedly and in time won their full trust.

sentences.zh: 十一年，道員曾國荃圍安慶，忠德自拔來歸，由是官軍始盡得賊中虛實。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Circuit Intendant Zeng Guoquan besieged Anqing; Zhongde broke free and came back to the government side; from this the government army first fully learned the true situation inside the rebel ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when Circuit Intendant Zeng Guoquan besieged Anqing, Zhongde escaped and returned to the government side. From that point the government army first learned the rebels' true condition in full.

sentences.zh: 五月，從攻菱湖兩岸賊壘平之，從克安慶及平江岸各城隘，擢千總。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he followed in attacking the rebel fortresses on both banks of Linghu and leveling them; he followed in capturing Anqing and the cities and passes on the Pingjiang bank; he was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he took part in storming and leveling the rebel fortresses on both banks of Linghu, helped capture Anqing and the cities and passes along the Pingjiang shore, and was promoted to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章援上海，選將得程學啟、郭松林于曾軍，忠德亦屬焉。

translations.literal: When Li Hongzhang relieved Shanghai, he selected generals Cheng Xueqi and Guo Songlin from Zeng's army; Zhongde was also placed under them.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang went to relieve Shanghai, he chose Cheng Xueqi and Guo Songlin from Zeng's army, and Zhongde was assigned to them as well.

sentences.zh: 從學啟破柘林、南匯、川沙、金山、青浦各城隘，擊退虹橋大股賊眾。

translations.literal: He followed Xueqi in taking Zhelin, Nanhui, Chuansha, Jinshan, Qingpu, and other cities and passes, and repelled a large body of bandits at Hongqiao.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xueqi in capturing Zhelin, Nanhui, Chuansha, Jinshan, Qingpu, and other cities and passes, and repelled a large rebel force at Hongqiao.

sentences.zh: 會克嘉定，並解北新涇、四江口之圍。

translations.literal: They then captured Jiading and likewise lifted the sieges of Beixinjing and Sijiangkou.
translations.idiomatic: They then captured Jiading and also lifted the sieges of Beixinjing and Sijiangkou.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，崑山、新陽既复，從規蘇州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, after Kunshan and Xinyang were recovered, he followed in the campaign against Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year, after Kunshan and Xinyang were recovered, he joined the campaign against Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，攻破花涇港、同里鎮，蘇州賊水陸萬餘來援，忠德力戰，負重創，卒敗之，遂收吳江、震澤。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they stormed Huajinggang and Tongli; more than ten thousand Suzhou rebels came by land and water to relieve them; Zhongde fought hard, suffered grave wounds, and at last defeated them; they then recovered Wujiang and Zhenze.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they stormed Huajinggang and Tongli. More than ten thousand Suzhou rebels came by land and water to relieve them. Zhongde fought hard, was gravely wounded, and at last routed them, after which Wujiang and Zhenze were recovered.

sentences.zh: 學啟軍益進，逼婁門外石壘，十月十九日，偽忠王李秀成、偽慕王譚紹光率萬人出婁門拒戰，學啟令忠德等擊敗之。

translations.literal: As Xueqi's army pressed forward, closing on the stone fortress outside Loud Gate; on the nineteenth day of the tenth month the false Loyal King Li Xiucheng and false Mu King Tan Shaoguang led ten thousand men out Loud Gate to resist; Xueqi ordered Zhongde and others to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: As Xueqi's army pressed forward toward the stone fortress outside Loud Gate, the rebel Loyal King Li Xiucheng and rebel Mu King Tan Shaoguang led ten thousand men out through Loud Gate on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. Xueqi ordered Zhongde and others to defeat them.

sentences.zh: 李、潭二逆走入城，石壘遂下。

translations.literal: The two rebels Li and Tan fled into the city; the stone fortress was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: Li and Tan fled into the city, and the stone fortress fell.

sentences.zh: 賊計窮，其黨郜雲官等殺譚逆以城降，蘇州复，賞勇號。

translations.literal: The bandits' stratagems were exhausted; their followers such as Gao Yunguan killed the rebel Tan and surrendered the city; Suzhou was recovered; Zhongde was rewarded with a brave-title.
translations.idiomatic: With their options exhausted, rebels such as Gao Yunguan killed Tan and surrendered the city. Suzhou was recovered, and Zhongde was rewarded with an honorific martial title.

sentences.zh: 累以功擢副將，加總兵銜。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was promoted to deputy brigade-general and given the rank of brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: For repeated merit he was promoted to deputy brigade-general and given brigade-general rank.

sentences.zh: 後以克嘉興擢總兵，隨攻湖州，中砲歿於陣，照提督例賜卹。

translations.literal: Later for capturing Jiaxing he was promoted to brigade-general; following the attack on Huzhou he was hit by cannon and died in the ranks; posthumous benefits were granted according to the precedent for grand coordinators.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for capturing Jiaxing, he was promoted to brigade-general. During the assault on Huzhou he was struck by cannon fire and died in battle. Posthumous honors were granted according to the precedent for a grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 复吳之役，死於戰者：攻青浦，為都司劉玉林、守備熊得春；

translations.literal: In the campaign to recover Wu, those who died in battle: at the assault on Qingpu, Battalion Commander Liu Yulin and Garrison Commander Xiong Dechun;
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign to recover Wu, those who died in battle included, at Qingpu, Battalion Commander Liu Yulin and Garrison Commander Xiong Dechun;

sentences.zh: 攻太倉，為參將王國安；

translations.literal: At the assault on Taicang, Colonel Wang Guoan;
translations.idiomatic: at Taicang, Colonel Wang Guoan;

sentences.zh: 攻長洲、望亭，為把總沈玉德；

translations.literal: At the assault on Changzhou and Wangting, Platoon Commander Shen Yude;
translations.idiomatic: at Changzhou and Wangting, Platoon Commander Shen Yude;

sentences.zh: 攻無錫，為游擊汪龍淦。

translations.literal: At the assault on Wuxi, Brigade Commander Wang Longgan.
translations.idiomatic: and at Wuxi, Brigade Commander Wang Longgan.

sentences.zh: 皆奮身陷陣，優恤，給世職。

translations.literal: All charged into the ranks with fervor; they received exceptional posthumous honors and hereditary offices.
translations.idiomatic: All had charged into the thick of battle. They received exceptional posthumous honors and hereditary offices.

sentences.zh: 黃金友，字益亭，湖南人。

translations.literal: Huang Jinyou, styled Yiting, was a native of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jinyou, styled Yiting, was a native of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 初從軍廣西，轉戰湖北、江西、安徽，積功至副將，賜勇號。

translations.literal: At first he followed the army in Guangxi; he campaigned in Hubei, Jiangxi, and Anhui; for accumulated merit he reached deputy brigade-general and was granted a brave-title.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service in Guangxi, then fought through Hubei, Jiangxi, and Anhui. For accumulated merit he rose to deputy brigade-general and was granted an honorific martial title.

sentences.zh: 金友躬犯矢石，創遍體。

translations.literal: Jinyou personally braved arrows and stones; wounds covered his body.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyou had repeatedly braved arrows and stones, and wounds covered his body.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，江蘇巡撫薛煥奏調駐金山衛。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng, Jiangsu Governor Xue Huan requested his transfer to garrison Jinshanwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xianfeng, Jiangsu Governor Xue Huan requested his transfer to garrison Jinshanwei.

sentences.zh: 十一年，賊犯浙江平湖，陷乍浦，東略姚廊，窺金山，金友迎戰大破之，遂平新倉賊壘，晉總兵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year bandits invaded Pinghu in Zhejiang, took Zhapu, pushed east toward Yaolang, and eyed Jinshan; Jinyou met them in battle and routed them greatly; he then pacified the rebel fortress at Xincang and was promoted to brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year rebels invaded Pinghu in Zhejiang, took Zhapu, pushed east toward Yaolang, and threatened Jinshan. Jinyou met them in battle and won a great victory, then cleared the rebel stronghold at Xincang and was promoted to brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 平湖知縣汪元祥乞師規复，金友壯之，檄金山、華亭、奉賢各營同赴援，躬督師進駐平湖之廣陳。

translations.literal: Pinghu magistrate Wang Yuanxiang begged troops to recover the county; Jinyou encouraged him, issued orders to Jinshan, Huating, and Fengxian camps to join the relief together, and personally led the army to advance and encamp at Guangchen in Pinghu.
translations.idiomatic: Pinghu magistrate Wang Yuanxiang begged for troops to recover the county. Jinyou took heart from the request, ordered the camps at Jinshan, Huating, and Fengxian to join the relief, and personally led the army to encamp at Guangchen in Pinghu.

sentences.zh: 元祥率民兵迎勞，請為鄉導，賊連營三十里，一鼓破之。

translations.literal: Yuanxiang led militia to welcome and refresh them, asked to serve as guide; rebel camps stretched thirty li; Jinyou broke them in one assault.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxiang led militia out to welcome the troops and offered to guide them. The rebel camps stretched thirty li, and Jinyou broke them in a single assault.

sentences.zh: 賊會嘉興援賊分道來襲，金友迎禦於十字街，賊大集，相持久，金友右肋被槍，猶誓死力戰，士皆奮呼，無不一當百。

translations.literal: Bandits combined with relief forces from Jiaxing and came by separate routes to attack; Jinyou met and blocked them at Shizi Street; bandits massed heavily; the contest lasted long; Jinyou was shot in the right ribs; still he swore to fight to the death; the men all shouted in ardor; every one fought as if worth a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels joined with relief forces from Jiaxing and attacked by separate routes. Jinyou met them at Shizi Street. The rebels massed heavily, and the fight dragged on. Jinyou was shot in the right ribs, yet still swore to fight to the death. His men shouted in fury, and each fought as though he were worth a hundred.

sentences.zh: 賊始卻，而金友創發不能騎，舁至明珠菴，卒。

translations.literal: The bandits at last retreated; but Jinyou's wound broke open and he could not ride; he was carried to Mingzhu Hermitage and died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels at last fell back, but Jinyou's wound reopened and he could no longer ride. He was carried to Mingzhu Hermitage, where he died.

sentences.zh: 贈提督，卹如例。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed grand coordinator; posthumous compensation according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of grand coordinator, with posthumous honors according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 麟瑞，字靄人，滿洲瓜爾佳氏，乍浦駐防。

translations.literal: Lin Rui, styled Airen, of the Gūwalgiya clan of the Manchus, was stationed at Zhapu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Rui, styled Airen, of the Gūwalgiya clan of the Manchus, was garrisoned at Zhapu.

sentences.zh: 父觀成官南川知縣，有德政，蜀人為立生祠，稱小關廟，以關、瓜音通也。

translations.literal: His father Guancheng served as magistrate of Nanchuan; he had virtuous administration; Shu people built him a living shrine, called the Little Guan Temple—the words Guan and Gua sound alike.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guancheng had served as magistrate of Nanchuan with a reputation for good governance. The people of Shu built him a living shrine called the Little Guan Temple, playing on the homophony between Guan and Gua.

sentences.zh: 麟瑞以筆帖式歷印務章京。

translations.literal: Lin Rui rose through the ranks as a clerk in the seal office to seal-office secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Rui rose from clerk in the seal office to seal-office secretary.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年，賊犯乍城，從副都統錫齡阿出督戰，偕弟鳳瑞、雲瑞手燃巨砲縱擊，賊驚卻，拔出難民無算。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng, when bandits invaded Zhapu city, he followed Vice Commander-in-Chief Xiling'a out to direct the battle; together with his younger brothers Fengrui and Yunrui he lit great guns by hand and opened fire; the bandits were startled and fell back; countless refugees were pulled out to safety.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng, when rebels attacked Zhapu, he followed Vice Commander-in-Chief Xiling'a out to direct the fighting. With his younger brothers Fengrui and Yunrui he fired the great guns by hand. The rebels fell back in alarm, and countless refugees were brought out to safety.

sentences.zh: 城陷，麟瑞率眾巷戰，力刃數賊，賊環攻，被槍，歿於陣。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Lin Rui led the crowd in street fighting, killed several bandits by blade; bandits surrounded and attacked; he was shot and died in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Lin Rui led the defenders in street fighting and killed several rebels with his blade. Surrounded and pressed from all sides, he was shot and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈副都統，予世職，祀昭忠祠，諡忠節。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed vice commander-in-chief; granted a hereditary office; enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty; given the posthumous title Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of vice commander-in-chief, given a hereditary office, enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty, and awarded the posthumous title Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 雲瑞陷賊不屈死。

translations.literal: Yunrui, captured by bandits, refused to submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yunrui was captured by the rebels, refused to submit, and died.

sentences.zh: 鳳瑞出從李鴻章軍，轉戰江、浙，攻和州、含山，以百騎計破賊萬餘，鴻章嘗稱為非常人。

translations.literal: Fengrui went out to follow Li Hongzhang's army; he campaigned in Jiangsu and Zhejiang; attacking Hezhou and Hanshan, with a hundred cavalry by stratagem he broke more than ten thousand bandits; Hongzhang once called him an extraordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Fengrui joined Li Hongzhang's army and fought through Jiangsu and Zhejiang. At Hezhou and Hanshan, with a hundred cavalry and a stratagem he routed more than ten thousand rebels. Li Hongzhang once called him a man of rare ability.

sentences.zh: 克太倉等處皆有功，贈將軍。

translations.literal: In capturing Taicang and other places he had merit; he was posthumously appointed general.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the capture of Taicang and other places and was posthumously granted the rank of general.

sentences.zh: 麟瑞督戰時，本為副都統，護印至死不釋。

translations.literal: When Lin Rui directed the battle, he was originally vice commander-in-chief; he guarded the seal of office and to his death did not release it.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Rui directed the fighting, he was already vice commander-in-chief. He guarded the official seal and never let it go, even unto death.

sentences.zh: 後其子柏梁官乍浦副都統，蒞任拜印，啟視，斑斑猶見血痕雲。

translations.literal: Later his son Bailiang served as vice commander-in-chief at Zhapu; when he arrived to assume office and received the seal, he opened it and could still see bloodstains here and there.
translations.idiomatic: Later his son Bailiang served as vice commander-in-chief at Zhapu. When he arrived to take office and received the seal, he opened it and could still see bloodstains upon it.

sentences.zh: 柏樑自有傳。

translations.literal: Bailiang has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Bailiang has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 蔡東祥，湖南湘陰人。

translations.literal: Cai Dongxiang was a native of Xiangyin, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Dongxiang was a native of Xiangyin, Hunan.

sentences.zh: 充湖北水師水勇。

translations.literal: He served in the Hubei naval force as a water militiaman.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Hubei naval force as a water militiaman.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，粵匪再陷武昌，與漢陽為犄角。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng, when Cantonese rebels again took Wuchang, it stood in paired horns with Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng, when the Cantonese rebels again took Wuchang, it and Hanyang stood in mutual support like paired horns.

sentences.zh: 東祥隨攻武漢兩岸賊，多有斬獲。

translations.literal: Dongxiang followed the assault on bandits on both banks of Wuhan and had many beheadings and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Dongxiang took part in the assault on rebels on both banks of the Wuhan stretch and won many kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 隨攻鮎魚套，焚賊船，通糧道。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Nianyutao, burned rebel boats, and opened the grain route.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the attack on Nianyutao, burned rebel boats, and reopened the grain route.

sentences.zh: 湖北提督楊載福追賊田家鎮，賊聯木簰，置砲石，於半壁山拒敵。

translations.literal: Hubei Grand Coordinator Yang Zaifu pursued bandits to Tianjiazhen; bandits linked wooden rafts, placed cannon and stones, and blocked the enemy at Banbishan.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei Grand Coordinator Yang Zaifu pursued the rebels to Tianjiazhen. The rebels linked wooden rafts, mounted cannon and stones on them, and made their stand at Banbishan.

sentences.zh: 東祥奉令以火具鎔鐵鎖斷之，水師驟下，燔賊艘無算，遂拔田家鎮。

translations.literal: Dongxiang received orders to use fire tools to melt and sever the iron chains; the naval force suddenly descended, burned countless rebel vessels, and then took Tianjiazhen.
translations.idiomatic: Dongxiang was ordered to use fire to melt through the iron chains. The fleet swept down at once, burned countless rebel vessels, and took Tianjiazhen.

sentences.zh: 於湖口、望江、九江、東流、建德、樅陽、蕪湖、銅陵諸戰皆有功，累擢至副將。

translations.literal: In battles at Hukou, Wangjiang, Jiujiang, Dongliu, Jiande, Zongyang, Wuhu, Tongling, and elsewhere he had merit; he was repeatedly promoted to deputy brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in battles at Hukou, Wangjiang, Jiujiang, Dongliu, Jiande, Zongyang, Wuhu, Tongling, and elsewhere, and was repeatedly promoted until he reached deputy brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 同治初，布政使曾國荃親率十二營與道員劉連捷分道擊江岸分踞賊，東祥分攻桐城，克雍家鎮。

translations.literal: In the early Tongzhi period, Provincial Administration Commissioner Zeng Guoquan personally led twelve battalions and, with Circuit Intendant Liu Lianjie dividing forces, struck bandits holding separate positions on the river bank; Dongxiang separately attacked Tongcheng and captured Yongjia Town.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tongzhi period, Provincial Administration Commissioner Zeng Guoquan personally led twelve battalions. With Circuit Intendant Liu Lianjie dividing the forces, they struck rebels holding separate positions along the riverbank. Dongxiang separately attacked Tongcheng and captured Yongjia Town.

sentences.zh: 又會攻巢縣、含山、和州與裕溪口、江心洲、梁山各隘，复太平、蕪湖二縣。

translations.literal: Again they jointly attacked Chaosxian, Hanshan, Hezhou, and the various passes at Yuxikou, Jiangxinzhou, and Liangshan, and recovered the two counties of Taiping and Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: They again jointly attacked Chaosxian, Hanshan, Hezhou, and the passes at Yuxikou, Jiangxinzhou, and Liangshan, and recovered Taiping and Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 陸軍進逼金柱關，兵部侍郎彭玉麟率東祥等分水師為三隊，連環轟擊，躍上堤埂，短兵擊刺，積骸滿渠。

translations.literal: The land army pressed toward Jinzhu Pass. Vice Minister of War Peng Yulin led Dongxiang and others, dividing the naval force into three squadrons. They bombarded in unbroken sequence, leaped onto the embankment, fought at close quarters with stabbing weapons, and corpses piled until the ditches were full.
translations.idiomatic: The land army pressed toward Jinzhu Pass. Vice Minister of War Peng Yulin led Dongxiang and others, dividing the fleet into three squadrons. They kept up a rolling bombardment, leaped onto the embankment, and fought hand to hand until corpses filled the ditches.

sentences.zh: 關破，並劃三汊河、上駟渡賊壘，江岸肅清。

translations.literal: When the pass fell, they also cleared rebel fortifications at Sanchahe and Shangsidu, and the riverbank was thoroughly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When the pass fell, they also cleared rebel fortifications at Sanchahe and Shangsidu, and the riverbank was fully secured.

sentences.zh: 先後賞雄勇巴圖魯等勇號，加總兵銜。

translations.literal: He was successively granted brave titles such as Xiongyong Baturu and given the rank of brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively awarded brave titles including Xiongyong Baturu and promoted to brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 東祥勇決有謀，七年湖口之戰，大風，舟入口為賊所抄，不得出。
