translations.literal: Dongxiang was bold, resolute, and resourceful. In the seventh year at the battle of Hukou, a great wind arose. Boats entering the mouth were cut off by rebels and could not get out.
translations.idiomatic: Dongxiang was bold, resolute, and shrewd. At the battle of Hukou in the seventh year, a fierce wind arose. Boats that entered the river mouth were cut off by rebels and could not escape.

sentences.zh: 所領長龍艦一，偃旗與賊艦混，須臾風止，急槳貫賊陣出，賊覺，追之不及。

translations.literal: The single long-dragon ship under his command lowered its banners and blended among rebel vessels. In a moment the wind stopped; he rowed furiously and pierced through the rebel formation to escape. The rebels noticed but could not catch him.
translations.idiomatic: The lone long-dragon ship under his command lowered its banners and mingled with rebel vessels. When the wind suddenly dropped, he rowed hard and drove straight through the rebel line. The rebels noticed too late and could not overtake him.

sentences.zh: 是役失長龍艦五、舢板十三，將弁死者二十一人，而東祥舟獨完。

translations.literal: In that battle five long-dragon ships and thirteen sampans were lost, and twenty-one officers and commanders died, yet Dongxiang's vessel alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: In that battle five long-dragon ships and thirteen sampans were lost, and twenty-one officers died, yet Dongxiang's ship alone came through unscathed.

sentences.zh: 十一年安慶之戰，水師屢挫，賊易視之，見輒爭擊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year at the battle of Anqing, the naval force suffered repeated setbacks, and the rebels came to hold them in contempt, rushing to attack whenever they appeared.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Anqing in the eleventh year, the fleet had suffered repeated defeats, and the rebels had learned to despise it, rushing to attack at every sighting.

sentences.zh: 東祥請易戰艦白旗為紅旗，賊疑為援兵，駭愕間，急率所部乘之，賊以敗，軍威復振。

translations.literal: Dongxiang requested that the battle ships change their white banners to red. The rebels, suspecting reinforcements, were stunned. He swiftly led his unit to press the advantage; the rebels were defeated and army prestige revived.
translations.idiomatic: Dongxiang had the warships swap their white banners for red. The rebels, mistaking them for fresh reinforcements, were thrown into confusion. He swiftly led his men to exploit the moment, routed the enemy, and restored the army's prestige.

sentences.zh: 旋調江蘇勦賊，偕副將歐陽利見，率淮陽水師，巡防三江口，戰嘉善。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to suppress rebels in Jiangsu. Together with Deputy Brigadier-General Ouyang Lijian, he led the Huaiyang naval force to patrol and guard Sanjiangkou, and fought at Jiashan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Jiangsu to suppress rebels. With Deputy Brigadier-General Ouyang Lijian he led the Huaiyang fleet to patrol Sanjiangkou and fought at Jiashan.

sentences.zh: 奮勇駛進西塘，援賊猝至，兩岸夾攻，被槍子傷，落水死。

translations.literal: He drove forward valiantly into Xitang. Rebel reinforcements arrived suddenly and attacked from both banks. He was wounded by a musket ball, fell into the water, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He drove boldly into Xitang, but rebel reinforcements arrived without warning and attacked from both banks. Struck by a musket ball, he fell into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 東祥轉戰克敵，素稱勇敢，照總兵例議卹，贈提督銜，給世職。

translations.literal: Dongxiang had fought in many battles and defeated the enemy, and was long renowned for valor. Posthumous honors were deliberated according to the brigade-general precedent; he was given the posthumous rank of regional commander and granted a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: Dongxiang had fought across many campaigns and was long famed for courage. Posthumous honors were granted according to the brigade-general precedent: he was given the posthumous rank of regional commander and a hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 鄒上元，字蘭亭，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Zou Shangyuan, styled Lanting, was a native of Xiangxiang, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Shangyuan, styled Lanting, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，投羅澤南營，澤南自江西援湖北，取道崇陽、通城，進攻佛嶺賊卡。

translations.literal: In the early Xianfeng period he joined Luo Zinan's camp. Zinan marched from Jiangxi to aid Hubei, taking the route through Chongyang and Tongcheng to attack the rebel stockade at Foling.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xianfeng era he entered Luo Zinan's camp. Zinan marched from Jiangxi to relieve Hubei, passing through Chongyang and Tongcheng to attack the rebel stockade at Foling.

sentences.zh: 上元隨隊由佛嶺北攀岩先進，與諸軍夾擊，破之。

translations.literal: Shangyuan followed the column, climbed the cliffs north of Foling ahead of the rest, and with the other armies attacked from both sides, breaking the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyuan followed the column, scaled the cliffs north of Foling ahead of the others, and with the rest of the army struck from both sides until the position fell.

sentences.zh: 賊自崇陽三路來攻，上元從破右路，克崇陽、咸寧諸役均有功，擢千總。

translations.literal: Rebels attacked from Chongyang in three columns. Shangyuan helped break the right column. He earned credit in the captures of Chongyang, Xianning, and other operations, and was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels attacked from Chongyang in three columns, Shangyuan helped break the right flank. He distinguished himself in the captures of Chongyang, Xianning, and other engagements, and was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 五年，賊犯湖南，巡撫駱秉章檄蕭啟江募勇助剿，號湘果營，上元隸焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year rebels invaded Hunan. Governor Luo Bingzhang ordered Xiao Qijiang to raise militia to assist in suppression, forming the camp called Xiangguo. Shangyuan served under it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when rebels invaded Hunan, Governor Luo Bingzhang ordered Xiao Qijiang to raise militia for the campaign. The unit was called the Xiangguo Camp, and Shangyuan served in it.

sentences.zh: 從援江西，克萬載，复袁州，果擢都司。

translations.literal: He followed the relief of Jiangxi, captured Wanzai, recovered Yuanzhou, and was accordingly promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the relief of Jiangxi, captured Wanzai, recovered Yuanzhou, and was promoted to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 秉章督蜀，檄黃純熙率果毅營從，上元方假歸，純熙招偕行，充營官。

translations.literal: When Bingzhang went to supervise Sichuan, he ordered Huang Chunxi to lead the Guoyi Camp to follow. Shangyuan was on leave at home; Chunxi recruited him to go together, and he served as camp officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingzhang went to supervise Sichuan, he ordered Huang Chunxi to lead the Guoyi Camp after him. Shangyuan was then at home on leave; Chunxi recruited him to come along, and he served as camp officer.

sentences.zh: 賊酋何國樑、彭紹福率黨攻定遠急，定遠東北瀕江，賊屯東南，造浮橋江上遏外援。

translations.literal: Rebel chiefs He Guoliang and Peng Shaofu led their bands in a pressing assault on Dingyuan. Dingyuan lay northeast by the river. The rebels encamped in the southeast and built a pontoon bridge on the river to block outside relief.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chiefs He Guoliang and Peng Shaofu led their followers in a fierce assault on Dingyuan. The city stood in the northeast by the river, while the rebels encamped to the southeast and built a pontoon bridge across the water to cut off outside relief.

sentences.zh: 上元從純熙疾赴，師至興學場，賊分黨逆戰。

translations.literal: Shangyuan followed Chunxi in hurrying there. When the army reached Xingxuechang, the rebels divided their band to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyuan hurried there with Chunxi. When the army reached Xingxuechang, the rebels split their force and met them in battle.

sentences.zh: 上元從右路襲擊，賊大奔，乘勝追至祖師殿，毀沿途二十餘壘，蹙賊江乾，何國樑鳧水遁，上元追斬之。

translations.literal: Shangyuan struck from the right flank. The rebels fled in disorder. Pressing the victory, they pursued to Zushidian, destroyed more than twenty fortifications along the way, and drove the rebels to the riverbank. He Guoliang swam away across the water. Shangyuan pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyuan struck from the right flank and the rebels broke and ran. Pursuing the victory to Zushidian, they destroyed more than twenty fortifications along the way and cornered the enemy at the riverbank. He Guoliang swam away, but Shangyuan overtook him and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 彭紹福聞敗，糾黨來援，踞燕子窩、二郎場等處。

translations.literal: When Peng Shaofu heard of the defeat, he gathered his band to reinforce and occupied Yanzowo, Erlangchang, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Shaofu heard of the defeat, he rallied his followers and seized Yanzowo, Erlangchang, and other positions.

sentences.zh: 二郎場者絕地也，四山壁立，鳥道一線，西北阻涪江，純熙恐失寇，不待軍集，率千人追之。

translations.literal: Erlangchang was a dead-end place: sheer cliffs on all four sides, a single thread of a bird path, the Fuling River blocking the northwest. Chunxi, fearing the rebels would escape, did not wait for the army to gather and led a thousand men in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Erlangchang was a trap of a place—cliffs on every side, a single narrow track, and the Fuling River blocking the northwest. Chunxi, fearing the rebels would slip away, did not wait for the full army to assemble and led a thousand men in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 上元慮有伏，進至距二郎場二十里，遣諜偵之，不見賊，土人皆言賊去遠。

translations.literal: Shangyuan feared an ambush. When they had advanced to within twenty li of Erlangchang, he sent spies to reconnoiter. No rebels were seen, and local people all said the rebels had gone far away.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyuan feared an ambush. When they were still twenty li from Erlangchang, he sent scouts ahead but found no rebels; the locals all said the enemy had fled far off.

sentences.zh: 夜半，至燕子窩，突遇賊騎，進逼之，賊繞山竄入場，純熙知中伏，分道搜之，伏盡發。

translations.literal: At midnight they reached Yanzowo and suddenly encountered rebel cavalry. Pressing forward, they drove the rebels around the mountain into the field. Chunxi knew they had fallen into an ambush and divided his forces to search them out. All the hidden troops sprang forth.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight they reached Yanzowo and suddenly ran into rebel cavalry. As they pressed the attack, the rebels slipped around the mountain into the field. Chunxi realized they had walked into an ambush and split his force to search the ground—and every hidden unit sprang up at once.

sentences.zh: 官軍偪處泥淖間，不能成列，上元馳救，突圍入，手刃數賊，賊環刺之，死，純熙亦歿。

translations.literal: Government troops were pressed in the mud and mire and could not form ranks. Shangyuan raced to their rescue, broke through the encirclement, and personally killed several rebels. The rebels surrounded him and stabbed him to death. Chunxi also perished.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops were trapped in mud and could not hold formation. Shangyuan galloped to their aid, broke through the encirclement, and killed several rebels with his own hand. The rebels closed around him and stabbed him to death. Chunxi also fell.

sentences.zh: 定遠之捷，上元擢參將。

translations.literal: For the victory at Dingyuan, Shangyuan was promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: For the victory at Dingyuan, Shangyuan was promoted to colonel.

sentences.zh: 死事聞，命視副將例，賞世職，附祀純熙祠。

translations.literal: When news of his death in service reached the court, he was ordered to be honored according to the deputy brigadier-general precedent, granted a hereditary office, and enshrined jointly in Chunxi's memorial hall.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death in battle reached the court, he was honored according to the deputy brigadier-general precedent, granted a hereditary office, and given a place in Chunxi's memorial hall.

sentences.zh: 郝上庠，直隸沙河人。

translations.literal: Hao Shangxiang was a native of Shahe, Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Shangxiang was a native of Shahe in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 由武進士授侍衛。

translations.literal: Having passed the military palace examination, he was appointed an imperial bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the military palace examination, he was appointed an imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 道光二十六年，出為山東曹州鎮標守備，累遷至武定游擊。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Daoguang he left the capital to serve as garrison commandant of the Caozhou garrison in Shandong, and was promoted in succession to battalion commander of Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Daoguang he left the capital to serve as garrison commandant of the Caozhou garrison in Shandong, and rose in succession to battalion commander of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，韓莊盜起，山東巡撫張亮基慮徐州道梗，知上庠饒將略，薦署兗州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng, bandits rose at Hanzhuang. Shandong Governor Zhang Liangji feared the route to Xuzhou would be blocked. Knowing Shangxiang was skilled in military strategy, he recommended him to serve as acting brigade-general of the Yanzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng, bandits rose at Hanzhuang. Shandong Governor Zhang Liangji feared the road to Xuzhou would be cut, and knowing Shangxiang's skill in command, recommended him to serve as acting brigade-general of the Yanzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 賊帥硃廣田寇郯、蘭、沂、莒諸屬，上庠率所部會鄉兵擊走之。

translations.literal: Rebel chief Zhu Guangtian raided the districts of Tan, Lan, Yi, and Ju. Shangxiang led his troops together with local militia and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chief Zhu Guangtian raided Tan, Lan, Yi, Ju, and neighboring districts. Shangxiang led his troops with local militia and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 賊南竄贛榆，上庠追及，殲其眾，斬廣田於陣，擢參將。

translations.literal: The rebels fled south to Ganyu. Shangxiang overtook them, annihilated their force, and slew Guangtian in battle. He was promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled south to Ganyu. Shangxiang caught up with them, wiped out their force, and killed Guangtian in battle. He was promoted to colonel.

sentences.zh: 五年，山東金鄉賊陶三相為亂，上庠疾馳誅其渠，餘眾驚潰，事得解。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, bandits led by Tao San in Jinxiang, Shandong, rose in rebellion. Shangxiang rushed there, executed their ringleader, and the rest scattered in panic. The affair was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Tao San and his band rose in rebellion at Jinxiang in Shandong. Shangxiang rushed there, executed their leader, and the rest fled in panic. The crisis was ended.

sentences.zh: 時海上多盜，連舟窺諸口，將北犯天津洋。

translations.literal: At the time pirates were numerous at sea. They linked boats and lurked at various ports, intending to invade the waters north toward Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: At the time pirates swarmed the coast. They linked their boats and prowled the harbors, preparing to raid north toward the waters off Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 山東巡撫崇恩疏請以上庠攝登州鎮總兵，專司防務。

translations.literal: Shandong Governor Chong'en memorialized requesting that Shangxiang act as brigade-general of the Dengzhou garrison, with sole charge of coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong Governor Chong'en memorialized the throne to appoint Shangxiang acting brigade-general of the Dengzhou garrison with sole charge of coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 往來策應，先後擒斬賊首李希夢等，以功敘沂州協副將。

translations.literal: Moving back and forth in mutual support, he successively captured and beheaded pirate leaders including Li Ximeng. For his merit he was given the rank of deputy brigade-general of the Yizhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Moving back and forth in support of other commands, he captured and beheaded pirate leaders including Li Ximeng. For his service he was promoted to deputy brigade-general of the Yizhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 上庠每戰，輒身先士卒，不避艱險，以勇武受上知。

translations.literal: In every battle Shangxiang took the lead ahead of his soldiers and did not shun danger. For his courage and martial prowess he won the court's notice.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle Shangxiang led from the front and never shrank from danger. His courage and martial skill won him the court's favor.

sentences.zh: 賊平，手詔褒美，命以總兵記名。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, the emperor's own edict praised him and ordered his name registered for brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified, the emperor issued a personal edict praising him and ordered his name registered for promotion to brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 十年，署曹州鎮總兵，以疏防捻寇入境，奪記名，留鎮如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he acted as brigade-general of the Caozhou garrison. For lax defense that allowed Nian bandits to enter the province, his registered name was revoked, but he remained at his post as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he served as acting brigade-general of the Caozhou garrison. Because lax defense had allowed Nian bandits to cross the border, his registered promotion was revoked, though he remained at his post.

sentences.zh: 十一年，官軍取濮州，河北肅清。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year government troops took Puzhou and the Hebei region was thoroughly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year government troops captured Puzhou and the Hebei region was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 上庠以屢勝功复官，賜提督銜。

translations.literal: Shangxiang, for repeated victories, had his office restored and was granted the rank of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: For a string of victories Shangxiang had his office restored and was granted the rank of regional commander.

sentences.zh: 九月，賊潛渡濮、範，上庠不能禦，與賊遇陽穀，又戰不利，為山東巡撫譚廷襄所劾，落職。

translations.literal: In the ninth month rebels secretly crossed at Pu and Fan. Shangxiang could not stop them. He met the rebels at Yanggu and again fought without success. Shandong Governor Tan Tingxiang impeached him, and he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month rebels secretly crossed the border at Pu and Fan. Shangxiang failed to stop them, met the enemy at Yanggu, and was defeated again. Shandong Governor Tan Tingxiang impeached him, and he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 十月，克張秋鎮，移兵會營總烏爾棍扎布、游擊緒倫攻堂邑賊，戰於丁家廟，敗之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he captured Zhangqiu Town, moved his troops to join Banner Commander Wuerken Zhabu and Battalion Commander Xulun in attacking rebels at Tangyi, fought at Dingjiamiao, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he captured Zhangqiu Town, then moved his troops to join Banner Commander Wuerken Zhabu and Battalion Commander Xulun in an attack on rebels at Tangyi. They fought at Dingjiamiao and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊益眾來援，上庠奮擊不退，馬蹶墮地，拔刀殺賊數十人，力竭，戰死。

translations.literal: More rebels came in force to reinforce. Shangxiang fought fiercely and would not retreat. His horse stumbled and he fell to the ground. Drawing his sword he killed dozens of rebels. His strength exhausted, he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel reinforcements arrived in greater numbers. Shangxiang fought on without yielding until his horse stumbled and threw him. He drew his sword and killed dozens of rebels before his strength gave out and he fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 命優恤，諡勤勇。

translations.literal: The court ordered exceptional posthumous honors and granted the posthumous title Qinyong.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered exceptional posthumous honors and granted him the posthumous title Qinyong, Diligent and Brave.

sentences.zh: 聊城士民念上庠捍賊功，請立祠東昌，從之。

translations.literal: The gentry and people of Liaocheng, remembering Shangxiang's merit in defending against rebels, requested a memorial hall be erected at Dongchang. The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and people of Liaocheng, remembering his service in holding off the rebels, petitioned for a memorial hall at Dongchang, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 張遇祥，字瑞麟，直隸新樂人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuxiang, styled Ruilin, was a native of Xinle, Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuxiang, styled Ruilin, was a native of Xinle in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 年十五，能開兩石弓。

translations.literal: At fifteen he could draw a two-stone bow.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he could draw a two-stone bow.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年，成武進士，授乾清門侍衛。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the military palace examination and was appointed a bodyguard of the Qianqing Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the military palace examination and was appointed a bodyguard of the Qianqing Gate.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，選浙江衢州城守營都司，公廉能得士卒心。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was selected as battalion commander of the Quzhou garrison in Zhejiang. Upright and incorruptible, he won the hearts of his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was appointed battalion commander of the Quzhou garrison in Zhejiang. Upright and fair, he won the loyalty of his men.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，在壽張游擊任，匪林鳳祥、李開芳率粵匪圍懷慶，山東巡撫李僡檄遇祥從征當一路，為士卒先，所向披靡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, while serving as battalion commander of Shouzhang, bandits Lin Fengxiang and Li Kaifang led Cantonese rebels to besiege Huaiqing. Shandong Governor Li Han ordered Yuxiang to join the campaign and hold one route. He went ahead of his soldiers and swept all before him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng, while serving as battalion commander of Shouzhang, Lin Fengxiang and Li Kaifang led Cantonese rebels to besiege Huaiqing. Shandong Governor Li Han ordered Yuxiang to join the campaign on one route. He always went ahead of his men and swept all before him.

sentences.zh: 經略勝保嘉其勇，益感奮。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Sheng Bao praised his valor, and he fought with redoubled zeal.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Sheng Bao praised his courage, and he fought with renewed fervor.

sentences.zh: 嘗夤夜渡河戰，自寅至申，始奉令而返。

translations.literal: Once he crossed the river to fight in the dead of night, from the yin hour to the shen hour, before he received orders to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Once he crossed the river to fight through the night, from dawn until late afternoon, before he received orders to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，曹縣捻匪亂起，攜親兵百人入城，捻首陳九千歲、張四大王擁眾擾城市，無敢攖者。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year, Nian bandits rose in disorder in Caoxian. He entered the city with a hundred personal troops. Nian leaders Chen Jiuqiansui and Zhang Sidawang led mobs to harass the city, and no one dared confront them.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year, Nian bandits rose in revolt at Caoxian. He entered the city with a hundred personal troops while Nian leaders Chen Jiuqiansui and Zhang Sidawang led mobs to terrorize the town, and no one dared stand against them.

sentences.zh: 遇祥密令伏兵於外，變服入賊巢，詐言他事，賊優禮之。

translations.literal: Yuxiang secretly ordered ambush troops outside, changed clothes, entered the rebel nest, and pretended other business. The rebels treated him with honor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxiang secretly posted ambush troops outside, changed clothes, and entered the rebel stronghold on a pretext. The rebels received him courteously.

sentences.zh: 夜分，酒酣，遇祥驟起蹴賊，首腦迸裂死，賊群起，且戰且走，出巢伏起，賊皆駭散。

translations.literal: At midnight, when wine had gone deep, Yuxiang suddenly rose and kicked a rebel; his skull burst and he died. The rebels surged up. Fighting as they went, they left the nest; the ambush rose and the rebels all scattered in terror.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in the night, when the wine was flowing freely, Yuxiang suddenly rose and kicked a rebel leader, shattering his skull. The bandits surged up; fighting as they fled, they ran into the ambush outside and scattered in terror.

sentences.zh: 又偵知張四大王所在，託病不出，密令親信軍士夜馳百餘裡入賊室擒之。

translations.literal: He also learned where Zhang Sidawang was. Feigning illness and staying indoors, he secretly ordered trusted soldiers to ride through the night more than a hundred li into the rebel's quarters and seize him.
translations.idiomatic: He also learned where Zhang Sidawang was hiding. Feigning illness and staying indoors, he secretly ordered trusted soldiers to ride through the night more than a hundred li and seize the rebel leader in his own quarters.

sentences.zh: 粵匪攻臨清，率部卒二百人，夜砍賊營而入，殺無算。

translations.literal: When Cantonese rebels attacked Linqing, he led two hundred of his troops, cut their way into the rebel camp by night, and killed beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: When Cantonese rebels attacked Linqing, he led two hundred of his men, cut their way into the rebel camp by night, and slaughtered the enemy without number.

sentences.zh: 所部五十餘人被圍，复匹馬盪決者三，攜之出，無一失者。

translations.literal: When more than fifty of his men were surrounded, he three times charged through on a single horse alone, brought them out, and not one was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When more than fifty of his men were surrounded, he three times charged through alone on horseback and brought them all out without losing a single man.

sentences.zh: 右腿受矛傷，裹傷屢戰，賊不敢當。

translations.literal: His right leg was wounded by a spear. He bandaged the wound and fought again and again; the rebels dared not face him.
translations.idiomatic: His right leg was pierced by a spear. He bound the wound and kept fighting; the rebels dared not stand against him.

sentences.zh: 創劇不能起，巡撫親驗之，諭令歸養，新撫崇恩疑規避，奏參褫職，令解赴山東。

translations.literal: His wounds were severe and he could not rise. The governor personally examined him and ordered him to return home to recuperate. The new governor Chong'en suspected evasion, memorialized against him, stripped him of office, and ordered him escorted to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: His wounds were so severe that he could not rise. The governor personally examined him and ordered him home to recover. The new governor Chong'en suspected he was shirking duty, memorialized against him, stripped him of office, and ordered him escorted to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 既到標，崇恩始知其誣，慰勞備至。

translations.literal: When he reached headquarters, Chong'en finally learned he had been wrongly accused and comforted him with every courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached headquarters, Chong'en learned he had been wrongly accused and treated him with every mark of honor and comfort.

sentences.zh: 時金鄉、魚台、嘉祥、費縣、鉅野、鄆城、城武七縣被捻匪所陷，遇祥招舊部六百人，自為一隊，复七城，餘孽悉平。

translations.literal: At that time Jinxiang, Yutai, Jiaxiang, Feixian, Juye, Yuncheng, and Chengwo—seven counties—had fallen to Nian bandits. Yuxiang recruited six hundred of his former troops, formed his own detachment, recovered the seven cities, and all remaining bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: At that time seven counties—Jinxiang, Yutai, Jiaxiang, Feixian, Juye, Yuncheng, and Chengwo—had fallen to Nian bandits. Yuxiang raised six hundred of his old troops, formed an independent detachment, recovered all seven cities, and wiped out the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 復原官，以創發回籍調養。

translations.literal: His original office was restored. Because his old wounds reopened, he returned to his native place to recuperate.
translations.idiomatic: His original office was restored, but when his old wounds reopened he returned to his native place to recover.

sentences.zh: 十一年，山東教匪糾回、捻北犯直隸，勝保久無功，乃肅書聘遇祥，且令募勇自隨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Shandong sect rebels allied with Hui and Nian forces and invaded Zhili northward. Sheng Bao had long been without success and so wrote a formal letter inviting Yuxiang and ordered him to raise militia to bring with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Shandong sect rebels joined with Hui and Nian forces and invaded Zhili from the north. Sheng Bao, long without success, wrote a formal letter inviting Yuxiang and ordered him to raise militia to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 書至，即招募鄉中子弟五百人，星馳而往，一戰敗之。

translations.literal: When the letter arrived, he immediately recruited five hundred local youths, rushed there by forced marches, and defeated the enemy in the first battle.
translations.idiomatic: The moment the letter arrived, he recruited five hundred local youths, marched at forced pace, and routed the enemy in the first engagement.

sentences.zh: 勝保南移館陶，進次尖莊，賊麕集尖莊南，遇祥复馳救，賊奔。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao moved south to Guantao and advanced to Jianzhuang. Rebels massed south of Jianzhuang. Yuxiang again raced to the rescue and the rebels fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao moved south to Guantao and advanced to Jianzhuang. Rebels massed south of the town. Yuxiang again rushed to the rescue and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 民爭奉糗餌漿粥，軍得一飽，督隊回尖莊。

translations.literal: The people competed to offer rations, porridge, and gruel. The army had one full meal, and he led his column back to Jianzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The people vied to bring rations, porridge, and gruel. The army ate its fill, and he led his column back to Jianzhuang.

sentences.zh: 勝保又退守館陶，遇祥趨謁之。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao again fell back to defend Guantao. Yuxiang hurried to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao again fell back to defend Guantao, and Yuxiang hurried to report to him.

sentences.zh: 賊又欲渡河，勝保令往堵河口，遇祥曰：「士卒昨日一飯後，枵腹至今，烏能戰耶？

translations.literal: The rebels again intended to cross the river. Sheng Bao ordered him to go block the river mouth. Yuxiang said: "Since one meal yesterday, the soldiers' bellies have been empty until now. How can they fight?"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels again tried to cross the river. Sheng Bao ordered him to block the river mouth. Yuxiang said, "Since one meal yesterday the men have gone hungry until now. How can they fight?"

sentences.zh: 」勝保曰：「汝速往！

translations.literal: Sheng Bao said: "Go quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao said, "Go at once!"

sentences.zh: 吾即遣人執釜甑從汝也。

translations.literal: I will immediately send men carrying pots and steamers to follow you."
translations.idiomatic: I will send men with cooking pots and steamers right after you."

sentences.zh: 」遂率隊趨大河，士卒覓食不得，賊已先渡，遇祥匹馬陷賊陣，戰至日暮，下馬而搏。

translations.literal: So he led his column toward the great river. The soldiers could find no food. The rebels had already crossed first. Yuxiang alone on horseback plunged into the rebel formation. They fought until dusk, then he dismounted to grapple hand to hand.
translations.idiomatic: So he led his column toward the great river. His men could find nothing to eat. The rebels had already crossed first. Yuxiang alone on horseback plunged into the enemy line and fought until dusk, then dismounted to grapple hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 天明，回顧所部餘數十人，急揮之去，曰：「同死無益。

translations.literal: At daybreak he looked back and saw only a few dozen of his troops remaining. He urgently waved them away and said: "Dying together serves no purpose."
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he looked back and saw only a few dozen men still with him. He urgently waved them away and said, "Dying together serves no purpose."

sentences.zh: 吾身經數​​百戰，未曾一挫，今勢至此，不斬賊渠，不生還也！

translations.literal: I have fought several hundred battles and never once been defeated. Now that matters have come to this, unless I cut down the rebel chief, I will not return alive!"
translations.idiomatic: I have fought hundreds of battles and never once been beaten. Now that things have come to this, unless I cut down the rebel chief, I will not return alive!"

sentences.zh: 」縱馬示不返，士卒益感奮，誓同死，遇祥左右射，當者皆殪。

translations.literal: He spurred his horse to show he would not return. The soldiers were all the more stirred and swore to die with him. Yuxiang shot left and right; all who faced him fell.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred his horse to show he would not turn back. His men were all the more stirred and swore to die with him. Yuxiang shot left and right, and every man who faced him fell.

sentences.zh: 賊以長戟鉤斷其弦，乃舍弓提刀戰，至下堡寺，日近山，從者餘六人，忽見大纛下賊渠至，將聳身刃之，時已戰兩晝夜，飢甚，舊傷皆發，復中矛數十處，力既竭，遂歿於陣，時咸豐十一年十一月七日。

translations.literal: Rebels used long halberds to hook and break his bowstring. He then cast aside his bow, took up his saber, and fought on to Xiabao Temple. As the sun neared the mountains, only six followers remained. Suddenly he saw the rebel chief arrive beneath a great banner. He was about to spring up and cut him down. By then he had fought for two days and two nights, was famished, and all his old wounds had reopened. He was again struck by spears in dozens of places. His strength exhausted, he died in battle. It was the seventh day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Xianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels hooked his bowstring with long halberds and snapped it. He cast aside the bow, drew his saber, and fought on to Xiabao Temple. As the sun sank toward the mountains, only six men still followed him. Suddenly he saw the rebel chief arrive beneath a great banner and was about to spring forward and cut him down. By then he had fought for two days and two nights without rest, was starving, and every old wound had reopened. He was pierced by spears dozens of times more, and when his strength was spent he fell on the field. It was the seventh day of the eleventh month in the eleventh year of Xianfeng.

sentences.zh: 館陶、臨清諸村堡，爭建祠以祀。

translations.literal: Villages and forts around Guantao and Linqing all competed to erect memorial halls in his honor.
translations.idiomatic: Villages and forts around Guantao and Linqing all vied to erect memorial halls in his honor.

sentences.zh: 兄遇清，字芳辰。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yuqing, styled Fangchen.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yuqing, styled Fangchen.

sentences.zh: 武舉人。

translations.literal: A passed candidate of the military provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He had passed the military provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 官廣東，洊擢至督標參將，檄援廣西平南縣，提刀巷戰，賊槍刺其腹，腸出，益奮。

translations.literal: He served in Guangdong and was repeatedly promoted to colonel under the governor-general's banner. Ordered to reinforce Pingnan County in Guangxi, he fought in the alleys with drawn saber. A rebel speared his belly with a gun; his intestines spilled out, and he fought all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Guangdong and rose repeatedly to colonel under the governor-general's banner. Ordered to reinforce Pingnan County in Guangxi, he fought through the alleys with saber drawn. A rebel shot him in the belly; his intestines spilled out, and he fought all the harder.

sentences.zh: 賊折其刀，手執木棍抵拒，賊攢擊，死之。

translations.literal: The rebels broke his saber. He took a wooden club in hand to resist. The rebels closed in and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke his saber. He seized a wooden club and fought on until they closed in and killed him.

sentences.zh: 平南士民亦立祠以祀。

translations.literal: The gentry and people of Pingnan also erected a memorial hall in his honor.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and people of Pingnan also erected a memorial hall in his honor.

sentences.zh: 曹仁美，字擇庵，湘潭人。

translations.literal: Cao Renmei, styled Ze'an, was a native of Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Renmei, styled Ze'an, was a native of Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 初隸曾國荃軍，援江西，戰吉安天華山，克之。

translations.literal: At first he served under Zeng Guoquan's army, reinforced Jiangxi, fought at Tianhuashan in Ji'an, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served under Zeng Guoquan, joined the relief of Jiangxi, fought at Tianhuashan in Ji'an, and captured the position.

sentences.zh: 复景德鎮、浮梁，與有功。

translations.literal: He recovered Jingdezhen and Fuliang and shared in the merit.
translations.idiomatic: He helped recover Jingdezhen and Fuliang and shared in the credit.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，賊據黟縣、建德，勢張甚，時仁美改隸曾國籓麾下，官軍屢戰不利，堅壘與持。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng rebels held Yixian and Jiande and their power swelled greatly. By then Renmei had transferred to serve under Zeng Guofan. Government troops repeatedly fought without success and held fortified camps in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xianfeng rebels held Yixian and Jiande and their strength grew formidable. By then Renmei had transferred to Zeng Guofan's command. Government troops fought repeatedly without success and settled into a stalemate behind fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 仁美曰：「兩軍相持日久，當乘其懈而擊之，否則援至難圖也。

translations.literal: Renmei said: "The two armies have faced each other for a long time. We should strike while they are slack; otherwise, when reinforcements arrive it will be hard to overcome them."
translations.idiomatic: Renmei said, "The two armies have been locked in stalemate for too long. We should strike while they slacken; otherwise, once reinforcements arrive we will never overcome them."

sentences.zh: 」會夜大霧，仁美率所部摩其壘，更籌寂然，乃梯而入，手刃司柝者，縱火焚之。

translations.literal: Just then a great fog fell at night. Renmei led his unit up to their fortifications. The watch drums were silent. He entered by ladder, personally killed the watchman, and set fire to burn it.
translations.idiomatic: That night a heavy fog descended. Renmei led his men up to the enemy fortifications. The watch drums were silent. He climbed in by ladder, killed the watchman with his own hand, and set the camp ablaze.

sentences.zh: 眾軍為承，斬數千級，賊大潰，遂克之，獲器械無數。

translations.literal: The rest of the army followed up. They beheaded several thousand and the rebels fled in great disorder. The place was taken and countless weapons were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the army followed up, beheaded several thousand rebels, and routed the enemy completely. The position fell, and they captured weapons beyond count.

sentences.zh: 遷都司，賜號勵勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to battalion commander and granted the title Liyong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to battalion commander and granted the title Liyong Baturu.

sentences.zh: 十一年，國荃攻安慶，久不下，國籓遣仁美往助，偽英王陳玉成合江、淮賊來援，國荃督戰，中流矢，仁美負之登高，揮諸軍奮擊，城遂下。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Guoquan besieged Anqing but could not take it for a long time. Guofan sent Renmei to assist. The False Prince Chen Yucheng united Jianghuai rebels to relieve the city. Guoquan directed the battle and was struck by an arrow. Renmei carried him up to high ground, rallied the armies to strike fiercely, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Guoquan besieged Anqing but could not take it for a long time. Guofan sent Renmei to assist. The False Prince Chen Yucheng united Jianghuai rebels to relieve the city. Guoquan directed the battle and was struck by an arrow. Renmei carried him to higher ground, rallied the armies to strike hard, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 以次從克大江兩岸城隘。

translations.literal: In sequence he followed in capturing fortifications and cities on both banks of the great river.
translations.idiomatic: In turn he took part in capturing fortifications and cities on both banks of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從圍金陵，仁美屯雨花台西，國荃以城賊糧將匱，為坐困計，令諸軍毋與戰，凡四十有六日。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he joined the siege of Jinling. Renmei encamped west of Yuhuatai. Guoquan reckoned the city's rebels would soon run short of grain and planned to wear them down, ordering the armies not to fight—for forty-six days in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he joined the siege of Jinling. Renmei encamped west of Yuhuatai. Guoquan reckoned the rebels in the city would soon run short of grain and ordered a strategy of attrition, forbidding the armies to engage—for forty-six days in all.

sentences.zh: 仁美恚曰：「當賊不擊，將何待？

translations.literal: Renmei said in anger: "When the enemy is before us and we do not strike, what are we waiting for?"
translations.idiomatic: Renmei said in anger, "With the enemy before us and we do not strike—what are we waiting for?"

sentences.zh: 」乃以其軍出毀石壘，賊頗死。

translations.literal: So he led his army out and destroyed stone fortifications. Many rebels died.
translations.idiomatic: So he led his army out and destroyed the stone fortifications, killing many rebels.

sentences.zh: 國荃以其勇，薄責之，遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: Guoquan, because of his valor, lightly reprimanded him, and he then pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan, though displeased, reprimanded him only lightly because of his courage, whereupon Renmei pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 投入李鴻章軍，圍攻常州，鴻章檄劉銘傳等偏師直搗，仁美率眾繼進，大破之。

translations.literal: He joined Li Hongzhang's army; they besieged Changzhou; Hongzhang ordered Liu Mingchuan and others with a detached column to strike straight at the enemy; Renmei led the troops in follow-up advance; they routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Li Hongzhang's army and took part in the siege of Changzhou. Hongzhang sent Liu Mingchuan and a detached column to strike at the enemy directly, and Renmei advanced in support with his men and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 三年，克金陵，餘賊突出​​鏖戰，湘、淮諸軍屢挫於奔牛。

translations.literal: In the third year they took Jinling; remaining bandits burst out and fought bitterly; Xiang and Huai armies repeatedly suffered setbacks at Benniu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Jinling fell. The surviving rebels broke out and fought fiercely, and the Xiang and Huai armies suffered repeated reverses at Benniu.

sentences.zh: 銘傳軍被圍急，議者欲退保丹陽，仁美曰：「賊雖銳，猶困獸之鬥也，出奇兵勝之。

translations.literal: Mingchuan's army was besieged in urgent straits; those in council wished to withdraw and hold Danyang; Renmei said: "Though the bandits are sharp, they are still a cornered beast's fight—use unexpected troops to defeat them."
translations.idiomatic: Mingchuan's army was hard pressed under siege, and some argued for falling back to Danyang. Renmei said, "The rebels may be fierce, but they are fighting like cornered beasts. Send an unexpected force and we can defeat them."

sentences.zh: 」次日，與諸軍略其東南，賊眾轟擊以拒，仁美膝行至砲旁，連擲火彈，賊駭走，官軍鼓譟而登，夷東路各壘。

translations.literal: The next day, together with the various armies he raided their southeast; the bandit host opened thunderous fire to resist; Renmei crawled on his knees to the side of the guns, threw fire-bombs in succession; the bandits fled in alarm; the government army drummed and clamored as they mounted; they leveled each fort on the eastern road.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he joined the other units in a sweep of the southeast. The rebels opened a thunderous barrage to hold them off. Renmei crawled on his knees to the guns and hurled fire-bombs one after another. The rebels broke in alarm, and the government troops, drums roaring, stormed the heights and leveled every fort on the eastern road.

sentences.zh: 賊自隔河來犯，仁美夜乘輕舸，率健卒數人躍輪艦殺賊十餘，以火攻之，船盡裂，奔牛賊平。

translations.literal: Bandits came to attack from across the river; Renmei at night boarded a light skiff; leading several stalwart soldiers he leaped onto a paddle-wheel ship and killed more than ten bandits; he attacked with fire; the boats all split apart; the Benniu bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels attacked from across the river. Renmei took a light boat by night, led a handful of picked men aboard a paddle-wheel ship, and killed more than ten of the enemy. He set the vessels alight; the boats were ripped apart, and the rebels at Benniu were finally suppressed.

sentences.zh: 軍無錫，執遊兵擾民者斬以徇。

translations.literal: The army camped at Wuxi; he seized roaming soldiers who harassed the people and beheaded them as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The army was stationed at Wuxi. He arrested stragglers who had been harassing civilians and executed them as a warning to the ranks.

sentences.zh: 至是詔以總兵記名。

translations.literal: At this time an edict appointed him to brigade-general on the registry.
translations.idiomatic: He was then granted registry appointment as brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 四年，偽侍王李世賢陷漳浦，鴻章遣仁美與郭松林俱航海赴援。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the false Prince of Shi Li Shixian took Zhangpu; Hongzhang sent Renmei together with Guo Songlin by sea to go to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Taiping Prince of Shi, Li Shixian, captured Zhangpu. Hongzhang sent Renmei and Guo Songlin by sea to relieve the town.

sentences.zh: 既至，甫築壘，賊大至。

translations.literal: When they arrived, they had just begun building ramparts; the bandits came in force.
translations.idiomatic: They had barely begun building fortifications when the rebels arrived in force.

sentences.zh: 仁美令諸軍無動，獨率所部三百人迎敵。

translations.literal: Renmei ordered the various armies not to move; alone he led his own three hundred men to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Renmei ordered the other units to hold their ground and personally led his own three hundred men forward to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊疑有伏，不敢前，仁美伺懈擊之，賊奔南靖。

translations.literal: The bandits suspected an ambush and did not dare advance; Renmei waited for their slackness and struck; the bandits fled toward Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels suspected an ambush and hesitated to advance. Renmei waited until they relaxed their guard, then struck, and they fled toward Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 乘勝薄城下，率眾先登，世賢巷戰逾時，啟西門而遁，遂復漳州，下南靖。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory he closed on the city walls; leading the masses he was first to ascend; Shixian fought in the lanes for a long time; he opened the west gate and fled; thus they recovered Zhangzhou and took Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing his advantage he closed on the walls, led the assault, and was first over the top. Shixian fought street by street for a long time, then opened the west gate and fled. Zhangzhou was recovered and Nanjing subjugated.

sentences.zh: 擢提督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 進規漳浦，賊分門堅守，仁美與副將張遵道分路迎戰，賊稍卻，麾軍競進，攻克之。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Zhangpu, the bandits split by gates and held firm; Renmei and deputy brigade-general Zhang Zundao met them in battle by separate routes; the bandits fell back slightly; he waved the army to rush forward in competition; they captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to invest Zhangpu. The rebels held every gate in force. Renmei and deputy brigade-general Zhang Zundao engaged them on separate routes; the rebels gave ground, and he ordered a general rush that carried the city.

sentences.zh: 進復云霄廳。

translations.literal: Advancing, they recovered Yunxiao subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to recover Yunxiao subprefecture.

sentences.zh: 旋歸，以兄仁賢領其眾。

translations.literal: Soon he returned; he had his elder brother Rensian lead his troops.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned home, leaving his elder brother Rensian in command of his forces.

sentences.zh: 五年，國荃巡撫湖北，檄仁美與松林募軍進至唐縣，會東捻自信陽竄入，遇於德安，薄而擊之，追至鍾祥臼口。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Guoquan became governor of Hubei; he ordered Renmei and Songlin to raise troops and advance to Tang County; they met the Eastern Nian who had slipped in from Xinyang; they encountered them at De'an; pressed close and struck; pursued to Jiukou in Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Guoquan was appointed governor of Hubei and ordered Renmei and Songlin to raise troops and advance to Tang County. The Eastern Nian rebels had slipped in from Xinyang; the two forces met at De'an, where Renmei's men closed and attacked, chasing them as far as Jiukou in Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 師分三路入，仁美攻其左，抵羅家集，遇伏，與戰，力竭死之。

translations.literal: The army divided into three routes and entered; Renmei attacked their left; reached Luojiaji; encountered ambush; fought; exhausted his strength and died.
translations.idiomatic: The army split into three columns. Renmei took the left flank, reached Luojiaji, walked into an ambush, fought until his strength was spent, and died.

sentences.zh: 賞世職，予鍾祥及原籍建祠。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with a hereditary office; granted temples at Zhongxiang and his native place.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a hereditary office, and memorial temples were built for him at Zhongxiang and in his home county.

sentences.zh: 毛克寬，湖南溆浦人。

translations.literal: Mao Kekuan, a native of Xupu in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Kekuan was a native of Xupu in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，兄弟五人同入田興恕虎威營，皆以善戰著，克寬尤驍勇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng, five brothers together entered Tian Xingwu's Huwei camp; all were noted for skill in battle; Kekuan was especially fierce and brave.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xianfeng reign, five brothers together joined Tian Xingwu's Tiger Might Battalion. All were known as fine fighters, and Kekuan was the fiercest of them.

sentences.zh: 六年，隨興恕援江西，克萍鄉、萬載，复袁州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Xingwu to relieve Jiangxi; took Pingxiang and Wanzai; recovered Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Xingwu to Jiangxi, captured Pingxiang and Wanzai, and recovered Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 後從圍臨江，吉安賊來援，城賊填壕伺夾擊。

translations.literal: Later he followed in the siege of Linjiang; Ji'an bandits came to the relief; city bandits filled the moat and watched to strike from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: He later took part in the siege of Linjiang. Rebels from Ji'an came to relieve the city, while the defenders filled in the moat and waited to fall on the besiegers from both sides.

sentences.zh: 克寬從拒援寇，大破之太平墟，燒賊屯四十七，遂克臨江。

translations.literal: Kekuan followed to repel the relief raiders; routed them greatly at Taipingxu; burned forty-seven bandit stockades; then took Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Kekuan helped beat back the relief force and won a great victory at Taipingxu, burning forty-seven rebel encampments. Linjiang then fell.

sentences.zh: 湖南巡撫駱秉章以克寬久經戰陣、勞績甚多聞於朝。

translations.literal: Hunan Governor Luo Bingzhang reported to the court that Kekuan had long been through battle lines and had very many labors and achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan Governor Luo Bingzhang memorialized the court on Kekuan's long service in the field and his many accomplishments.

sentences.zh: 時貴州苗、教各匪麕聚，复隨興恕赴援，連克錦屏等處，克寬功最。

translations.literal: At that time Miao and teaching bandits of Guizhou gathered like deer in a herd; again he followed Xingwu to go to the relief; in succession took Jingping and other places; Kekuan's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Miao rebels and sectarian bandits were then massing in Guizhou. Kekuan again followed Xingwu to the relief, helping capture Jingping and other strongholds; his contribution was the greatest of all.

sentences.zh: 偽翼王石達​​開犯湖南，窺寶慶，克寬從興恕回援，破賊寶慶城南黃塘，复敗賊七架坡。

translations.literal: The false Prince of Yi Shi Dakai invaded Hunan and eyed Shaocheng; Kekuan followed Xingwu back to the relief; defeated bandits at Huangtang south of Shaocheng city; again defeated bandits at Qijiapo.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiping Prince of Yi, Shi Dakai, invaded Hunan and threatened Shaocheng, Kekuan followed Xingwu to the relief, routed the rebels at Huangtang south of the city, and again defeated them at Qijiapo.

sentences.zh: 賊合圍攻興恕壘，克寬日夜搏戰，援軍既集，內外夾攻，賊敗遁。

translations.literal: Bandits combined in siege to attack Xingwu's ramparts; Kekuan day and night fought fiercely; relief troops having gathered, inside and outside struck from both sides; bandits were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels surrounded Xingwu's camp. Kekuan fought day and night until relief troops arrived and attacked from within and without. The rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 追及九鞏橋、白楊鋪，復大破之。

translations.literal: Pursued to Jiugong Bridge and Baiyangpu; again routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued them to Jiugong Bridge and Baiyangpu and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 賊走廣西，遂以參將留湖南。

translations.literal: Bandits fled to Guangxi; he was then appointed colonel and retained in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled into Guangxi, and Kekuan was appointed colonel and retained for service in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 黔亂复熾，朝命興恕為貴州提督，督辦軍務。

translations.literal: The Qian disorders again flared; the court appointed Xingwu grand coordinator of Guizhou, to supervise military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Disorders in Guizhou flared anew, and the court appointed Xingwu grand coordinator of Guizhou with overall command of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 克寬再入黔，逆酋安太然及偽元帥韓成龍、偽招討覃國英等圍攻印江、石阡，克寬率虎後營分道進擊平陽等處賊屯百餘，斬韓成龍、覃國英，拔出難民三千餘人，遂解城圍，乘勝复甕安。

translations.literal: Kekuan again entered Qian; rebel chieftain An Tairan and the false marshals Han Chenglong and the false pacification commissioner Tan Guoying and others besieged Yinjiang and Shiqian; Kekuan led the Tiger Rear Battalion by separate routes to attack more than a hundred bandit stockades at places such as Pingyang; beheaded Han Chenglong and Tan Guoying; pulled out more than three thousand refugees; then relieved the city siege; pressing victory recovered Weng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Kekuan returned to Guizhou. Rebel chieftain An Tairan, the false marshals Han Chenglong and Tan Guoying, and others were besieging Yinjiang and Shiqian. Kekuan led the Tiger Rear Battalion along separate routes, stormed more than a hundred rebel camps around Pingyang and elsewhere, killed Han Chenglong and Tan Guoying, and brought more than three thousand civilians to safety. The siege was lifted, and pressing the advantage his men recovered Weng'an.

sentences.zh: 兩旬之間，蕩平數百里。

translations.literal: Within two ten-day periods they swept pacified several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Within twenty days they had cleared several hundred li of territory.

sentences.zh: 興恕疏薦克寬「膽識俱優，屢獲奇捷，隨徵六載，戰必身先，實屬英勇冠群」。

translations.literal: Xingwu memorialized recommending Kekuan: "Courage and capacity both excellent, repeatedly gaining marvelous victories, following campaigns six years, in battle always body first—truly bravery crowns the host."
translations.idiomatic: Xingwu memorialized the throne, praising Kekuan as "bold and capable in equal measure, repeatedly winning striking victories. In six years of campaigning he has always led from the front—a courage unmatched among his peers."

sentences.zh: 命以副將留黔，賞號銳勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He was ordered appointed deputy brigade-general retained in Qian; granted the title Ruiyong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed deputy brigade-general and retained in Guizhou, with the honorific title Ruiyong Baturu.

sentences.zh: 石達開從廣西犯黔，陷歸化、定番等城。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai from Guangxi invaded Qian; took Guihua, Dingfan, and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai invaded Guizhou from Guangxi and captured Guihua, Dingfan, and other towns.

sentences.zh: 克寬迎剿，破籠溪、猴坪賊巢，進駐赤土，督軍攻定番、長寨，克之，复解安順、安平城圍。

translations.literal: Kekuan went to meet and suppress; broke the bandit nests at Longxi and Houping; advanced and encamped at Chitu; directed the army to attack Dingfan and Changzhai; took them; again relieved the city sieges of Anshun and Anping.
translations.idiomatic: Kekuan marched out to meet him, destroyed the rebel strongholds at Longxi and Houping, and advanced to encamp at Chitu. He directed the attack on Dingfan and Changzhai, took both, and lifted the sieges of Anshun and Anping.

sentences.zh: 十一年，補大定協副將，移駐大水橋，通運道。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed deputy brigade-general of the Dading command; moved to garrison at Dashui Bridge; opened the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed deputy brigade-general of the Dading command, moved his garrison to Dashui Bridge, and secured the supply route.

sentences.zh: 賊乘營壘未成，遣悍黨分股來犯，克寬分隊逆戰，敗其左右翼，中路賊死抗不退，克寬策馬轢陣，往來盪決，刃悍賊數十，賊眾披靡。

translations.literal: Bandits, taking advantage of unfinished camp ramparts, sent fierce partisans in divided columns to attack; Kekuan split squads to meet battle; defeated their left and right wings; center-route bandits fought to the death and would not retreat; Kekuan drove his horse to crush the ranks, going back and forth sweeping and breaking through; bladed fierce bandits by the tens; the bandit host scattered in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels struck while his camp was still unfinished, sending fierce fighters in several columns. Kekuan divided his force to meet them, broke their left and right wings, then charged the center, where the enemy fought to the death. He spurred his horse back and forth through the melee, cut down dozens of their best fighters, and the rebel ranks collapsed.

sentences.zh: 會飛砲中馬，徒步奮擊，身受數創，歿於陣，年三十三。

translations.literal: Then a flying cannon-ball struck his horse; on foot he fought fiercely; his body received several wounds; died in the ranks; age thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: A stray cannon shot brought down his horse. He fought on foot, took several wounds, and died in battle at the age of thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 詔贈總兵銜，建專祠，賞世職。

translations.literal: Edict posthumously granted brigade-general rank; built a dedicated shrine; rewarded with hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of brigade-general, given a dedicated shrine, and awarded a hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 弟克佳，官把總，戰歿臨江。

translations.literal: Younger brother Kejia, officer rank platoon leader, died in battle at Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Kejia, a platoon officer, was killed fighting at Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 先死黔苗之亂者，有邢連科，原名正堉，貴州貴陽人。

translations.literal: Among those who died earlier in the Qian-Miao disorders was Xing Lianke, original name Zhengyu, a native of Guiyang in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who had fallen earlier in the Guizhou Miao uprisings was Xing Lianke, originally named Zhengyu, a native of Guiyang in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 台拱廳黃施衛千總。

translations.literal: Platoon leader of the Huangshi garrison in Taigong subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was a platoon leader of the Huangshi garrison in Taigong subprefecture.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，苗叛，攻城，連科迭乞援，累月兵始至。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng the Miao rebelled; attacked the city; Lianke repeatedly begged for relief; months passed before troops arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng the Miao rose in rebellion and attacked the city. Lianke sent repeated pleas for relief, but troops did not arrive for months.

sentences.zh: 連科蒐殘卒夾擊出陷陣，而援兵先潰，連科轉戰十家寨，陣亡。

translations.literal: Lianke gathered remnant soldiers and struck out from both sides into the trap ranks; but relief troops first broke; Lianke turned and fought at Shijiazhai; died in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Lianke rallied the remaining troops and led a sortie from within, but the relief force broke first. He fought his way to Shijiazhai and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 子士義。

translations.literal: His son was Shiyi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shiyi.

sentences.zh: 舉人，主講平越，先聞警，馳赴城守。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate; lectured at Pingyue; hearing the alarm first, galloped to the city to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi was a provincial graduate who lectured at Pingyue. At the first alarm he raced to the city to join its defense.

sentences.zh: 至是召家人環坐，縱火藥自焚，僕諶年有、婢玉蘭從死。

translations.literal: At this he summoned the family to sit in a circle; set off gunpowder and burned himself; servants Zhen Nianyou and maid Yulan followed in death.
translations.idiomatic: He then gathered his family in a circle, set off his store of gunpowder, and burned himself to death. His servant Zhen Nianyou and his maid Yulan died with him.

sentences.zh: 千總署堂皇之下，列屍二十有二。

translations.literal: Beneath the main hall of the platoon-leader's office, twenty-two corpses were lined up.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two bodies lay in a row beneath the main hall of the garrison office.

sentences.zh: 巡撫蔣霨遠、田興恕先後以闔門殉難聞，賜祀，予世職。

translations.literal: Governors Jiang Aiyuan and Tian Xingwu successively reported the whole household's martyrdom; granted enshrinement; given hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: Governors Jiang Aiyuan and Tian Xingwu memorialized the throne on the family's martyrdom. They were granted enshrinement and a hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 孫以謙，曾孫端，翰林院編修。

translations.literal: Grandson Yiqian; great-grandson Duan, compiler in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson was Yiqian; his great-grandson Duan served as a compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 田興奇，湖南鳳凰廳人。

translations.literal: Tian Xingqi, a native of Fenghuang subprefecture in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xingqi was a native of Fenghuang subprefecture in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 隸田興恕虎威營。

translations.literal: He belonged to Tian Xingwu's Huwei camp.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Tian Xingwu's Tiger Might Battalion.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，從平郴、桂、茶陵，以功敘外委。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he followed in pacifying Chen, Gui, and Chaling; for merit received appointment as external commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he helped pacify Chen, Gui, and Chaling, and for his service was appointed an external commissioner.

sentences.zh: 興恕援江西，進攻袁州，興恕躍馬突賊陣，興奇隨入，各軍繼之，遂獲大勝，賊潰奔數十里。

translations.literal: Xingwu relieved Jiangxi and advanced to attack Yuanzhou; Xingwu leaped his horse and burst into the bandit ranks; Xingqi followed in; each army followed; thus obtained a great victory; bandits broke and fled several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingwu went to relieve Jiangxi and attacked Yuanzhou, he charged the rebel line on horseback and Xingqi rode in with him. The rest of the army followed, and they won a great victory; the rebels broke and fled for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 分宜、袁州复，擢千總，加守備銜，賞藍翎。

translations.literal: Fenyi and Yuanzhou recovered; promoted to platoon leader; added battalion commander rank; granted blue plume.
translations.idiomatic: Fenyi and Yuanzhou were recovered. Xingqi was promoted to platoon leader, given battalion-commander rank, and awarded the blue plume.

sentences.zh: 七年，師次高安陰岡嶺，興奇斬偽監軍姜萬祥、總制艾得勝。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the army halted at Yingang Ridge in Gao'an; Xingqi beheaded the false military supervisor Jiang Wanxiang and the commander Ai Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, as the army camped at Yingang Ridge in Gao'an, Xingqi killed the false Taiping military supervisor Jiang Wanxiang and commander Ai Desheng.

sentences.zh: 攻复臨江，擢游擊，換花翎。

translations.literal: Attacked and recovered Linjiang; promoted to mobile corps commander; exchanged for flowered plume.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the recovery of Linjiang, was promoted to mobile-corps commander, and received the flowered plume.

sentences.zh: 八年夏，貴州寇起，隨興恕往援，敗賊黎平，夷其營。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eighth year banditry rose in Guizhou; he followed Xingwu to go to the relief; defeated bandits at Liping; leveled their camps.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eighth year rebellion broke out in Guizhou. He followed Xingwu to the relief, defeated the rebels at Liping, and destroyed their camps.

sentences.zh: 轉攻漢砦，斬馘二十餘級，夷賊營十餘處，追北十八江，斬偽侯黃必升等二十一人，擒偽將軍伍云童。

translations.literal: Turned to attack Hanzai; severed heads twenty-plus; leveled bandit camps more than ten places; pursued north to Shibajiang; beheaded the false marquis Huang Bisheng and twenty-one others; captured the false general Wu Yuntong.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to attack Hanzai, took more than twenty heads, and destroyed a dozen rebel camps. Pursuing north to Shibajiang, he killed the false marquis Huang Bisheng and twenty others and captured the false general Wu Yuntong.

sentences.zh: 黎平復，以參將留湖南補用，加副將銜。

translations.literal: Liping recovered; appointed colonel retained for assignment in Hunan; added deputy brigade-general rank.
translations.idiomatic: Liping was recovered. Xingqi was appointed colonel and retained for service in Hunan, with the rank of deputy brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 九年春，石達開率眾十餘萬犯寶慶，興恕軍適自黔還，道其境，駐軍九鞏橋。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year Shi Dakai led a host of more than one hundred thousand to invade Shaocheng; Xingwu's army happened to return from Qian; passed through its territory; encamped at Jiugong Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year Shi Dakai invaded Shaocheng with an army of more than one hundred thousand. Xingwu's force was just returning from Guizhou and happened to pass through the region, encamping at Jiugong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 賊乘其甫安營，悉眾來犯，隨興恕擊卻之。

translations.literal: Bandits, taking advantage of their just settling camp, brought their whole force to attack; he followed Xingwu and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels struck while the troops were still settling camp, but Xingqi joined Xingwu and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 是夜三鼓，興奇率壯士八百人襲賊營，賊驚潰，死亡相屬，餘眾奔逃。

translations.literal: That night at the third watch Xingqi led eight hundred stalwarts in a raid on the bandit camp; bandits broke in alarm; deaths followed one after another; remaining masses fled.
translations.idiomatic: That night, at the third watch, Xingqi led eight hundred picked men in a night assault on the rebel camp. The enemy broke in panic, dying in heaps as the rest fled.

sentences.zh: 寶慶平，擢副將。

translations.literal: Shaocheng pacified; promoted to deputy brigade-general.
translations.idiomatic: Shaocheng was pacified, and Xingqi was promoted to deputy brigade-general.

sentences.zh: 十年，從興恕剿貴州苗匪，興奇領虎勇二千人至石阡，戰龍潭，斬賊偽元帥韓成龍、覃國英，盡平其營。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he followed Xingwu to suppress Guizhou Miao bandits; Xingqi led two thousand Tiger Braves to Shiqian; fought at Longtan; beheaded the bandits' false marshals Han Chenglong and Tan Guoying; completely pacified their camps.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he followed Xingwu against the Miao rebels of Guizhou. Xingqi led two thousand Tiger Braves to Shiqian, fought at Longtan, killed the false marshals Han Chenglong and Tan Guoying, and destroyed their camps entirely.

sentences.zh: 越二日再攻，賊走馬坪，斬馘甚眾，並拔出被擄老穉男女三千餘口。

translations.literal: After two days they attacked again; bandits fled to Maping; severed heads were very many; also pulled out more than three thousand old and young men and women who had been captured.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later they attacked again. The rebels fled to Maping; many were killed, and more than three thousand elderly and young men and women who had been taken captive were brought to safety.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，賜衝勇巴圖魯名號，加總兵銜，仍駐石阡。

translations.literal: On news of victory he was granted the title Chongyong Baturu; added brigade-general rank; still garrisoned at Shiqian.
translations.idiomatic: When word of the victory reached the court, he was granted the honorific title Chongyong Baturu, given brigade-general rank, and remained garrisoned at Shiqian.

sentences.zh: 六月，擊賊雙溪，中伏，死之，時年三十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he attacked bandits at Shuangxi; walked into ambush; died; at the time age thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he attacked rebels at Shuangxi, walked into an ambush, and was killed at the age of thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 詔贈提督銜，諡剛介。

translations.literal: Edict posthumously granted grand coordinator rank; posthumous title Gangjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of grand coordinator and given the posthumous title Gangjie.

sentences.zh: 田興勝亦隸興恕部下，平郴、桂，援寶慶及援江西，同有功，累擢至守備。

translations.literal: Tian Xingsheng also belonged under Xingwu; pacified Chen and Gui; relieved Shaocheng and relieved Jiangxi; together had merit; repeatedly promoted until battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xingsheng also served under Xingwu. He helped pacify Chen and Gui, relieved Shaocheng and Jiangxi, and shared in the credit, rising through repeated promotions to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 又隨剿貴州各匪，破籠溪，解餘慶圍。

translations.literal: Again he followed in suppressing the various bandits of Guizhou; broke Longxi; relieved the siege of Yuqing.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined campaigns against the rebels of Guizhou, broke through at Longxi, and lifted the siege of Yuqing.

sentences.zh: 偕都司沈宏富等進屯雄黃、小崽等處。

translations.literal: Together with battalion commander Shen Hongfu and others he advanced and encamped at Xionghuang, Xiaozai, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Together with battalion commander Shen Hongfu and others, he advanced and encamped at Xionghuang, Xiaozai, and other points.

sentences.zh: 賊於老巢立堅壘十八，悍黨萬餘，分佈左右山梁，興勝約游擊楊岩寶兩路夾攻，自與沈宏富攻左路各寨；

translations.literal: Bandits at the old nest built eighteen strong forts; fierce partisans more than ten thousand; distributed on the left and right mountain ridges; Xingsheng arranged with mobile corps commander Yang Yanbao for a two-route pincer attack; himself with Shen Hongfu attacked the left-route stockades;
translations.idiomatic: At their stronghold the rebels had built eighteen fortified camps, manned by more than ten thousand fierce fighters spread along the ridges on both flanks. Xingsheng arranged with mobile-corps commander Yang Yanbao for a two-pronged assault, while he and Shen Hongfu took the left-route stockades;

sentences.zh: 都司田興考由右路繞山後出擊，並設伏後路。

translations.literal: Battalion commander Tian Xingkao from the right route circled behind the mountain to strike out; also set ambush on the rear route.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion commander Tian Xingkao was to circle behind the mountain on the right and strike from the rear, with ambushes set along the escape routes.

sentences.zh: 計定，率兵直衝首山梁，賊數千迎擊，興勝督隊沖突，鏖戰逾時，賊沿山潰遁，營內賊開卡狂竄，興勝親入賊陣，手刃悍目二。

translations.literal: The plan set, he led troops straight at the foremost mountain ridge; several thousand bandits met and attacked; Xingsheng supervised the squads in charge; fought bitterly for a long time; bandits along the mountain broke and fled; bandits inside the camp opened the gates and ran wildly; Xingsheng personally entered the bandit ranks; hand-bladed two fierce chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Once the plan was set, he led his men straight at the foremost ridge. Several thousand rebels met them head on. Xingsheng drove his squads forward in repeated charges; the fight dragged on until the enemy broke along the slope. Rebels inside the camp flung open the gates and fled in disorder. Xingsheng plunged into their ranks himself and cut down two of their chieftains.

sentences.zh: 宏富督後隊合圍，先毀其右寨，移攻左寨，破之。

translations.literal: Hongfu directed the rear ranks in combined encirclement; first destroyed their right stockade; shifted to attack the left stockade; broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfu brought up the rear columns to complete the encirclement, first destroying the right stockade, then shifting to the left and taking that as well.

sentences.zh: 乘勝追襲，有黃衣賊目率黨死拒，興勝射之，蹶，擒而梟示，餘賊大潰。

translations.literal: Pressing victory in pursuit, a yellow-robed bandit chieftain led his partisans in death resistance; Xingsheng shot him; he stumbled; captured and displayed severed head; remaining bandits broke greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the pursuit, a rebel chieftain in yellow robes led his men in a desperate stand. Xingsheng shot him down, had him captured and beheaded for display, and the rest of the rebels broke completely.

sentences.zh: 追十餘裡，墜崖死者無數。

translations.literal: Pursued more than ten li; those who fell from cliffs and died were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran more than ten li; countless rebels died falling from the cliffs.

sentences.zh: 是役共破堅寨十餘座，陣斬偽元帥韓進、楊正閏等二十餘人，馘千五百餘級，乘勝平賊營十餘座。

translations.literal: In this battle together broke more than ten strong stockades; in the ranks beheaded the false marshals Han Jin, Yang Zhengyun, and more than twenty others; severed heads more than fifteen hundred; pressing victory pacified more than ten bandit camps.
translations.idiomatic: In this engagement they stormed more than ten fortified camps, killed the false marshals Han Jin, Yang Zhengyun, and more than twenty others in battle, took more than fifteen hundred heads, and went on to level another dozen rebel camps.

sentences.zh: 复隨總兵劉吉三等夜攻三角莊，賊猝不及防，驚而潰，毀其連營三座。

translations.literal: Again he followed brigade-general Liu Jisan and others in a night attack on Sanjiaozhuang; bandits were caught unprepared; broke in alarm; destroyed their three linked camps.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined brigade-general Liu Jisan and others in a night attack on Sanjiaozhuang. Caught off guard, the rebels broke in alarm, and three linked camps were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 適松坪賊首石復明糾玉華山匪黨數万，分六股來撲，興勝偕游擊劉祖得合兵迎剿，都司徐祥太與興考各率所部設伏山麓及民舍中，賊遇伏大敗，死亡枕藉。

translations.literal: Just then Songping bandit chieftain Shi Fuming gathered Yuhuashan bandit partisans in tens of thousands; split into six columns to rush in; Xingsheng together with mobile corps commander Liu Zude combined troops to meet and suppress; battalion commanders Xu Xiangtai and Xingkao each led their own units to set ambush at the mountain foot and in civilian houses; bandits met ambush and were greatly defeated; dead bodies piled one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Songping chieftain Shi Fuming rallied tens of thousands of bandits from Yuhuashan and sent six columns against them. Xingsheng joined mobile-corps commander Liu Zude to meet the attack, while battalion commanders Xu Xiangtai and Xingkao laid ambushes at the foot of the mountain and in nearby houses. The rebels walked into the trap and were routed; the dead lay piled upon one another.

sentences.zh: 追至木影頂，地險峻，賊寨負隅難拔，因收隊。

translations.literal: Pursued to Muying Peak; the ground was steep and dangerous; the bandit stockade held a corner and was hard to take; therefore they withdrew the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit carried them to Muying Peak, where the ground was steep and the rebel stockade held a desperate position too strong to storm. They broke off and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明日，同知唐繩武等由間道出松坪之後，先取老巢，興勝奉令偕岩寶等攻木影頂，攀藤而上，賊礌石交下，軍少卻。

translations.literal: The next day, subprefect Tang Shengwu and others by a hidden route emerged behind Songping; first took the old nest; Xingsheng received orders together with Yanbao and others to attack Muying Peak; climbed by vines upward; bandits rolled stones down in succession; the army fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: The next day subprefect Tang Shengwu and others took a hidden route behind Songping and seized the old nest first. Xingsheng, under orders, joined Yanbao and others in the assault on Muying Peak. They climbed by vines, but the rebels rolled stones down upon them and the troops fell back briefly.

sentences.zh: 興勝橫刀躍馬，奮身進，飛登寨牆。

translations.literal: Xingsheng held his blade crosswise and leaped his horse; threw his body forward; flew up and mounted the stockade wall.
translations.idiomatic: Xingsheng spurred his horse forward with blade drawn, threw himself into the assault, and leaped onto the stockade wall.

sentences.zh: 賊矛攢刺，捉其矛而上，揮刀連斬悍賊十餘，諸軍繼進，賊散走。

translations.literal: Bandit spears gathered and stabbed; he seized a spear and climbed up; swung his blade and in succession beheaded more than ten fierce bandits; the various armies followed in advance; bandits scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Spears thrust at him from every side; he seized one and climbed up, then cut down more than ten of their best fighters in succession. The rest of the army surged after him, and the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 官軍四面兜剿，殲除殆盡，擒其渠秦官寶、劉老栘等，誅之。

translations.literal: The government army from four sides rounded up and suppressed; annihilated nearly all; captured their ringleaders Qin Guanbao, Liu Laoyi, and others; executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops closed in from all sides and wiped out nearly the entire force. They captured the ringleaders Qin Guanbao, Liu Laoyi, and others and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 松坪黃號賊眾五萬，連營三十餘，興勝等即時裹糧疾進，悉銳攻之，賊傾巢出拒，官軍奮擊敗之。

translations.literal: Songping Yellow Banner bandits numbered fifty thousand; linked camps more than thirty; Xingsheng and others at once wrapped rations and advanced swiftly; brought all elite forces to attack; bandits emptied the nest to come out and resist; the government army fought fiercely and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Songping the Yellow Banner rebels numbered fifty thousand in more than thirty linked camps. Xingsheng and the others marched at once with rations on their backs and threw their best troops into the attack. The rebels came out in full force to meet them, but the government army fought fiercely and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 有偽扶明王者，悍酋也，手斫敗退賊，挺身來抗。

translations.literal: There was a false King Who Supports Ming—a fierce chieftain—who with his hand cut down retreating bandits and straightened his body to come and resist.
translations.idiomatic: A false King Who Supports Ming, a fierce chieftain, cut down his own men as they fell back and stepped forward to fight.

sentences.zh: 興勝自與搏戰，殪之。

translations.literal: Xingsheng himself joined in combat and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xingsheng fought him hand to hand and killed him.

sentences.zh: 餘賊猶相持，宏富等已從後破其巢，賊乃潰竄。

translations.literal: Remaining bandits still held on; Hongfu and others had already from the rear broken their nest; the bandits then broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining rebels still held their ground, but Hongfu and the others had already broken through from the rear. The enemy then broke and fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 官軍夾擊，斬馘四千餘級，松坪賊壘皆平。

translations.literal: The government army struck from both sides; severed heads more than four thousand; all Songping bandit forts were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops attacked from both sides, took more than four thousand heads, and every rebel fort at Songping was leveled.

sentences.zh: 乘勝攻猴嶺，拔之。

translations.literal: Pressing victory they attacked Houling and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing their advantage, they attacked Houling and took it.

sentences.zh: 旋偕宏富移剿甕安，先破小山寺營、馬安營賊壘百餘，冒雨分三路進攻紅岡堡，興勝策馬陷陣，連刃數賊，諸軍繼之，立破其巢，躡追數里。

translations.literal: Soon together with Hongfu he shifted to suppress Weng'an; first broke more than a hundred bandit forts at Xiaoshansi camp and Ma'an camp; in rain split into three routes to attack Honggang Fort; Xingsheng drove his horse into the ranks; in succession bladed several bandits; the various armies followed; immediately broke their nest; pursued closely for several li.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Hongfu in operations against Weng'an, first storming more than a hundred rebel camps at Xiaoshansi and Ma'an. In the rain they split into three columns and attacked Honggang Fort. Xingsheng charged into the enemy line, cut down several rebels, and the rest of the army followed, breaking the stronghold at once and pursuing for several li.

sentences.zh: 會甕安賊來援，敗賊亦返鬥，興勝偕宏富等縱擊。

translations.literal: Just then Weng'an bandits came to the relief; defeated bandits also turned back to fight; Xingsheng together with Hongfu and others let loose in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel reinforcements from Weng'an arrived, and the defeated force turned to fight again. Xingsheng joined Hongfu and the others in a full pursuit.

sentences.zh: 射斃賊酋數名，賊亂返奔，官軍急躡之，賊不敢入城，奔至玉華山老巢。

translations.literal: Shot dead several bandit chieftains; bandits in disorder turned and fled; the government army urgently pursued; bandits did not dare enter the city; fled to the old nest at Yuhuashan.
translations.idiomatic: They shot down several rebel chieftains. The enemy broke in disorder, and the government troops pressed hard upon them. The rebels dared not re-enter the city and fled to their old stronghold on Yuhuashan.

sentences.zh: 甕安遂復，自是入省之路始通。

translations.literal: Weng'an was thus recovered; from this the route into the province was first opened.
