translations.idiomatic: Weng'an was recovered, and for the first time the road into the provincial capital was secure.

sentences.zh: 興恕疏稱「興勝每戰單槍陷陣，不計生死，實屬忠勇可嘉」。

translations.literal: Xingwu memorialized stating: "Xingsheng in every battle alone with spear plunged into the ranks, heedless of life and death—truly loyal and brave and worthy of praise."
translations.idiomatic: Xingwu memorialized the throne, writing that "in every battle Xingsheng charges alone into the enemy ranks, heedless of life and death—a loyalty and courage truly worthy of praise."

sentences.zh: 詔以游擊拔補，給果勇巴圖魯勇號。

translations.literal: Edict appointed him by selection to mobile corps commander; granted the brave title Guoyong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed mobile-corps commander by imperial selection and granted the honorific martial title Guoyong Baturu.

sentences.zh: 十一年，粵匪大股竄貴州境，踞定番州、長寨等處，偪近省垣，岩寶等攻之未下。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year a large force of Cantonese bandits fled into Guizhou, occupied Dingfan Prefecture, Changzhai, and other places, pressed close to the provincial capital, and Yan Bao and others attacked without taking them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year a large Cantonese rebel force slipped into Guizhou, seized Dingfan, Changzhai, and neighboring districts, and threatened the provincial capital. Yan Bao and others attacked but could not dislodge them.

sentences.zh: 興勝隨興恕往剿，屢戰皆捷，克定番，又偕副將周學桂進兵拔長寨，其別股踞土地關者，分黨撲安平以牽掣官軍，興勝馳救，立解城圍。

translations.literal: Xingsheng followed Xingwu to suppress them, won repeated victories, took Dingfan, and together with Deputy Brigadier Zhou Xuegui advanced to capture Changzhai; another band holding Tudiguan divided forces to strike Anping to tie down government troops; Xingsheng galloped to the rescue and immediately lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Xingsheng marched with Xingwu to suppress them, won battle after battle, and recovered Dingfan. With Deputy Brigadier Zhou Xuegui he then took Changzhai. When a separate rebel band at Tudiguan sent a detachment against Anping to pin down government forces, Xingsheng rode to the rescue and raised the siege at once.

sentences.zh: 匪首張遇恩勾結仲匪圍安順，並撲定南汛城，又隨總兵趙德昌擊退之，省會解嚴。

translations.literal: Bandit chieftain Zhang Yu'en colluded with Zhong bandits to besiege Anshun and also struck Dingnan garrison city; he again followed Brigade-General Zhao Dechang in driving them off, and the provincial capital lifted its alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leader Zhang Yu'en joined forces with the Zhong tribesmen to besiege Anshun and struck the garrison at Dingnan as well. Xingsheng again followed Brigade-General Zhao Dechang in beating them back, and the alarm at the provincial capital was lifted.

sentences.zh: 三月，偕岩寶等進攻土地關，與賊戰於赤土，賊敗走，賊首仰天燕斷後。

translations.literal: In the third month he advanced together with Yan Bao and others to attack Tudiguan, fought bandits at Chitu, the bandits were defeated and fled, and bandit chieftain Yangtianyan covered the retreat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he joined Yan Bao and others in an assault on Tudiguan. At Chitu they routed the rebels, and the rebel chief Yangtianyan covered the retreat.

sentences.zh: 興勝追之，將及，以乘騎飢疲，馳驟過猛，一蹶而斃。

translations.literal: Xingsheng pursued; just as he was about to overtake them, his mount, hungry and weary, was driven too hard in the gallop, stumbled once, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xingsheng gave chase and was almost upon them when his exhausted horse, driven too hard, stumbled once and collapsed dead beneath him.

sentences.zh: 賊回隊圍之，徒步格鬥，殺悍賊十餘人，身受多創，血流如注，猶抵死相持，力竭，歿於陣。

translations.literal: The bandits turned back and surrounded him; on foot he fought hand to hand, killed more than ten fierce bandits, received many wounds, blood poured in streams, yet still resisted to the death; his strength exhausted, he fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels wheeled about and surrounded him. Fighting on foot he killed more than a dozen of their toughest fighters. Wounds covered his body and blood poured from him, yet he held on until his strength gave out and he died on the field.

sentences.zh: 照總兵例優恤，諡武烈。

translations.literal: In accordance with the precedent for brigade-generals he was granted exceptional condolence honors and given the posthumous title Wulie.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him exceptional honors on the brigade-general scale and bestowed the posthumous title Wulie.

sentences.zh: 馬定國，四川萬縣人。

translations.literal: Ma Dingguo was a native of Wan County in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Dingguo came from Wan County in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，投鮑超霆營，從攻九江小池口，回援黃梅，疊破賊孔壟、大河鋪、億生寺、黃蠟山等處，定國功多，委帶霆字左營親兵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he entered Bao Chao's Ting Battalion, followed in attacking Xiaochikou at Jiujiang, returned to relieve Huangmei, and in succession broke bandits at Konglong, Dahepu, Yisheng Temple, Huanglashan, and other places; Dingguo's achievements were many, and he was entrusted to lead the Ting-character Left Battalion personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he joined Bao Chao's Ting Battalion, fought at Xiaochikou near Jiujiang, marched back to relieve Huangmei, and in a string of victories broke rebel positions at Konglong, Dahepu, Yisheng Temple, Huanglashan, and elsewhere. Dingguo's record was outstanding, and he was appointed to lead the personal guard of Bao's left battalion.

sentences.zh: 复隨剿太湖之楓香驛，破賊壘十餘座。

translations.literal: Again he followed in suppressing Fengxiang Post at Taihu and broke more than ten bandit fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: He then took part in the campaign at Fengxiang Post near Taihu and destroyed more than ten rebel stockades.

sentences.zh: 八年，上援麻城，遇賊黃土岡，拔主將出圍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he went up to relieve Macheng, encountered bandits at Huangtugang, and pulled the commanding general out of encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he marched to relieve Macheng, met rebels at Huangtugang, and fought his way out with his commander.

sentences.zh: 從克麻城、太湖，毀雷公埠、石牌逆壘，進攻安徽省城。

translations.literal: He followed in taking Macheng and Taihu, destroyed rebel fortifications at Leigongbu and Shipai, and advanced to attack the provincial capital of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He helped capture Macheng and Taihu, destroyed rebel works at Leigongbu and Shipai, and advanced on the Anhui provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 賊於北門外及東西山灣，連柵週亙，堅不能拔。

translations.literal: The bandits outside the north gate and at the eastern and western Shanjian Bays set up linked stockades all around; they could not be taken by force.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the north gate and at Shanjian Bay east and west the rebels had thrown up a ring of linked stockades that could not be carried by assault.

sentences.zh: 定國負楯直入重柵，破其數壘。

translations.literal: Dingguo carried a shield and charged straight into the heavy stockades, breaking several of their forts.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo took up a shield and charged straight into the inner works, smashing several of their forts.

sentences.zh: 會巡撫李續賓軍覆三河，賊由舒城、潛山上竄，遂從超退扼宿松之二郎河，賊來犯，擊破之。

translations.literal: When Governor Li Xubin's army was destroyed at Sanhe, bandits fled upward from Shucheng and Qianshan; thereupon he followed Chao in withdrawing to hold Erlang River in Susong; when bandits came to attack they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Li Xubin's army was wiped out at Sanhe, rebels surged down from Shucheng and Qianshan. Dingguo withdrew with Bao Chao to hold Erlang River in Susong, met the rebel attack, and drove it back.

sentences.zh: 复破賊於花涼亭，進圍太湖。

translations.literal: Again he defeated bandits at Hualiang Pavilion and advanced to besiege Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the rebels again at Hualiang Pavilion and pressed the siege of Taihu.

sentences.zh: 悍酋陳玉成以大股來援，超移壁小池驛，賊眾圍之。

translations.literal: Fierce chieftain Chen Yucheng came with a large force in relief; Chao moved his camp to Xiaochi Post, and the bandit masses surrounded him.
translations.idiomatic: The formidable rebel commander Chen Yucheng marched up with a large relief force. Bao Chao shifted his camp to Xiaochi Post, and the rebels surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，大戰，破賊壘數十座，斃賊萬餘，乘勝克太湖、潛山。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, in a great battle he broke several tens of bandit fortifications, killed more than ten thousand bandits, and taking advantage of victory took Taihu and Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year a great battle shattered dozens of rebel works and killed more than ten thousand men. Pressing the victory, the army recovered Taihu and Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 累擢至游擊，晉參將。

translations.literal: Through accumulated promotions he rose to brigade commander and was advanced to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Steady promotion carried him to brigade commander and then to colonel.

sentences.zh: 從規皖南，收黟縣，大破賊盧村、羊棧嶺，命以副將用，乞假回籍。

translations.literal: He followed in planning the southern Anhui campaign, recovered Yi County, inflicted a great defeat on bandits at Lucun and Yangzhanling, was ordered to use as deputy brigade-general, and requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the southern Anhui campaign, recovered Yi County, and won a crushing victory at Lucun and Yangzhanling. The court ordered him appointed deputy brigade-general, after which he asked leave to return to his native place.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，滇匪擾四川萬縣之紅谷田，定國率鄉兵禦賊，戰歿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Yunnan bandits harassed Honggutian in Wan County, Sichuan; Dingguo led local militia to resist bandits and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi, Yunnan rebels raided Honggutian in Wan County. Dingguo led the local militia against them and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 詔贈總兵銜，建專祠，賞世職。

translations.literal: By imperial decree he was posthumously granted the rank of brigade-general, a dedicated shrine was built, and an hereditary office was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously granted him the rank of brigade-general, ordered a dedicated shrine built in his honor, and awarded an hereditary office.
